fe: My younger sibling asked me what I'm eating.
xk: 다른 사람이 한 질문을 전해요. 동사·형용사 어간에 -냐고를 붙이고, 보통 물었어요를 써요. 의문사는 그대로 둬요.
xe: Report a question someone asked. Add -냐고 to the verb or adjective stem, usually with 물었어요. Keep the question word.
nk: 질문을 -다고로 전하면 대답처럼 들려요. ㄹ 동사는 ㄹ이 빠져요(살다 → 사냐고). '묻다'는 ㄷ 불규칙이라 '물었어요'가 돼요.
ne: Using -다고 makes it sound like an answer, not a question. ㄹ verbs drop ㄹ (살다 → 사냐고). 묻다 becomes 물었어요.
ex: 엄마가 저한테 몇 시에 오냐고 물었어요.
Mom asked me what time I'm coming.
Hajun asked me where I live.
The teacher asked whether the test is hard.
지민이 저한테 이 옷이 비싸냐고 물었어요.
Jimin asked me if this outfit is expensive.
Sara asked me if I'm busy at the weekend.
The team leader asked me if I have a lot of work.
cz: Dohyun asked me what I'm doing now.
Yuna asked me if the weather is cold.

fe: Jiwoo asked me if I am a student.
xk: 명사로 된 질문을 전해요. 받침이 있으면 이냐고, 없으면 냐고를 붙여요.
xe: Report a question that ends with a noun. Use 이냐고 after a final consonant and 냐고 after a vowel.
nk: '누구예요?' 같은 질문은 '누구냐고'로 전해요. 동사·형용사의 -냐고와 쓰임이 같아요. 의문사는 그대로 둬요.
ne: A question like 누구예요? becomes 누구냐고. It works like -냐고 on verbs and adjectives. Keep the question word.
ex: 선생님이 이 단어가 무슨 뜻이냐고 물으셨어요.
The teacher asked what this word means.
사라가 저한테 이 가방이 누구 거냐고 물었어요.
Sara asked me whose bag this is.
가게 손님이 이 모자가 얼마냐고 물었어요.
A customer asked how much this hat is.
Minsu asked me if tomorrow is the test.
엄마가 저 사람이 제 친구냐고 물었어요.
Mom asked if that person is my friend.
cz: Hajun asked me if that person is a teacher.
Sujin asked me if today is Monday.

fe: My friend suggested having lunch together.
xk: 다른 사람이 함께 하자고 한 말을 전해요. 동사 어간에 -자고 해요를 붙여요.
xe: Report a "let's…" suggestion. Add -자고 해요 to the verb stem.
nk: '같이 가자'를 '같이 간다고'로 말하면 '친구가 간다'는 뜻이 돼요. 제안에는 시제를 붙이지 않아요(✕ 갔자고). 말한 사람이 윗사람이면 -자고 하셨어요를 써요.
ne: Saying 같이 간다고 means "my friend is going", not "let's go". Do not add a tense (✕ 갔자고). If the speaker is a senior person, use -자고 하셨어요.
ex: The team leader suggested having a team dinner today.
Mike suggested meeting at the park on Saturday.
Mom suggested we cook dinner together.
The teacher suggested we all sing together.
cz: Jimin suggested we ride bikes together.
Yuna suggested having tea during the break.

fe: Minsu said let's not be late tomorrow.
xk: 하지 말자고 한 제안을 전해요. 동사 어간에 -지 말자고 해요를 붙여요.
xe: Report a "let's not…" suggestion. Add -지 말자고 해요 to the verb stem.
nk: '-지 말자'는 같이 하지 말자는 뜻이에요. 상대에게만 하지 말라고 하는 '-지 마세요'와 달라요. ㄹ 동사도 ㄹ이 그대로예요(놀지).
ne: -지 말자 means "let's both not do it". It differs from -지 마세요, which tells only the listener not to. ㄹ verbs keep ㄹ (놀지).
ex: 팀장님이 회의 중에 전화하지 말자고 하셨어요.
The team leader said let's not make calls during the meeting.
하준이 밤에 커피를 마시지 말자고 했어요.
Hajun said let's not drink coffee at night.
Sara said let's not make noise in the library.
엄마가 오늘은 밖에서 먹지 말자고 했어요.
Mom said let's not eat out today.
선생님이 시험 전에 놀지 말자고 하셨어요.
The teacher said let's not play before the test.
cz: Seoyeon said let's not take photos here.
Dohyun said let's not throw trash on the street.

fe: I couldn't sleep last night because I was working late.
xk: 한 활동에 시간과 힘을 써서 다른 일을 못 했을 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-느라고'를 붙여요. 시제는 뒤 문장에만 써요.
xe: Use it when spending time and effort on one activity caused something else not to happen. Add -느라고 to a verb stem. Put the tense only on the last verb.
nk: 주로 '못 했다'나 안 좋은 결과가 와요. 앞뒤 주어는 같아야 해요. 형용사에는 못 써요. '-아/어서'는 이런 제한이 없어요.
ne: The result is usually something you couldn't do or something bad. Both clauses need the same subject, and it doesn't work with adjectives. -아/어서 has no such limits.
ex: I couldn't do my homework because I was playing games.
I missed the bus because I was talking with a friend.
I didn't see the text because I was watching a movie.
I stayed up all night because I was making a cake.
I came home late because I was preparing a presentation.
I couldn't eat lunch because I was cleaning.
cz: I was late for class because I was busy waiting for a friend.
I was late for the meeting because I was busy looking for my wallet.

fe: I was so tired, so I went to bed early.
xk: 이유를 말할 때 써요. '-아/어서'와 뜻이 비슷해요. 어간에 '-아/어'를 붙이고 '가지고'를 써요.
xe: Use it to give a reason. It means about the same as -아/어서. Add -아/어 to the stem, then 가지고.
nk: 친구나 가족에게 편하게 말할 때 써요. 보고서, 면접, 발표 같은 글이나 격식 있는 말에서는 '-아/어서'를 써요.
ne: It sounds casual and is for speech with friends and family. In reports, interviews, or formal speech, use -아/어서.
ex: It rained, so I couldn't go.
The road was jammed, so I was late.
배가 너무 아파 가지고 병원에 갔어요.
My stomach hurt so much that I went to the hospital.
I lost my wallet, so I walked home.
돈이 없어 가지고 아무것도 못 샀어요.
I had no money, so I couldn't buy anything.
It was so hot that I turned on the air conditioner.
cz: 길이 ___ 택시를 탔어요. (멀다 + 가지고, 편한 말)
It was a long way, so I took a taxi. (casual speech)
너무 ___ 커피를 마셨어요. (졸리다 + 가지고, 편한 말)
I was so sleepy, so I drank coffee. (casual speech)

fe: I don't know if the weather will be nice tomorrow.
xk: 아직 정해지지 않았거나 알 수 없는 앞일을 말해요. 어간에 -(으)ㄹ지를 붙이고 '모르겠어요'를 써요. 받침이 있으면 -을지, 없으면 -ㄹ지예요.
xe: Use it for a future matter that is not decided or not known yet. Add -(으)ㄹ지 to the stem, then 모르겠어요. After a final consonant use -을지; after a vowel use -ㄹ지.
nk: 아직 정해지지 않은 앞일이나 예측하는 일에는 -(으)ㄹ지를 써요. 이미 정해진 일정이나 사실은 앞일이어도 -는지가 자연스러워요(회의가 몇 시에 끝나는지). 예/아니요로 고민할 때는 -(으)ㄹ지 말지를 써요.
ne: Use -(으)ㄹ지 for a future matter that is undecided or only predicted. A fixed schedule or fact takes -는지 even if it is in the future (회의가 몇 시에 끝나는지). For yes/no indecision, say -(으)ㄹ지 말지.
ex: I'm worried the test will be hard.
I don't know what to eat for dinner.
새 직장에서 잘 지낼 수 있을지 모르겠어요.
I don't know if I can get along well at my new job.
이 신발이 맞을지 몰라서 신어 봤어요.
I didn't know if these shoes would fit, so I tried them on.
I didn't know if the train would be late, so I set out early.
cz: 내일 이 선물을 줄 거예요. 동생이 ___ 모르겠어요 (좋아하다 + -(으)ㄹ지).
I'll give this gift tomorrow. I don't know if my younger sibling will like it.
다음 주에 숙제가 ___ 몰라서 미리 했어요 (많다 + -(으)ㄹ지).
I didn't know if there would be a lot of homework next week, so I did some in advance.

fe: I left early because I was worried the road would be jammed.
xk: 그런 일이 생길까 걱정돼서 미리 한 일을 말해요. 앞에는 걱정하는 일, 뒤에는 미리 한 행동을 써요.
xe: Use it for something you did ahead of time because you worried a certain thing might happen. Put the worry first, then the action you took.
nk: 걱정하는 일은 아직 일어나지 않았어요. 앞일이면 뒤 동사는 -(으)ㄹ 거예요로 써요(내일 길이 막힐까 봐 일찍 나갈 거예요). 이미 일어난 이유는 -아/어서나 -기 때문에를 써요.
ne: The feared event has not happened yet. For a future plan, put the last verb in -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (내일 길이 막힐까 봐 일찍 나갈 거예요). A reason that has already happened takes -아/어서 or -기 때문에.
ex: I bought bread in case my younger sibling got hungry.
I studied at night because I was afraid of failing the test.
친구가 화낼까 봐 말을 못 했어요.
I couldn't say it because I was afraid my friend would get angry.
I put my phone in my bag so I wouldn't lose it.
I made a lot of food in case it wasn't enough.
cz: I closed the door because I was worried the child would be cold.
I wrote the appointment on the calendar because I was afraid I would forget it.

fe: I'm thinking of meeting a friend this weekend.
xk: 아직 확실하지 않은 계획이나 생각을 말해요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ까 해요를 붙여요. '~할 생각이에요'와 비슷해요.
xe: Use it for a plan or idea that is not settled yet. Add -(으)ㄹ까 해요 to a verb stem. It means "I'm thinking of doing …".
nk: 이미 정한 일은 -기로 했어요, 아직 고민 중인 일은 -(으)ㄹ까 해요를 써요. 형용사에는 쓰지 않아요. -(으)ㄹ까 봐(걱정)와 달라요: 봐는 걱정, 해는 계획이에요.
ne: Use -기로 했어요 for something already decided, and -(으)ㄹ까 해요 for something you are still considering. It is used with verbs only. Do not mix it up with -(으)ㄹ까 봐 (worry): 봐 is worry, 해 is a plan.
ex: I'm thinking of watching a movie tonight.
I'm thinking of starting to exercise next month.
I was thinking of having noodles for lunch.
새 노트북을 살까 하고 가게에 왔어요.
I came to the store thinking of buying a new laptop.
I'm thinking about quitting my job.
cz: I'm tired, so I'm thinking of going to bed early today.
아직 안 정했어요. 내년에 다른 도시로___ (이사하다).
I haven't decided yet. I'm thinking of moving to another city next year.

fe: If you want to lose weight, you have to walk every day.
xk: 이루고 싶은 일을 앞에 말하고, 그 일에 필요한 것이나 방법을 뒤에 말해요. 받침이 없거나 ㄹ이면 -려면, 받침이 있으면 -으려면이에요.
xe: Put the goal first, then say what is needed or how to do it. No final consonant or ㄹ: -려면. Other consonants: -으려면.
nk: -(으)면은 그냥 조건이에요. -(으)려면은 '~하고 싶으면'이라는 목표가 앞에 있어요. 뒤에는 -아/어야 해요, -(으)면 돼요, -아/어 보세요가 자주 와요. 앞에 과거(-았/었)는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: -(으)면 is a plain condition. -(으)려면 means "if you want to …", so a goal comes first. It is often followed by -아/어야 해요, -(으)면 돼요, or -아/어 보세요. Don't use the past tense before it.
ex: If you want to make friends, try saying hello first.
비행기 표를 사려면 여권이 있어야 해요.
To buy a plane ticket, you need a passport.
맛있는 김치찌개를 만들려면 김치가 잘 익어야 해요.
To make good kimchi stew, the kimchi has to be well fermented.
시험에 붙으려면 하루에 두 시간씩 공부하면 돼요.
To pass the exam, you just need to study two hours a day.
회사에 늦지 않으려면 여섯 시에 일어나야 해요.
To not be late for work, you have to get up at six.
To borrow this book, you need a student ID.
cz: If you want to live long, you have to be healthy.
If you want to take the bus, go to the bus stop.

fe: When you get home, wash your hands first.
xk: 그런 일이 생기면 그때 할 일을 말해요. 어간에 -거든을 붙여요. 뒤에는 부탁·명령·약속이 와요.
xe: Says "if/when that happens, then (do this)". Add -거든 to the stem. A request, command, or promise follows.
nk: 친한 사이에서 자주 써요. 뒤에 지난 일(-았/었어요)은 오지 않아요. -(으)면은 뒤에 아무 말이나 올 수 있지만, -거든은 부탁·명령·약속만 와요. -거든요는 이유를 말하는 다른 말이에요.
ne: Common among people who know each other well. A past-tense ending can't follow. -(으)면 can be followed by any kind of sentence, but -거든 only by a request, command, or promise. -거든요 is a different ending that gives a reason.
ex: 배가 고프거든 냉장고에 있는 빵을 드세요.
If you get hungry, have the bread in the fridge.
If you have a question, ask me.
시험이 끝나거든 같이 영화 보러 갈게요.
When the exam is over, I'll go see a movie with you.
If the road is jammed, take the subway.
If you're tired, go to bed first.
cz: When you finish all your homework, go out and play.
If you need money, tell me.

fk: 이 가방은 예쁘기는 하지만 너무 무거워요.
fe: This bag is pretty, I admit, but it's too heavy.
xk: 좋은 점이나 맞는 점을 먼저 인정하고, 그다음에 다른 면을 말해요. 어간에 -기는 하지만을 붙여요.
xe: First admit a good or true point, then give the other side. Add -기는 하지만 to the stem.
nk: -지만보다 '그건 맞아요' 하고 인정하는 느낌이 강해요. 앞의 말이 사실이라는 걸 먼저 보여 줘요. 앞에 과거를 붙이지 않고 뒤에서 했지만으로 과거를 나타내요.
ne: It sounds more like 'that's true' than plain -지만. It shows the first point is real before the contrast. Don't put the past tense before -기는; put it after, as 했지만.
ex: 그 사람은 친절하기는 하지만 약속을 자주 잊어요.
He is kind, but he often forgets promises.
Korean is hard, but it's fun.
지하철이 빠르기는 하지만 사람이 너무 많아요.
The subway is fast, but there are too many people.
그 책을 읽기는 했지만 내용을 잘 몰라요.
I did read that book, but I don't understand the content well.
새 집이 좋기는 하지만 회사에서 멀어요.
The new house is nice, but it's far from work.
cz: This restaurant is clean, I'll give you that, but the price is high.
I did solve that problem, but the answer was wrong.

fk: 이 옷은 마음에 들기는 한데 좀 커요.
fe: I do like this outfit, but it's a bit big.
xk: 대화에서 좋은 점을 인정하고 뒷말을 부드럽게 이어요. 어간에 -기는 한데를 붙이고, 끝에 요를 붙이면 더 공손해요.
xe: In conversation, admit a point and lead gently into the rest. Add -기는 한데 to the stem; adding 요 makes it more polite.
nk: -기는 하지만보다 말할 때 더 자주 써요. 뒷말을 하지 않고 '-기는 한데요…'로 끝내면 '사실은 문제가 있어요'라는 뜻을 부드럽게 전해요. 글에서는 -기는 하지만이 더 자연스러워요.
ne: It is more common in speech than -기는 하지만. Ending with '-기는 한데요…' softly hints that there is a problem. In writing, -기는 하지만 is more natural.
ex: 배가 고프기는 한데 지금은 먹고 싶지 않아요.
I am hungry, but I don't want to eat now.
그 일이 힘들기는 한데 할 수 있어요.
The work is hard, but I can do it.
친구를 만나기는 했는데 이야기는 많이 안 했어요.
I did meet my friend, but we didn't talk much.
고향이 그립기는 한데요, 지금은 갈 수 없어요.
I do miss my hometown, but I can't go now.
운동을 하기는 한데 자주는 못 해요.
I do exercise, but I can't do it often.
cz: Work is busy these days, but it's rewarding.
I did go to that shop, but there was nobody there.

fe: He has a lot of money for a student.
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙여요. 그 부류에서 보통 생각하는 것과 다르다고 말할 때 써요.
xe: Attach it to a noun. Use it to say something is different from what you would usually expect of that group.
nk: '그런 부류 중에서는 드물게'라는 뜻이라서 은근한 비교예요. 기대와 다르다는 말이라서 칭찬에도 불만에도 써요.
ne: It means 'unusually, for that kind of thing', so it is a quiet comparison. It sets what you see against what is expected of that kind, so it works for both praise and complaint.
ex: She thinks deeply for a child.
The rooms in this house are big for Seoul.
That singer is friendly for a star.
He is short for an athlete.
cz: 저 아이는 ___ 글을 잘 읽어요. (다섯 살 + 치고는)
That child reads well for a five-year-old.
That person is very young for a professor.

fk: 이 집은 넓기는 해요. 그런데 너무 비싸요.
fe: This house is spacious, yes. But it's too expensive.
xk: 앞 말이 맞다고 인정하는 말이에요. 어간에 -기는 해요를 붙이고, 뒤에 다른 면을 이어 말해요.
xe: It admits that something is true. Attach -기는 해요 to the stem, then follow with the other side.
nk: -기는 하지만처럼 '그건 맞아요'라는 느낌이에요. 문장을 여기서 끝내도 '그런데 문제가 있어요'라는 뜻이 전해져요. 과거는 -기는 했어요로 바꿔요.
ne: Like -기는 하지만, it feels like "yes, that's true". Even if you stop the sentence here, it hints that there is a problem. For past, change it to -기는 했어요.
ex: 그 가게는 싸기는 해요. 그런데 멀어요.
That shop is cheap, yes. But it's far.
회사 일이 재미있기는 해요. 그래도 많이 힘들어요.
My job is fun, yes. Still, it's very hard.
한국어 책을 사기는 했어요. 아직 안 읽었어요.
I did buy a Korean book. I haven't read it yet.
여행을 가고 싶기는 해요. 시간이 없어요.
I do want to travel. I don't have time.
우리 아이는 착하기는 해요. 그런데 숙제를 안 해요.
My child is kind, yes. But they don't do their homework.
날씨가 좋기는 해요. 그런데 바람이 많이 불어요.
The weather is nice, yes. But it's very windy.
cz: 이 신발은 ___ 그런데 너무 작아요. (예쁘다 + -기는 해요)
These shoes are pretty, yes. But they're too small.
저는 운동을 ___ 그런데 시간이 없어서 못 해요. (좋아하다 + -기는 해요)
I do like exercise, yes. But I don't have time, so I can't do it.

fe: Oh, not at all. I still have a lot to learn.
xk: 칭찬을 들었을 때 '아니에요'라는 뜻으로 겸손하게 말해요. 상대가 말한 동사·형용사 어간에 -기는요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to politely say "not at all" after a compliment. Attach -기는요 to the verb/adjective stem the other person just said.
nk: 상대 말을 그대로 되받아서 '그렇지 않아요'라고 해요. 그냥 '아니에요'보다 부드러워요. 겸손하게 사양할 때도 있고, '피곤하기는요. 잠을 많이 잤어요.'처럼 진짜로 아니라고 할 때도 있어요. 물음에 답할 때도 써요: 피곤하세요? 피곤하기는요.
ne: You echo the other person's word and say it isn't so. It sounds softer than a plain '아니에요'. Sometimes it is modest, and sometimes it really means "no", as in '피곤하기는요. 잠을 많이 잤어요.' It can also answer a question with "no, not at all": 피곤하세요? 피곤하기는요.
ex: 옷이 정말 예쁘네요. — 예쁘기는요. 싸게 산 옷이에요.
Your clothes are so pretty. — Pretty? Not really. I bought them cheap.
요즘 많이 바쁘세요? — 바쁘기는요. 오늘은 일찍 끝났어요.
Are you very busy these days? — Busy? Not at all. I finished early today.
한국어 발음이 좋네요. — 좋기는요. 아직 어려워요.
Your Korean pronunciation is good. — Good? Not really. It's still hard.
피곤하지 않아요? — 피곤하기는요. 잠을 많이 잤어요.
Aren't you tired? — Tired? Not at all. I slept a lot.
집이 넓고 멋있네요. — 멋있기는요. 오래된 집이에요.
Your house is big and nice. — Nice? Not really. It's an old house.
Thanks for helping. — No need to thank me. I had fun too.
cz: 일을 정말 빨리 하시네요. — ___ 아직 많이 느려요. (빠르다)
You work so fast. — Fast? Not at all. I'm still very slow.
머리가 정말 좋으시네요. — ___ 그냥 열심히 해요. (좋다)
You're really smart. — Smart? Not really. I just work hard.

fk: 손님이 오니까 음료수를 미리 사 뒀어요.
fe: Guests are coming, so I bought drinks in advance.
xk: 나중에 필요해서 미리 해 놓는 일에 써요. 동사 어간에 -아/어 두다를 붙여요. 말할 때는 '뒀어요'로 줄여요.
xe: Use it for something you do ahead of time because you will need it later. Add -아/어 두다 to the verb stem. In speech it shortens to 뒀어요.
nk: '미리', '먼저' 같은 말과 자주 같이 써요. 준비한 결과가 그대로 남아 있어요. 그래서 '사 뒀어요'처럼 '두다'에만 시제를 붙여요. -아/어 놓다도 비슷하지만, 두다는 '나중을 위한 준비'라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
ne: It often goes with 미리 (in advance) or 먼저 (first). The prepared result stays in place afterward, so only 두다 takes the tense, as in 사 뒀어요. 놓다 is similar, but 두다 feels more like 'preparing for later'.
ex: 여행 가기 전에 호텔을 예약해 뒀어요.
I booked the hotel before the trip.
내일 회의가 있으니까 파일을 미리 저장해 둘게요.
I have a meeting tomorrow, so I'll save the file in advance.
겨울이 오기 전에 난로를 창고에서 꺼내 뒀어요.
Before winter came, I took the heater out of the storage room.
시험이 있어서 단어를 미리 외워 뒀어요.
I have an exam, so I memorized the words ahead of time.
There was a lot of bread, so I put it in the freezer for later.
cz: It's my friend's birthday, so I ordered the cake in advance.
다음 주에 이사해요. 그래서 어제 짐을 미리 ___ (싸다 + 두다).
I'm moving next week. So I packed my things in advance yesterday.

fe: I bought fruit at the store, brought it over, and gave it to the guest.
xk: 어디에서 무엇을 해서, 그것을 가지고 다른 곳으로 가서 다음 일을 할 때 써요. 사다, 가지다(가져다가), 따다 같은 동사에 붙여요.
xe: Use it when you do something (buy, pick) in one place, bring the result to another place, and do the next thing there. It goes with verbs like 사다, 가지다 (가져다가), 따다.
nk: 앞 동작의 결과(물건)를 옮겨서 뒤 동작을 해요. 그래서 장소가 두 군데 있어요. 그냥 -다가(하던 일이 중간에 바뀜)와는 달라요. 한 덩어리로 붙여 써요(✕ 사 다가).
ne: The result of the first action (an object) is carried to a new place for the second action, so two places are involved. This differs from plain -다가, where an action is interrupted. Write it as one piece (✕ 사 다가).
ex: 집에서 국을 끓여다가 아픈 친구에게 줬어요.
I made soup at home, brought it over, and gave it to my sick friend.
친구 집에서 의자를 가져다가 우리 집에서 썼어요.
I brought a chair from my friend's house and used it at my place.
마당에서 꽃을 꺾어다가 탁자 위에 놓았어요.
I picked flowers in the yard and put them on the table.
I printed the file at the office and gave it to the teacher.
I got some kimchi from the neighbors and ate it at dinner.
cz: I picked tomatoes in the field and ate them at dinner.
I borrowed a book at the library and read it at home.

fe: It smelled, so I left the door open.
xk: 행동을 하고 그 결과를 그대로 둘 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -아/어 놓다를 붙여요. 말할 때는 '놨어요'로 줄여요.
xe: Use it when you do something and leave the result as it is. Add -아/어 놓다 to the verb stem. In speech it shortens to 놨어요.
nk: 지금도 그 상태예요. '문을 열어 놨어요'는 문이 아직 열려 있다는 뜻이에요. 미리 준비한다는 느낌이 필요하면 -아/어 두다를 써요.
ne: The state is still there now. 문을 열어 놨어요 means the door is still open. If you want the feeling of preparing in advance, use -아/어 두다.
ex: I hung family photos on the wall (and they are still there).
엄마가 탁자 위에 과일을 올려 놓았어요.
Mom left some fruit on the table.
I turned on the meeting room lights (they are on now).
It was cold, so I closed the curtains.
아이가 장난감을 바닥에 다 꺼내 놨어요.
The child took all the toys out onto the floor.
cz: It rained, so I hung the laundry up in the room (and it's still there).
The child is sleeping, so I turned the TV off (and left it off).

fe: Mom made the child eat vegetables.
xk: 다른 사람이 어떤 행동을 하게 만들거나 허락할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -게 하다를 붙여요. 하는 사람은 을/를이나 에게로 말해요.
xe: Use it to make or let someone do an action. Add -게 하다 to the verb stem. Mark the person who acts with 을/를 or 에게.
nk: 문장 속 뜻으로 시킨 것인지 허락한 것인지 알 수 있어요. 한 단어로 시키는 말(먹이다, 재우다)보다 어떤 동사에든 쓸 수 있어요. 내가 하는 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: Context tells you whether it means make or let. Unlike single words such as 먹이다 or 재우다, it works with almost any verb. Do not use it for your own action.
ex: The teacher had the students memorize words.
아버지는 제가 혼자 여행을 가게 해 주셨어요.
My father let me go on a trip alone.
The boss let the staff leave work early.
The doctor made the patient rest well.
My older sister made her younger sibling go to bed early.
cz: The teacher made the students stand at the front of the classroom.
The company had its employees exercise every day.

fe: That news made me happy.
xk: 무엇이 사람이나 물건을 어떤 상태가 되게 만들 때 써요. 형용사 어간에 -게 하다를 붙여요. 기분을 나타내는 말과 자주 써요.
xe: Use it when something puts a person or thing into a state. Add -게 하다 to the adjective stem. It often goes with feeling words.
nk: 주어는 사람뿐 아니라 소식, 말, 노래, 날씨 같은 것도 될 수 있어요. 그것 때문에 상대가 그렇게 되었다는 영향을 말해요. 스스로 그렇게 된 일에는 -아/어지다를 써요.
ne: The subject can be a thing too: news, words, a song, the weather. It stresses that this caused the state. For something that just becomes so by itself, use -아/어지다.
ex: My friend's letter made me happy.
The loud noise made the baby uneasy.
A small mistake made things hard for the team.
The rain made the road slippery.
cz: That remark made me feel lonely.
That song made me feel at ease.

fk: 민수 씨는 매운 음식을 잘 먹는군요.
fe: Oh, Minsu, you eat spicy food well.
xk: 동사 현재일 때, 처음 알게 된 일에 반응해요. 어간에 -는군요를 붙여요. 먹다 → 먹는군요.
xe: Use it with a present-tense verb to react to something you just found out. Add -는군요 to the stem: 먹다 → 먹는군요.
nk: '아, 그렇구나' 하고 놀라거나 이해할 때 써요. 이미 알고 있던 일에는 안 써요. -네요보다 '이제 알겠다'는 느낌이 더 강해요. 받침 ㄹ은 없어져요: 살다 → 사는군요.
ne: Use it when you are surprised or have just understood something. Don't use it for things you already knew. It feels more like 'now I get it' than -네요. The ㄹ final drops: 살다 → 사는군요.
ex: So Sara, you exercise every morning.
This shop is open at night too.
I see, Dohyun, you live near the school.
I see, your little brother is playing a game in his room.
cz: Oh, I see, Jiwoo drinks coffee every day.
I see, Emily, you study Korean.

fe: Oh, this room is really quiet.
xk: 형용사와 명사에 써요. 형용사는 어간에 -군요를 붙여요. 명사는 받침이 있으면 이군요, 없으면 군요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it with adjectives and nouns. Adjective: stem + -군요. Noun: 이군요 after a final consonant, 군요 without one.
nk: 처음 보거나 알게 된 모습에 반응해요. 예를 들어 방에 들어가서 '조용하군요' 하고 말해요. 물어볼 때는 안 써요.
ne: React to how something looks or what it is when you first notice it. For example, you walk into a room and say '조용하군요'. It is not used to ask a question.
ex: This bread is really nutty and tasty.
So that person is the teacher.
The weather is really warm today.
cz: Oh, this book is really fun.
Oh, that person is Minsu's younger sibling.

fe: Oh, so that's why you were late.
xk: 지난 일을 방금 알았을 때 써요. 어간에 -았/었군요를 붙여요. 동사·형용사는 같아요. 명사는 받침이 있으면 이었군요, 없으면 였군요를 써요(학생이었군요, 의사였군요).
xe: Use it when you just learned about something in the past. Add -았/었군요 to the stem. It is the same for verbs and adjectives. For nouns, use 이었군요 after a final consonant and 였군요 without one: 학생이었군요, 의사였군요.
nk: 이유나 결과를 듣고 '아, 그랬구나' 하고 이해할 때 많이 써요. 과거에는 -는군요가 아니라 -았/었군요를 써요.
ne: Often used when you hear a reason or result and think 'ah, that's how it was'. In the past, use -았/었군요, not -는군요.
ex: Oh, it rained a lot yesterday.
아, 사라 씨가 이 케이크를 만들었군요.
지민 씨는 어릴 때 키가 작았군요.
So Jimin, you were short as a child.
So you were very sick yesterday.
cz: Oh, so that's why you didn't go to school yesterday.

fe: Oh, it's raining.
xk: 친구에게나 혼잣말로 쓰는 말이에요. 동사 현재는 -는구나, 형용사·과거·명사는 -구나예요.
xe: The casual form, for friends or talking to yourself. Present verb: -는구나. Adjective, past, noun: -구나.
nk: '아, 그렇구나' 하고 혼자 생각할 때도 많이 써요. 윗사람에게는 안 써요. 윗사람에게는 -군요를 써요.
ne: Also common when you think to yourself, 'ah, I see'. Don't use it with older or senior people; use -군요 with them.
ex: Wow, this puppy is really cute!
Oh, so this is our classroom.
cz: Wow, this flower is really pretty.
Oh, so you like this movie.

fe: People stand in line in front of the popular restaurant.
xk: 차례를 기다리려고 한 줄로 서는 일이에요. 식당, 버스 정류장, 은행 같은 곳에서 써요. '줄을 서요, 줄을 섰어요'로 말해요.
xe: It means to stand in a single line and wait for your turn. Use it at restaurants, bus stops, banks, and similar places. Say 'jureul seoyo' and 'jureul seosseoyo'.
nk: '서다'는 모음으로 끝나서 '서+어요'가 '서요', '서+었어요'가 '섰어요'로 줄어요. 비슷한 말 '줄을 짓다'는 글에서 써요. 말할 때는 '줄을 서다'가 자연스러워요. 새치기는 '줄을 서다'와 반대로 줄에 끼어드는 일이에요.
ne: 'Seoda' ends in a vowel, so 'seo + eoyo' contracts to 'seoyo' and 'seo + eosseoyo' contracts to 'seosseoyo'. The similar 'jureul jitda' is more of a written phrase. In speech, 'jureul seoda' sounds natural. Cutting in line is the opposite of waiting properly in line.
ex: 버스를 타려고 정류장에서 줄을 서고 있어요.
I am standing in line at the stop to take the bus.
If you want to buy a ticket, please line up over there.
점심시간에는 사람이 많아서 줄을 서야 해요.
At lunch time there are many people, so we have to wait in line.
새 휴대폰을 사려고 어젯밤부터 줄을 섰어요.
I have been standing in line since last night to buy a new phone.
여기서 줄을 서지 마세요. 저쪽이 맞아요.
Please don't line up here. The line is over there.
cz: 어제 공연장 앞에서 팬들이 세 시간 동안 ___ (줄을 서다).
Yesterday fans stood in line in front of the concert hall for three hours.
택시를 타고 싶어요? 그럼 여기에서 ___ (줄을 서다).
You want a taxi? Then please line up here.

fe: It might snow tomorrow.
xk: 확실하지 않지만 그럴 가능성이 있다고 말해요. 받침 없으면 ㄹ지도, 받침 있으면 을지도를 붙여요. 과거는 -았/었을지도 몰라요.
xe: You say something is possible though not certain. No final consonant: ㄹ지도. Final consonant: 을지도. Past: -았/었을지도 몰라요.
nk: 뒤에 대비하는 말이 자주 와요(우산을 가져가세요). -는지/-(으)ㄹ지 몰라요는 '모른다'는 뜻이고, -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다는 '가능성이 있다'는 뜻이에요. -것 같다보다 확신이 약해요.
ne: A precaution often follows. '-(으)ㄹ지 몰라요' means 'I don't know whether…', but '-(으)ㄹ지도 모르다' means 'it's possible'. It is less certain than -것 같다.
ex: The road might be slippery. Be careful.
My younger brother may have caught a cold.
그 사람은 지금 집에 없을지도 몰라요.
He might not be home right now.
The test might be easier than you think.
I might have left my wallet at home.
cz: My friend may have already arrived.
The shop might be busy today.

f: V/A 어간+ㄹ/을 리가 없다, N일 리가 없다
fk: 민수 씨가 그 일을 모를 리가 없어요.
fe: There's no way Minsu doesn't know about it.
xk: 그럴 이유가 없다고 강하게 말해요. 받침 없으면 ㄹ 리가 없다, 받침 있으면 을 리가 없다를 써요. 과거는 -았/었을 리가 없다예요.
xe: You strongly say there is no reason for something to be true. No final consonant: ㄹ 리가 없다. Final consonant: 을 리가 없다. Past: -았/었을 리가 없다.
nk: 이유를 함께 말하면 자연스러워요. 내 생각이 아주 강해요. -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다는 '가능성이 있다'이고, -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다는 '가능성이 없다'예요.
ne: It sounds natural when you give a reason. Your opinion is very strong. -(으)ㄹ지도 모르다 says 'it's possible'; -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 says 'it's impossible'.
ex: 하준 씨가 이렇게 쉬운 시험에서 떨어질 리가 없어요.
There's no way Hajun will fail such an easy test.
어제 산 우유가 벌써 상했을 리가 없어요.
The milk I bought yesterday can't have gone bad already.
지우 씨가 늦을 리가 없어요. 매일 일찍 와요.
There's no way Jiwoo is late. She comes early every day.
사라 씨가 그 말을 했을 리가 없어요.
There's no way Sarah said that.
이렇게 큰 가방이 천 원일 리가 없어요.
There's no way such a big bag costs 1,000 won.
cz: 동생이 방금 밥을 먹었어요. 벌써 배가 ___ (고프다)
My younger sibling just ate. There's no way they're hungry already.
저는 열쇠를 가방에 넣었어요. 열쇠가 집에 ___ (있다)
I put the key in my bag. There's no way the key is at home.

fe: The neighbors seem to be having a party.
xk: 보거나 들은 것으로 추측해요. 동사와 있다/없다에는 어간에 -나 봐요를 붙여요. 과거는 -았/었나 봐요예요.
xe: You guess from something you saw or heard. Add -나 봐요 to a verb or 있다/없다. Past is -았/었나 봐요.
nk: 직접 확인하지 못했지만 단서가 있을 때 써요. 단서를 먼저 말하고 뒤에 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 내 일에는 쓰지 않아요. -것 같다보다 단서가 있다는 느낌이 강해요.
ne: Use it when you have not checked yourself but have a clue, which you often mention first. Do not use it about your own actions. It feels more evidence-based than -것 같다.
ex: 지우 씨가 전화를 안 받아요. 지금 자나 봐요.
Jiwoo isn't answering the phone. She must be sleeping now.
가게 앞에 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요. 오늘 할인이 있나 봐요.
People are lined up in front of the shop. There must be a sale today.
민수 씨가 계속 기침을 해요. 감기에 걸렸나 봐요.
Minsu keeps coughing. He must have caught a cold.
The road is jammed. There must have been an accident.
강아지가 문 앞에서 짖어요. 누가 왔나 봐요.
The dog is barking at the door. Someone must have come.
cz: The window is open. Someone must have gone out.
My friend keeps smiling. Something good must have happened.

fe: It seems cold outside today.
xk: 보이는 단서로 상태나 사람·물건을 추측해요. 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ가 봐요, 명사는 -인가 봐요를 붙여요.
xe: You guess a state, person, or thing from clues. Add -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 to an adjective and -인가 봐요 to a noun.
nk: 동사에는 -나 봐요를 써요. 내 기분이나 몸 상태는 내가 아니까 쓰지 않아요. 말할 때는 형용사에도 -나 봐요를 쓰는 사람이 있어요.
ne: Verbs take -나 봐요 instead. Do not use it for your own feelings or health, which you know yourself. In speech some people also say -나 봐요 with adjectives.
ex: 하준 씨 얼굴이 빨개요. 많이 더운가 봐요.
Hajun's face is red. He must be very hot.
This problem seems hard for the kids.
저 사람이 새로 온 직원인가 봐요.
That person seems to be the new employee.
이 우산은 지우 씨 것인가 봐요.
This umbrella seems to be Jiwoo's.
아이가 계속 하품을 해요. 많이 졸린가 봐요.
The child keeps yawning. He must be very sleepy.
cz: People are crying a lot. The movie must be sad.
책상 위에 빨간 가방이 있어요. 에밀리 씨___ (가방).
There is a red bag on the desk. It must be Emily's bag.

f: V 어간+는 모양이다, A 어간+(으)ㄴ 모양이다, N인 모양이다
fe: It looks like it is snowing outside.
xk: 보이는 모습이나 상황으로 추측해요. 동사 현재는 -는 모양이에요, 동사 과거와 형용사 현재는 -(으)ㄴ 모양이에요, 명사는 -인 모양이에요를 붙여요. 형용사 과거는 따로 -았/었던 모양이에요를 써요(예: 추웠던 모양이에요).
xe: You guess from how things look or from the situation. Use -는 모양이에요 for present verbs, -(으)ㄴ 모양이에요 for past verbs and present adjectives, and -인 모양이에요 for nouns. For past adjectives, use -았/었던 모양이에요 instead (e.g. 추웠던 모양이에요).
nk: -나 보다와 뜻이 비슷하지만 조금 더 글말 같아요. 눈에 보이는 상황을 바탕으로 말해요. 내 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: The meaning is close to -나 보다, but it sounds a little more written. It rests on a situation you can see. Do not use it about yourself.
ex: 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요. 새 가게가 문을 여는 모양이에요.
People are lined up. A new shop seems to be opening.
하준 씨가 오늘 기분이 좋은 모양이에요.
Hajun seems to be in a good mood today.
The classroom is quiet. They seem to be taking a test.
현관에 신발이 많아요. 손님이 온 모양이에요.
There are many shoes at the door. Guests seem to have come.
That person seems to be the boss of this company.
cz: 집 안이 어두워요. 가족이 모두 ___ (자다 / -는 모양이다).
The house is dark. The whole family seems to be sleeping.
아이가 아침부터 계속 자요. 어제 많이 ___ (놀다 / -(으)ㄴ 모양이다).
The child has been sleeping since morning. They seem to have played a lot yesterday.

fe: The more you read a book, the more fun it is.
xk: 앞의 정도가 커지면 뒤의 정도도 같이 커지거나 작아져요. 동사나 형용사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ수록을 붙여요. 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
xe: When the first thing grows, the second thing grows or shrinks with it. Add -(으)ㄹ수록 to a verb or adjective stem. Write it as one word.
nk: '점점 더'의 뜻이 있어서 정도가 같이 변하는 관계에 써요. 한 번만 하는 조건은 -(으)면을 써요. 강조할 때는 '-(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록'으로 말해요.
ne: It means 'more and more', so use it when two degrees change together. For a simple one-time condition, use -(으)면. To stress it, say '-(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록'.
ex: The more I exercise, the lighter my body gets.
The more you eat kimchi, the tastier it is.
The colder the weather, the better hot tea is.
The bigger the house, the harder it is to clean.
The more I meet Seoyeon, the nicer a person she is.
The more I walk, the more my legs hurt.
cz: The more I listen to Korean songs, the more I like them.
The heavier the bag, the harder it is to carry.

fk: 잠을 못 잔 탓에 오늘 너무 피곤해요.
fe: I'm very tired today because I couldn't sleep.
xk: 나쁜 결과의 원인을 말할 때 써요. 지난 일은 동사 '-(으)ㄴ 탓에', 지금 하는 일은 '-는 탓에', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ 탓에'예요.
xe: Use it for the cause of a bad result. Past verb: -(으)ㄴ 탓에. Present verb: -는 탓에. Adjective: -(으)ㄴ 탓에.
nk: 원인이 누구 또는 무엇의 잘못이라는 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 결과에는 안 써요. '-기 때문에'는 좋고 나쁨 모두 쓸 수 있어요. '-는 바람에'는 뜻밖의 일이고, '탓에'는 잘못을 말해요.
ne: It carries a sense of blame for the cause. Don't use it for good results. -기 때문에 works for good or bad. -는 바람에 is about something unexpected, while 탓에 points to fault.
ex: 연락이 늦은 탓에 친구가 화가 났어요.
Because I was slow to get in touch, my friend got angry.
과속을 하는 탓에 사고가 자주 나요.
Accidents happen often because people speed.
I wasted money, so my pay runs short.
I fell a lot because the road was slippery.
직원이 일을 소홀히 한 탓에 손님이 줄었어요.
Because the staff did the job carelessly, we lost customers.
cz: 약속 시간을 ___ 친구가 오래 기다렸어요. (잊다 + -(으)ㄴ 탓에)
I forgot the meeting time, so my friend waited a long time.
방이 ___ 잠을 잘 못 잤어요. (덥다 + -(으)ㄴ 탓에)
The room was hot, so I couldn't sleep well.

fe: It's all my fault.
xk: 명사 뒤에 '탓에'를 붙이면 나쁜 결과의 원인이 돼요. '탓이다'로 문장을 끝낼 수도 있어요. 자기 잘못은 '제 탓이에요'라고 해요.
xe: Put 탓에 after a noun to give the cause of a bad result. You can also end a sentence with 탓이다. To admit your own fault, say '제 탓이에요'.
nk: '제 탓이에요'는 자기 잘못을 인정하는 말이라서 자주 써요. 남에게 '당신 탓이에요'라고 하면 무례하게 들려요. 좋은 결과에는 안 써요.
ne: '제 탓이에요' admits your own fault, so people say it often. Telling someone '당신 탓이에요' sounds rude. Don't use it for good results.
ex: 공사 소리 탓에 잠을 못 잤어요.
I couldn't sleep because of the construction noise.
My bank account is empty because of overspending.
This mistake is due to carelessness.
My stomach hurts. It's the cold milk's fault.
The family grew apart because of indifference.
cz: I couldn't do my homework. It's all because of the game.
The work was ruined because of a small mistake.

fe: The test was hard, and on top of that, I even ran out of time.
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙여요. 이미 안 좋은 일이 있는데, 마지막 남은 것까지 안 좋아질 때 써요.
xe: Attach it after a noun. Use it when things are already bad and the last remaining thing goes wrong too.
nk: 보통 나쁜 일에 써요. 좋은 일에는 '까지'를 써요. '까지'보다 더 힘들고 속상한 느낌이에요. 뒤에 '없다, 떠나다, 고장 나다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.
ne: Mostly used for bad things. For good things, use 까지. It feels more upset and hopeless than 까지. It often goes with words like 없다, 떠나다, and 고장 나다.
ex: The company is struggling, and even my pay was cut.
There are no customers in the shop, and now it's even raining.
My younger sibling is sick, and even Mom is sick.
We ate even the last bit of bread that was left.
During the trip, even my camera broke down.
cz: There's no rice, and there's not even water.
I don't know the way, and even the internet doesn't work.

f: V 어간+(으)ㄴ/는 탓에, A 어간+(으)ㄴ 탓에
fe: I was late for class because I overslept.
xk: 나쁜 결과의 이유를 말해요. 동사는 지난 일에 -(으)ㄴ 탓에, 지금 하는 일에 -는 탓에를 써요. 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ 탓에예요.
xe: Gives the reason for a bad result. For verbs, use -(으)ㄴ 탓에 for past actions and -는 탓에 for ongoing ones. For adjectives, use -(으)ㄴ 탓에.
nk: 나쁜 결과에만 써요. 좋은 결과에는 쓰지 않아요. '때문에'는 그냥 이유를 말하지만, '탓에'는 잘못이나 책임이 있다는 느낌이에요. 다른 사람 잘못으로 말하면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
ne: Use it only for bad results, never good ones. 때문에 just states a reason, but 탓에 implies fault or blame. Blaming another person can sound rude.
ex: 요즘 과소비를 한 탓에 돈이 없어요.
I have no money because I've overspent lately.
I was late for the appointment because of the traffic jam.
너무 짠 음식을 자주 먹는 탓에 몸이 안 좋아요.
I don't feel well because I often eat very salty food.
Work is hard because the weather is hot.
I broke the cup because I was careless.
cz: I fell down because the road was slippery.
약을 ___ 감기가 안 나았어요. (안 먹다 + 탓에)
My cold didn't get better because I didn't take the medicine.

fe: This mistake is my fault.
xk: 명사 뒤에 '탓에'를 붙이면 나쁜 결과의 이유가 돼요. '탓이다'는 '잘못은 이 사람이나 이 일에 있다'는 뜻이에요.
xe: Put 탓에 after a noun to give the reason for a bad result. N 탓이다 means 'the fault lies with N'.
nk: '제 탓이에요'는 내 잘못을 인정하는 말이라 예의 바르게 들려요. 다른 사람에게 '○○ 탓이에요'라고 하면 책망하는 느낌이 강해요. 일이나 상황에는 편하게 써요.
ne: 제 탓이에요 admits your own fault, so it sounds polite. Saying 'It's ○○'s fault' about someone else sounds accusing. It is fine to use for things and situations.
ex: The customers dropped off because of the unfriendly service.
I'm tired these days because of the overtime work.
The accident happened because of speeding.
I couldn't do my homework because I was lazy.
회의에 늦은 건 교통 탓이 아니에요.
Being late for the meeting wasn't the traffic's fault.
cz: 배탈이 난 건 찬 음식 ___. (탓 + 이다, 현재)
My stomachache is because of the cold food.
I was late for school because the bus broke down.

fe: The weather was nice, among other reasons, so I went to the park.
xk: 이유가 여러 개일 때 그중 하나를 대표로 말해요. 어간에 '-고 해서'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to give one reason among several. Attach -고 해서 to the verb or adjective stem.
nk: '-고 해서'는 이유가 이것만은 아니라는 느낌이 있어요. 말이 부드럽고 가벼워요. 이유가 딱 하나이고 분명하면 '-아/어서'를 써요.
ne: -고 해서 suggests this is not the only reason, so it sounds soft and casual. If there is one clear reason, use -아/어서.
ex: I was hungry, among other things, so I ate ramen.
오늘은 비가 오고 해서 집에 있었어요.
It was raining and such, so I stayed home.
The store was far, among other reasons, so I took a taxi.
회사에서 일이 많고 해서 늦게 왔어요.
I had a lot of work at the office, among other things, so I came late.
I was curious about Seoul, among other reasons, so I came to visit.
cz: My head hurt, among other reasons, so I took medicine.
It was very hot, among other reasons, so I opened the window.

fe: Maybe because it rained, the street is quiet.
xk: 확실하지 않은 이유를 짐작해서 말해요. '-아/어서'에 '-인지'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to guess a cause you are not sure about. Add -인지 to -아/어서.
nk: '아마 이것 때문인 것 같다'는 느낌이에요. 이유를 잘 알면 '-아/어서'를 써요. 뒤에는 이미 본 결과나 상태가 와요.
ne: It means 'it is probably because of this.' If you know the reason for sure, use -아/어서. The result that follows is something you already see or know.
ex: Maybe because I slept late, I'm tired this morning.
Perhaps because the food is good, there are many customers.
Maybe because it's vacation, there is nobody in the library.
Perhaps because I have a lot of work these days, I keep getting sleepy.
Maybe because the hotel was clean, I slept well.
cz: Maybe because I'm in a good mood, I keep singing today.
Perhaps because I didn't eat breakfast, I have no energy.

fe: Even if it is hard, I will finish it.
xk: '만약 그런 일이 있어도'라는 뜻이에요. 어간에 '-더라도'를 붙여요.
xe: It means 'even if that happens.' Attach -더라도 to the stem.
nk: '-아/어도'보다 가정하는 느낌이 강해요. '비록', '아무리'와 자주 써요. 뒤에는 다짐, 조언, 규칙이 많이 와요. 이미 일어난 일에는 '-는데도'를 써요.
ne: It is more hypothetical and emphatic than -아/어도. It often goes with 비록 or 아무리. A resolution, advice or rule usually follows. For something that already happened, use -는데도.
ex: Even if it rains, we will play the game tomorrow.
No matter how hard it is, I will practice every day.
돈이 많이 들더라도 꼭 가고 싶어요.
Even if it costs a lot, I really want to go.
Even if the road is jammed, come at the agreed time.
몸이 아프더라도 약은 꼭 먹어야 해요.
Even if you feel sick, you must take your medicine.
cz: Even if the weather is cold tomorrow, I will go to the mountain.
No matter how sleepy you are, write your diary before you sleep.

fe: Even if it is the weekend, I have to work.
xk: 'N이어도'라는 뜻이에요. 받침이 있으면 '이더라도', 없으면 '더라도'를 써요.
xe: It means 'even if it is N.' Use 이더라도 after a final consonant and 더라도 after a vowel.
nk: 주말이라는 조건이 있어도 결과는 달라지지 않아요. 뒤에는 규칙이나 조언이 자주 와요.
ne: Even with a condition like 'it's the weekend,' the result does not change. A rule or advice often follows.
ex: Even adults don't know some things.
Even on Sunday, the store opens.
Even if it is a small task, I do it carefully.
Even if it's a close friend, don't lie.
Even the boss has to follow the rules.
cz: Even if it is summer, it is cold at night on the mountain.
Even if you are the class president, you have to do your homework.

fe: If you are hungry, have at least some snacks.
xk: 가장 좋은 것은 아니지만 그것도 괜찮다는 뜻이에요. 받침이 있으면 '이라도', 없으면 '라도'를 써요.
xe: It means 'it's not the best, but this will do.' Use 이라도 after a final consonant and 라도 after a vowel.
nk: 첫째 선택이 어려울 때 둘째 선택을 권해요. '지금이라도'처럼 늦었지만 괜찮다는 뜻으로도 써요. 가장 좋은 것을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: You suggest a second choice when the first is hard. It also works like 'even now' for something late but still fine. Do not use it for the best choice.
ex: If there is no coffee, please give me at least some water.
If you have no time, at least call me.
If you have no umbrella, at least use a newspaper.
I couldn't go today, but let's go tomorrow at least.
If there is no plane ticket, at least take a train.
cz: If there is no rice at home, at least have some ramyeon.
If there is no taxi, at least take a bus.

fe: Even though I took medicine, my fever won't go down.
xk: 앞 내용에서 예상한 것과 다른 결과가 나올 때 써요. 동사는 '-는데도', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ데도', 명사는 '인데도'예요. 과거는 '-았/었는데도'예요.
xe: Used when the result is not what you'd expect from a fact that is already true. V -는데도, A -(으)ㄴ데도, N 인데도; past: -았/었는데도.
nk: 앞일에는 쓰지 않아요. 내일 일은 '-아/어도'를 써요. '-지만'보다 놀람이나 불만이 더 커요.
ne: Not for future events; use -아/어도 for tomorrow's plans. It sounds more surprised or dissatisfied than -지만.
ex: 비가 오는데도 사람들이 줄을 서 있어요.
Even though it's raining, people are standing in line.
Even though it's very expensive, it sells well.
Even though the test was easy, I got many wrong.
Even though it's Sunday, I have to go to the office.
Even though the road was jammed, luckily I wasn't late.
그 식당은 사람이 많은데도 음식이 빨리 나와요.
Even though that restaurant is crowded, the food comes out fast.
cz: 어제 밥을 많이 ___ 지금 배가 고파요. (먹다 · -는데도)
Even though I ate a lot of rice yesterday, I'm hungry now.
Even though the room is big, it feels stuffy.

fe: I understood only after I heard his story.
xk: 어떤 일을 한 뒤에 비로소 다른 일이 일어날 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-고서야'를 붙여요. 뒤에는 보통 '알았어요, 이해했어요'처럼 지난 일이 와요.
xe: Used when something happens only after you do something else. Attach -고서야 to a verb stem. The next part is usually a past event like 'I realized'.
nk: 그 일을 하기 전에는 몰랐거나 못 했다는 뜻이에요. '-고 나서'는 순서만 말하지만 '-고서야'는 생각보다 늦게 비로소 했다는 느낌이에요.
ne: It means you didn't know or couldn't do it before. -고 나서 only gives order; -고서야 adds a feeling of 'only then, and later than expected'.
ex: I left the house only after the rain stopped.
My brother played games only after finishing his homework.
Only after the illness got serious did I go to the hospital.
혼자 살아 보고서야 엄마의 일이 얼마나 많은지 알았어요.
Only after living alone did I realize how much work my mom does.
I looked at the clock only after I missed the bus.
cz: Only after seeing the exam result did I feel relieved.
Only after I went outside did I realize it was raining.

f: V 어간+지 않고서는 + -(으)ㄹ 수 없다/안 되다
fk: 책을 읽지 않고서는 좋은 글을 쓸 수 없어요.
fe: You can't write good pieces without reading books.
xk: 이 카드는 '-지 않고서는' 형태를 배워요. 뒤에 '-(으)ㄹ 수 없다', '안 되다'가 오면 '그렇게 하지 않으면 안 된다'는 뜻이에요. 이 뜻은 '-지 않고서는' 형태로만 써요.
xe: This card teaches the form -지 않고서는. Followed by -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 or 안 되다, it means 'without doing this, you can't'. This meaning is made only by -지 않고서는.
nk: 꼭 필요한 조건을 강하게 말해요. '-(으)면'보다 더 강해요. 뒤에는 꼭 부정이 와요.
ne: It states a must-have condition strongly, stronger than -(으)면. The ending must be negative.
ex: 돈을 모으지 않고서는 집을 살 수 없어요.
You can't buy a house without saving money.
사전을 보지 않고서는 이 글을 이해할 수 없어요.
I can't understand this text without a dictionary.
약속을 지키지 않고서는 사람들의 믿음을 얻을 수 없어요.
You can't earn people's trust without keeping your promises.
실제로 써 보지 않고서는 좋은 물건인지 몰라요.
You can't tell if it's a good product without actually using it.
일을 끝내지 않고서는 집에 갈 수 없어요.
I can't go home without finishing my work.
cz: 먼저 이름을 ___ 문을 열어 줄 수 없어요. (말하다 · -고서는 + 부정)
I can't open the door unless you say your name first.
잠을 충분히 ___ 내일 일을 잘할 수 없어요. (자다 · -고서는 + 부정)
You can't do well tomorrow without enough sleep.

use: 앞뒤가 어울리지 않는 두 가지 사실(그런데도)
fe: Minsu keeps eating even though he's full.
xk: 두 가지가 같은 때에 있는데 서로 안 어울릴 때 써요. 동사·형용사 어간에 '-(으)면서도', 명사 뒤에는 '이면서도'를 붙여요. 앞뒤 주어가 같아요.
xe: Used when two facts are true at the same time but don't fit together. Attach -(으)면서도 to a verb/adjective stem, or 이면서도 to a noun. The subject is the same.
nk: '-(으)면서'는 두 일이 같이 일어나는 것만 말해요. '도'가 붙으면 '그런데 이상하게'라는 느낌이 있어요. '-는데도'는 앞뒤 주어가 달라도 돼요.
ne: -(으)면서 only says two things happen together. Adding 도 gives a 'yet, strangely' feel. -는데도 allows different subjects.
ex: Jiwoo is always smiling even though she's busy.
That bag is small, yet sturdy.
사라는 한국 사람이면서도 한국어를 잘 못해요.
Sara is Korean, yet she isn't good at Korean.
Hajun stayed home even though he had plans.
That restaurant is expensive, yet it doesn't taste good.
cz: 수진은 ___ 회사에 나왔어요. (아프다 · -(으)면서도, 앞뒤 주어가 같아요)
Sujin came to work even though she was sick.
유나는 길을 ___ 물어보지 않았어요. (모르다 · -(으)면서도, 앞뒤 주어가 같아요)
Yuna didn't ask even though she didn't know the way.

fk: 비용이 들더라도 이 방법을 쓰고 싶어요.
fe: Even if it costs money, I want to use this method.
xk: '-더라도'는 '-아/어도'처럼 '그렇다고 가정해도'라는 뜻이에요. 앞 일이 있어도 뒤 말은 그대로예요. 어간에 바로 붙여요.
xe: -더라도 means 'even if'. The first part may happen, but the second part stays the same. Attach it right after the stem.
nk: 주로 '비록', '아무리'와 함께 써요. 뒤에는 내 생각이나 바람(-고 싶다, -(으)면 좋겠다)이 잘 와요. '-아/어도'보다 강하게 들려요.
ne: Often used with 비록 or 아무리. The second part usually shows your will or hope (-고 싶다, -(으)면 좋겠다). It sounds stronger than -아/어도.
ex: 다른 사람이 반대하더라도 저는 제 의견을 말할 거예요.
Even if others disagree, I will speak my mind.
시간이 오래 걸리더라도 끝까지 해 보고 싶어요.
Even if it takes a long time, I want to try until the end.
날씨가 춥더라도 내일 운동하러 갈 거예요.
Even if the weather is cold, I will go exercise tomorrow.
Even if the food doesn't taste good, don't leave any.
친구와 의견이 다르더라도 서로 인정하면 좋겠어요.
Even if you and your friend disagree, I hope you accept each other.
cz: Even if it rains, we will go on the picnic.
No matter how busy you are, you have to keep your promise.

fk: 이 방법이 좋기는 하지만 조금 비싸요.
fe: This way is good, but it's a little expensive.
xk: 앞 말을 먼저 인정하고, 뒤에서 다른 생각을 말해요. 어간에 '-기는 하지만'을 붙여요.
xe: First acknowledge the first statement, then give a different view. Attach -기는 하지만 to the stem.
nk: 상대 말을 먼저 인정해서 부드러워요. 반박의 첫 단계로 좋아요. '-지만'보다 '맞아요, 그런데…' 하는 느낌이 더 커요.
ne: Admitting the other point first makes it soft. It is a good first step in a rebuttal. It feels more like 'yes, true, but…' than plain -지만.
ex: 그 의견도 맞기는 하지만 다른 방법도 있어요.
That opinion is right too, but there are other ways.
I do know it, but it's still hard.
Studying Korean is fun, but it's hard.
그 식당은 맛있기는 하지만 너무 멀어요.
That restaurant is tasty, but it's too far.
일찍 일어나기는 하지만 아침을 못 먹어요.
I do get up early, but I can't eat breakfast.
The test was easy, but there wasn't enough time.
cz: 저는 매운 음식을 ___ 많이 못 먹어요. (좋아하다 · -기는 하지만)
I do like spicy food, but I can't eat much.
이 가방이 ___ 색이 마음에 안 들어요. (예쁘다 · -기는 하지만)
This bag is pretty, but I don't like the color.

f: V 어간+ㄴ/는다고 해서 · A 어간+다고 해서 · N(이)라고 해서 … -(으)ㄴ/는 것은 아니에요
fk: 돈이 많다고 해서 다 행복한 것은 아니에요.
fe: Having a lot of money doesn't mean everyone is happy.
xk: 앞 말이 맞아도 항상 그런 것은 아니라는 뜻이에요. 동사는 '-ㄴ/는다고', 형용사는 '-다고', 명사는 '-(이)라고'를 써요.
xe: Even if the first part is true, it is not always so. Use -ㄴ/는다고 for verbs, -다고 for adjectives, -(이)라고 for nouns.
nk: '다', '모두', '꼭' 같은 말과 자주 써요. 상대 주장이 너무 넓다고 말할 때 좋아요. '-기는 하지만' 다음 단계로 써요.
ne: Often used with 다, 모두 or 꼭. Good for saying the other person's claim is too broad. Use it as the step after -기는 하지만.
ex: 비싸다고 해서 꼭 좋은 것은 아니에요.
Being expensive doesn't mean it's always good.
많이 먹는다고 해서 살이 찌는 것은 아니에요.
Eating a lot doesn't mean you gain weight.
한국에 오래 살았다고 해서 한국어를 다 아는 것은 아니에요.
Living in Korea a long time doesn't mean you know Korean perfectly.
친구라고 해서 모든 것을 말하는 것은 아니에요.
Being friends doesn't mean you tell everything.
열심히 한다고 해서 항상 일이 잘되는 것은 아니에요.
Working hard doesn't mean things always go well.
cz: 키가 ___ 농구를 다 잘하는 것은 아니에요. (크다 · -다고 해서)
Being tall doesn't mean everyone is good at basketball.
값이 ___ 모두 맛있는 것은 아니에요. (싸다 · -다고 해서)
Being cheap doesn't mean all of it tastes good.

fk: 혼자 따져 봤자 아무도 안 들어요.
fe: Even if you argue alone, no one listens.
xk: 그렇게 해도 소용없다는 강한 말이에요. 어간에 '-아/어 봤자'를 붙여요. 뒤에는 '소용없다'나 '-(으)ㄹ 거예요'가 와요.
xe: A strong 'even if you do that, it's no use'. Attach -아/어 봤자 to the stem. It is followed by 소용없다 or -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
nk: 반박 중 가장 센 말이에요. 앞 단계 뒤에 마지막으로 써요. 상대 노력을 깎아내리는 말로 들릴 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해요.
ne: This is the strongest rebuttal. Use it last, after the earlier steps. It can sound like you look down on the other person's effort, so be careful with seniors.
ex: 화를 내 봤자 문제는 안 풀려요.
Even if you get angry, the problem won't be solved.
아무리 설명해 봤자 그 사람은 안 변할 거예요.
No matter how much you explain, that person won't change.
그 사람에게 물어 봤자 대답을 안 할 거예요.
Even if you ask that person, they won't answer.
비싼 옷을 입어 봤자 마음이 불편하면 소용없어요.
Even if you wear expensive clothes, it's no use if you feel uneasy.
빨리 뛰어 봤자 버스를 못 탈 거예요.
Even if you run fast, you won't catch the bus.
cz: 그 문제는 오래 ___ 답이 안 나올 거예요. (생각하다 + -아/어 봤자)
Even if you think about that problem for a long time, no answer will come.
여기서 ___ 아무도 도와줄 수 없어요. (울다 + -아/어 봤자)
Even if you cry here, no one can help you.

use: 앞 일을 하고도 기대와 다른 결과
fe: Even after taking medicine, my cold didn't get better.
xk: 앞 일을 했는데 기대와 다른 결과가 와요. 동사 어간에 '-고도'를 붙여요. 앞에 '았/었'을 붙이지 않아요.
xe: You did the first thing, but the result is not what you expect. Attach -고도 to the verb stem. Do not put 았/었 before it.
nk: 앞 일을 한 뒤라는 점을 말해요. '-는데도'는 앞뒤 주어가 달라도 되지만, '-고도'는 보통 같은 사람이 앞뒤 일을 해요.
ne: It stresses that the first action was done. -는데도 allows different subjects before and after, but -고도 usually has the same person doing both.
ex: Even after eating a lot, I'm still hungry.
그 길을 알고도 일부러 다른 길로 갔어요.
Even though I knew that road, I went another way on purpose.
Even after studying hard, I failed the exam.
Even after finishing all the homework, I didn't play.
Even after looking at the photo, I didn't know who it was.
cz: Even after meeting my friend, I didn't say hello.
Even after resting enough, I'm still sleepy.

fk: 그 사람은 제 말에 갑자기 따지고 들었어요.
fe: That person suddenly came at me, demanding answers about what I said.
xk: 동사 뒤에 붙여서, 상대에게 달려들듯이 세게 한다는 뜻이에요. '따지고 들다', '캐묻고 들다'처럼 써요.
xe: Attach it to a verb to mean doing it aggressively, as if charging at someone. Examples: 따지고 들다, 캐묻고 들다.
nk: 보통 나쁜 느낌이에요. 화가 났거나 고집이 센 모습을 말해요. '제가 따지고 들었어요'처럼 내 행동에도 쓸 수 있어요. 하지만 윗사람에게 이렇게 하면 무례해요.
ne: It usually has a negative feel. It describes someone angry or stubborn. You can use it for your own actions too, as in '제가 따지고 들었어요'. But doing this to a senior is rude.
ex: 회의에서 하준 씨가 먼저 반박하고 들었어요.
At the meeting, Hajun was the first to push back hard.
동생이 제 말마다 왜냐고 묻고 들어서 힘들었어요.
My younger sibling kept demanding to know why about everything I said, so it was hard.
그렇게 의심하고 들면 대화가 안 돼요.
If you go in suspicious like that, there can be no conversation.
서연이는 제 의견에 무조건 반대하고 들어요.
Seoyeon always goes against my opinion, no matter what.
cz: 친구가 자기 말이 맞다고 ___ 저는 포기했어요. (우기다 + -고 들다 + -아/어서)
My friend insisted fiercely that they were right, so I gave up.
친구가 말하기도 전에 ___ 친구는 입을 닫아요. (따지다 + -고 들다 + -(으)면)
If you start challenging your friend before they even speak, they will shut up.

fk: 미리 준비했더라면 시험을 잘 봤을 거예요.
fe: If I had prepared in advance, I would have done well on the test.
xk: 실제로는 안 한 과거 일을 생각해요. 앞에는 -았/었더라면, 뒤에는 -았/었을 거예요를 써요.
xe: Imagine a past thing that did not happen. Use -았/었더라면 in the first part and -았/었을 거예요 in the second.
nk: 그때 일은 이미 끝났고 바꿀 수 없어요. 그래서 아쉬움이나 후회, 때로는 다행이라는 마음이 들어 있어요. 앞으로 일어날 일에는 -(으)면을 써요.
ne: The event is over and cannot change, so it often carries regret or relief. For future situations, use -(으)면 instead.
ex: 비가 오지 않았더라면 산에 갔을 거예요.
If it hadn't rained, I would have gone to the mountain.
회사에서 더 오래 일했더라면 월급을 더 받았을 거예요.
If I had worked at the company longer, I would have gotten a higher salary.
사춘기에 부모님 말씀을 들었더라면 덜 힘들었을 거예요.
If I had listened to my parents in my teens, it would have been less hard.
길이 막히지 않았더라면 약속 시간에 도착했을 거예요.
If the road hadn't been jammed, I would have arrived on time.
돈을 더 모았더라면 집을 샀을 거예요.
If I had saved more money, I would have bought a house.
cz: 어제 일찍 ___ 학교에 안 늦었을 거예요 (자다).
If I had gone to bed early yesterday, I wouldn't have been late for school.
If I had brought an umbrella, I wouldn't have gotten wet in the rain.

fk: 제가 학생이었더라면 방학에 여행을 갔을 거예요.
fe: If I had been a student, I would have gone on a trip during vacation.
xk: 명사 뒤에 받침이 있으면 이었더라면, 없으면 였더라면을 붙여요. 실제와 다른 과거 상황을 말해요.
xe: After a noun, add 이었더라면 if it ends in a consonant and 였더라면 if it ends in a vowel. It describes a past situation that was not real.
nk: '그때 내가 그 사람(그 날)이었다면' 하고 다르게 생각해 볼 때 써요. 뒤에는 보통 -았/었을 거예요가 와요.
ne: Use it to imagine a different past: "if I had been that person or if it had been that day." The second part is usually -았/었을 거예요.
ex: 내가 의사였더라면 아픈 사람을 도왔을 거예요.
If I had been a doctor, I would have helped sick people.
If today had been a holiday, I would have rested at home.
그 사람이 내 친구였더라면 같이 놀았을 거예요.
If that person had been my friend, we would have hung out.
그날이 주말이었더라면 가게에 안 갔을 거예요.
If that day had been a weekend, I wouldn't have gone to the shop.
제가 선생님이었더라면 숙제를 적게 줬을 거예요.
If I had been a teacher, I would have given less homework.
cz: If yesterday had been Sunday, I would have rested.
If I had been a singer, I would have sung a lot.

fe: This is the friend I met on a trip last year.
xk: 이미 끝난 과거 일을 떠올리며 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요. 동사·형용사 어간에 -았/었던을 붙여요.
xe: It recalls a finished past event and describes the noun after it. Add -았/었던 to a verb or adjective stem.
nk: 그 일은 끝났다는 느낌이 강해요. 반복하거나 끝나지 않은 일에는 -던을 써요. 지금도 하는 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: It feels clearly finished. For repeated or unfinished actions, use -던. Do not use it for something that is still going on.
ex: The bread I ate yesterday was really good.
I gave my friend the book I read last month.
The company where I worked before is in Seoul.
Do you remember the day we played together?
The bag I bought was too small.
cz: I still remember the movie I had watched for the first time back then.
I went again to the restaurant that I had been to last week.

fe: I very nearly dropped the cup.
xk: 거의 그렇게 될 뻔했지만 실제로는 안 일어난 일을 말해요. 어간에 받침이 없으면 -ㄹ 뻔했어요, 있으면 -을 뻔했어요를 써요.
xe: It says something almost happened but did not. Use -ㄹ 뻔했어요 after a vowel and -을 뻔했어요 after a consonant.
nk: 주로 과거형 -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다로 써요. '하마터면'과 자주 같이 써요. 실제로 일어난 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 놀람이나 다행이라는 마음이 들어 있어요.
ne: It is mostly used in the past form, often with 하마터면. Don't use it for things that really happened. It carries surprise or relief.
ex: I nearly got hit by a bike. I was really startled.
I almost fell asleep during the test.
The road was jammed, so I was almost late for the meeting.
I was so shocked my heart nearly stopped.
I almost lost my wallet at the shop.
cz: I nearly fell into the water at the river.
It was so spicy that I nearly cried.

fe: If you keep playing around like that, you'll fail the test.
xk: 지금 하는 행동을 계속하면 나쁜 일이 생긴다고 경고해요. 동사 어간에 -다가는을 붙여요.
xe: It warns that if you keep doing an action, something bad will happen. Add -다가는 to a verb stem.
nk: 뒤에는 나쁜 결과만 와요. 좋은 결과에는 -(으)면을 써요. 보통 다른 사람에게 주의를 줄 때 써요.
ne: Only a bad result follows. For good results, use -(으)면. It is mostly used to warn someone.
ex: If you keep skipping meals, you will collapse.
If you keep shouting, your throat will hurt.
이렇게 돈을 쓰다가는 월급이 남지 않아요.
If you keep spending money like this, no salary will be left.
If you keep looking only at your phone, your eyes will get worse.
If you keep not doing homework, the teacher will scold you.
cz: 비 오는 날 우산 없이 ___ 감기에 걸려요 (걷다).
If you keep walking without an umbrella on a rainy day, you'll catch a cold.
If you keep working without rest, you will get sick.

fe: I should have checked the checklist yesterday.
xk: 과거에 해야 했는데 하지 않은 일을 지금 반성할 때 써요. 어간에 -았어야/었어야 했어요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to reflect on something you needed to do in the past but didn't. Add -았어야/었어야 했어요 to the stem.
nk: '-아/어야 했어요'는 그때 해야 하는 일이었다는 뜻이에요. '-았/었어야 했어요'는 지금 생각하니 잘못했다는 반성이에요. 영어의 'should have'와 같아요.
ne: -아/어야 했어요 says something was required back then. -았/었어야 했어요 is regret now that you didn't do it. It matches 'should have'.
ex: I should have studied more before the exam.
I should have attached the file to the email.
I should have been more honest then.
I should have asked Sara first.
I should have bought the ticket before the trip.
cz: I was late for the meeting. I should have gotten up earlier.
I lost my wallet. I should have closed my bag properly.

fe: I should have rested a little more…
xk: 해야 했는데 못 한 일이 아쉬울 때 써요. 말을 끝내지 않고 뒤에 이유나 지금 상황을 이어 말해도 돼요.
xe: Use it when you regret not doing what you should have. You can leave the sentence open or add the reason or the situation now.
nk: '-았/었어야 했어요'보다 아쉬운 마음이 커요. 끝을 흐리면 혼잣말처럼 들려요. 뒤에 '그런데'의 뜻으로 지금 상황이 와요.
ne: It sounds more wistful than -았/었어야 했어요. Trailing off sounds like talking to yourself. What follows is the 'but' part, the situation now.
ex: I should have taken my medicine, but I forgot.
지난주 부서 회의에서 말했어야 했는데 못 했어요.
I should have said it at last week's department meeting, but I couldn't.
집에서 나오기 전에 문을 잠갔어야 했는데 걱정돼요.
I should have locked the door before leaving home. Now I'm worried.
여행 가방을 더 가볍게 쌌어야 했는데 너무 무거워요.
I should have packed my travel bag lighter, but it's too heavy.
I should have apologized to Seoyeon, but I felt shy.
cz: I have a lot of homework. I should have started early, but I kept playing.
길이 막혔어요. 지하철을 ___ 제가 차로 왔어요. (타다)
The road was jammed. I should have taken the subway, but I came by car.

fe: You should have contacted your friend first!
xk: 해야 했는데 안 한 일을 말하는 사람이 강하게 말할 때 써요. 어간에 -았어야죠/었어야죠를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to say strongly that someone should have done something and didn't. Add -았어야죠/었어야죠 to the stem.
nk: 상대에게 하면 책망으로 들려요. 윗사람이나 공식 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. 나에게 하면 '내가 잘못했다'는 뜻이에요.
ne: Said to another person, it sounds like blame. Don't use it with a boss or in formal settings. Said about yourself, it means 'that was my mistake'.
ex: You should have practiced before the presentation!
You should have done your homework before playing the game!
Mike, you should have come on time!
You should have greeted the customer first!
Oh, I should have helped you first.
cz: 하준 씨, 내일 시험이에요. 어제 일찍 ___ (자다).
Hajun, the exam is tomorrow. You should have gone to bed early yesterday!
The customer is waiting. You should have made the food faster!

fe: I took a shower with my clothes on.
xk: 어떤 상태를 그대로 두고 다른 일을 할 때 써요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ 채로, 받침이 있으면 -은 채로예요.
xe: Use it when you leave one state as it is and do something else. After a vowel add -ㄴ 채로; after a consonant add -은 채로.
nk: 보통 이상하거나 안 좋은 상황에 써요. '-(으)면서'는 두 일을 같이 하는 거예요. '-(으)ㄴ 채로'는 한 상태가 그대로 있는 거예요. 부정은 '-지 않은 채로'나 '안 V-(으)ㄴ 채로'로 써요.
ne: It usually describes an odd or bad situation. -(으)면서 means doing two actions at once; -(으)ㄴ 채로 means one state stays unchanged. For a negative, use -지 않은 채로 or 안 V-(으)ㄴ 채로 (e.g. 안 한 채로).
ex: 마스크를 쓴 채로 말하면 잘 안 들려요.
If you talk with a mask on, it's hard to hear you.
휴대폰을 손에 든 채로 길을 걸었어요.
I walked down the street with my phone in my hand.
서연 씨는 눈을 감은 채로 노래했어요.
Seoyeon sang with her eyes closed.
I got on the bus with my bag on my back.
도현 씨는 아무 말도 안 한 채로 나갔어요.
Dohyun went out without saying anything.
cz: 침대에 눕지 않고 의자에 ___ 잠들었어요. (앉다 + -(으)ㄴ 채로)
I fell asleep still sitting in the chair, without lying down.
I ate without washing my hands.

fe: If I had hurried then, I would have caught the train.
xk: 이미 지난 일이 실제와 달랐다면 어땠을지 말해요. 어간에 -았/었더라면을 붙이고, 뒤에 -았/었을 거예요를 써요.
xe: Use it to imagine a past event going differently. Add -았/었더라면 to the stem, then end with -았/었을 거예요.
nk: 실제로는 그렇게 되지 않았다는 뜻이 들어 있어요. 그래서 아쉬움이 함께 느껴져요. 앞으로의 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 앞으로의 가정은 -(ㄴ/는)다면을 써요.
ne: It implies that things did not actually happen that way, so it carries a note of regret. Do not use it for the future; use -(ㄴ/는)다면 for that.
ex: If we had left early, we wouldn't have been late.
비가 오지 않았더라면 소풍을 갔을 거예요.
If it hadn't rained, we would have gone on a picnic.
퇴직하지 않았더라면 아직도 일하고 있을 거예요.
If I hadn't retired, I would still be working.
그때 돈이 있었더라면 그 집을 샀을 거예요.
If I had had money then, I would have bought that house.
시험 전에 더 공부했더라면 점수가 높았을 거예요.
If I had studied more before the exam, my score would have been high.
cz: If I had written my friend a letter then, my friend would have been happy.
If I had taken the bus, I would have arrived early.

fe: I almost missed the subway.
xk: 어떤 일이 거의 일어날 뻔했지만 일어나지 않았을 때 써요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄹ 뻔했어요, 받침이 있으면 -을 뻔했어요.
xe: Use it when something nearly happened but did not. Add -ㄹ 뻔했어요 after a vowel, -을 뻔했어요 after a consonant.
nk: 실제로는 일어나지 않았어요. 나쁜 일이 거의 생길 뻔했을 때 자주 써요. 앞에 '하마터면'을 같이 쓰면 더 자연스러워요.
ne: The event did not actually happen. It is often used for a bad thing that almost happened. Adding '하마터면' makes it sound more natural.
ex: The road was slippery, so I almost fell.
I almost lost my wallet on the bus.
시험 시간을 잘못 알아서 시험을 못 볼 뻔했어요.
I got the exam time wrong and almost couldn't take the exam.
I laughed so much that I almost cried.
I almost spilled the hot coffee.
cz: The child almost fell down the stairs.
The alarm didn't ring, so I was almost late for the meeting.

fe: I should have prepared the materials before the meeting.
xk: 해야 했는데 하지 않은 일을 반성할 때 써요. 어간에 -았/었어야 했어요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it for something you ought to have done but did not. Add -았/었어야 했어요 to the stem.
nk: 책임이나 의무가 있었는데 하지 못했다는 무거운 반성이에요. 큰 결정이나 중요한 일에 알맞아요. 가벼운 후회에는 -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다를 써요.
ne: It is a serious reflection: there was a duty and it was not met. It fits big decisions and important matters. For light regret, use -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬다.
ex: If you made a promise, you should have been on time.
아플 때 일찍 병원에 갔어야 했어요.
I should have gone to the hospital early when I was sick.
I should not have gotten angry at my friend.
I should have been more careful when driving.
I should have read the contract before moving.
cz: I should have gone to sleep early the night before the exam.
I should have opened the door when the guest came.

fe: I wish I had brought an umbrella.
xk: 하지 않은 일을 가볍게 후회할 때 써요. 어간에 -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬어요를 붙여요. 말할 때 자주 써요.
xe: Use it for mild regret about something you didn't do. Add -(으)ㄹ걸 그랬어요 to the stem. It is common in speech.
nk: 작은 일에 대한 가벼운 아쉬움이에요. 혼잣말처럼도 써요. 인생의 큰 결정에 쓰면 너무 가볍게 들려요. 그럴 때는 -았/었어야 했다를 써요.
ne: It expresses mild regret about small things and works like talking to yourself. For big life decisions it sounds too light; use -았/었어야 했다 instead.
ex: I'm hungry. I wish I had eaten more lunch.
세일할 때 그 옷을 살걸 그랬어요.
I wish I had bought that outfit when it was on sale.
I wish I had called my friend yesterday.
It's cold. I wish I had worn a coat.
여행 가기 전에 지도를 볼걸 그랬어요.
I wish I had looked at the map before the trip.
cz: The class is hard. I wish I had studied in advance.
It's raining a lot. I wish I had stayed home.

fk: 돈이 많다면 큰 집을 사고 싶어요.
fe: If I had a lot of money, I'd like to buy a big house.
xk: 실제와 다르거나 일어날 가능성이 낮은 일을 가정해요. 동사는 -ㄴ/는다면, 형용사는 -다면, 명사는 -(이)라면이에요.
xe: Use it to imagine something unreal or unlikely. Verbs take -ㄴ/는다면, adjectives -다면, nouns -(이)라면.
nk: -(으)면보다 가정의 느낌이 강해요. 정말 일어날 일에는 -(으)면이 더 자연스러워요. 뒤에는 보통 -(으)ㄹ 거예요나 -고 싶어요가 와요.
ne: It sounds more hypothetical than -(으)면. For things that will really happen, -(으)면 is more natural. It is usually followed by -(으)ㄹ 거예요 or -고 싶어요.
ex: If I could rest for just one day, I'd like to go to the sea.
If I were a singer, I would sing every day.
하늘을 날 수 있다면 어디에 가고 싶어요?
If you could fly, where would you like to go?
이 근처에 산다면 매일 걸어서 출근할 거예요.
If I lived near here, I would walk to work every day.
If today were a holiday, I'd want to sleep until late.
cz: 내가 새처럼 하늘을 ___ 구름 위에서 잘 거예요. (날다 + -다면)
If I could fly through the sky like a bird, I would sleep on the clouds.
If I were rich, I would get up early every day.

fk: 어제 일찍 잤다면 오늘 피곤하지 않을 거예요.
fe: If I had slept early yesterday, I wouldn't be tired today.
xk: 지난 일을 가정하거나, 이미 끝난 일을 조건으로 말할 때 써요. 어간에 -았/었다면을 붙여요.
xe: Use it to suppose a past event, or to set a finished action as a condition. Add -았/었다면 to the stem.
nk: 뒤에는 보통 -았/었을 거예요가 와요. 이미 끝난 일을 조건으로 쓸 수도 있어요. 숙제를 다 했다면 놀아도 돼요처럼 말해요.
ne: It is usually followed by -았/었을 거예요. It can also treat a finished action as a condition, as in '숙제를 다 했다면 놀아도 돼요'.
ex: 그때 이 길로 갔다면 더 빨랐을 거예요.
If we had taken this road then, it would have been faster.
아침에 일찍 일어났다면 지각하지 않았을 거예요.
If I had gotten up early in the morning, I wouldn't have been late.
방이 더 컸다면 친구들을 초대했을 거예요.
If my room had been bigger, I would have invited my friends.
If the vacation had been long, I would have gone abroad.
If you have finished all your homework, you may play.
cz: If my friend had come, we would have gone together.
If the food had been tasty, I would have eaten more.

f: V 어간+ㄴ/는대요, A 어간+대요, N(이)래요, 과거 -았/었대요
fe: According to the news, it's going to rain tomorrow.
xk: 들은 말을 줄여서 전해요. 동사는 -ㄴ/는대요, 형용사는 -대요, 명사는 -(이)래요예요. 출처는 앞에 'N에 따르면'으로 써요.
xe: Use it to pass on what you heard. Verbs take -ㄴ/는대요, adjectives -대요, nouns -(이)래요. Name the source with 'N에 따르면'.
nk: '-다고 해요'를 줄인 말이에요. 들은 일이 과거면 -았/었대요처럼 앞에 시제를 써요. 직접 본 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: It is a short form of '-다고 해요'. If the heard event is past, put the tense before it: -았/었대요. Do not use it for things you saw yourself.
ex: According to the research institute, this winter will be cold.
I heard Minsu is very busy these days.
I heard Jimin went home early yesterday.
I heard that person is the new teacher.
I heard Sujin's younger sibling is a university student.
cz: I heard Hajun is learning Korean these days.
I heard Seoyeon's father is a doctor.

fe: The doctor says to take the medicine.
xk: 남이 한 명령이나 부탁을 전해요. 받침이 없으면 -래요, 받침이 있으면 -으래요를 써요.
xe: Use it to pass on someone's order or request. Add -래요 after a vowel, -으래요 after a consonant.
nk: '-(으)라고 해요'를 줄인 말이에요. 원래 말이 명령이나 부탁일 때만 써요. 평서문이면 -대요를 써요. 문장 종류를 먼저 확인해요.
ne: It is short for '-(으)라고 해요'. Use it only when the original was an order or request; for statements use -대요. Check the sentence type first.
ex: Mom says to go to bed early.
The teacher says to bring the book tomorrow.
Mike says to close the window.
The doctor says to drink a lot of water.
cz: My father told me to clean the room.
Sarah told me to write the name.

fe: Minsu is asking if I have time tomorrow.
xk: 남이 한 질문을 전해요. 동사, 형용사, '있다/없다'는 -냬요, 명사는 -(이)냬요예요.
xe: Use it to pass on someone's question. Verbs, adjectives and 있다/없다 take -냬요, nouns -(이)냬요.
nk: '-냐고 해요'를 줄인 말이에요. 남이 한 질문을 그대로 전해요. 과거 질문은 -았/었냬요처럼 앞에 시제를 써요.
ne: It is short for '-냐고 해요'. It passes on a question someone else asked, as it was asked. For past questions, put the tense first: -았/었냬요.
ex: My friend is asking where I live.
The teacher is asking if I ate lunch.
Jiwoo is asking whose book this is.
엄마가 오늘 저녁에 뭘 먹고 싶냬요.
Mom is asking what I want to eat for dinner tonight.
The customer is asking how much this bag is.
cz: Emily is asking what time I went to bed yesterday.
Anna is asking if this hat is expensive.

fe: Hajun suggests having lunch together.
xk: 남이 '같이 해요'라고 한 말을 전해요. 동사 어간에 -재요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to pass on someone's suggestion 'let's do it'. Add -재요 to the verb stem.
nk: '-자고 해요'를 줄인 말이에요. 함께 하자는 제안일 때만 써요. 동사에만 붙고, 형용사와 명사에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: It is short for '-자고 해요'. Use it only for a suggestion to do something together. It attaches only to verbs, not adjectives or nouns.
ex: Yuna suggests watching a movie at the weekend.
My friends suggest meeting early tomorrow.
Sujin suggests taking a photo together.
My younger sibling suggests playing outside now.
My neighbor suggests cleaning together this week.
cz: Emily suggests walking together in the evening.
Minsu suggests going on a trip together next week.

f: V 어간+는 것으로, A 어간+(으)ㄴ 것으로, 과거 -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났어요
fk: 조사 결과 대다수가 버스를 이용하는 것으로 나타났어요.
fe: The survey showed that most people use the bus.
xk: 조사나 통계가 보여 준 결과를 말해요. 동사는 -는 것으로, 형용사와 과거는 -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났어요를 써요.
xe: Use it to report what a survey or statistics showed. Verbs take -는 것으로, adjectives and past take -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났어요.
nk: 내 생각 없이 결과만 객관적으로 전해요. 뉴스와 발표, 글에 자주 나와요. '조사 결과'는 조사 없이 문장 앞에 써요. '-다고 나타났어요'는 틀려요.
ne: It reports results objectively, without your own opinion, and is common in news, talks and writing. '조사 결과' stands at the start without a particle. '-다고 나타났어요' is wrong.
ex: 응답자의 절반이 운동을 하지 않는 것으로 나타났어요.
The survey showed that half of the respondents do not exercise.
연령대가 높을수록 걷기를 좋아하는 것으로 나타났어요.
The older the age group, the more they like walking.
작년보다 올해 책값이 오른 것으로 나타났어요.
Book prices rose this year compared with last year.
평균 수면 시간이 짧은 것으로 나타났어요.
The average sleeping time turned out to be short.
가게에 손님이 많이 줄어든 것으로 나타났어요.
The number of customers in the shop has dropped a lot.
cz: 조사 결과 청소년이 하루에 두 시간 게임을 ___ (하다).
The survey showed that teenagers play games two hours a day.
The survey showed that house prices in this neighborhood are high.

fk: 조사 결과 가장 인기 있는 과목은 영어로 나타났어요.
fe: The survey showed that the most popular subject is English.
xk: 조사 결과의 수치나 항목을 말해요. 받침이 없거나 ㄹ이면 -로, 받침이 있으면 -으로 나타났어요를 써요.
xe: Use it to give the figure or item a survey found. Add -로 after a vowel or ㄹ, -으로 after a consonant.
nk: 조사에서 나온 수치, 순위, 이유를 그대로 전해요. 앞에는 '~은/는'으로 무엇을 조사했는지 보여 줘요.
ne: It states the figure, rank or reason found in the survey as it is. The topic is usually shown before it with ~은/는.
ex: Korea came out in first place in the ranking.
Women made up 55% of the respondents.
The largest age group was people in their thirties.
대답이 가장 많은 이유는 가격으로 나타났어요.
The most common reason given was price.
cz: 조사 결과 가장 좋아하는 계절은___ 나타났어요. (가을)
The survey showed that the favorite season is autumn.
The average daily exercise time was 30 minutes.

fe: Prices in the city came out high.
xk: 조사 결과가 어떤 상태로 보였는지 말해요. 형용사 어간에 -게 나타났어요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to say what state a result showed. Add -게 나타났어요 to an adjective stem.
nk: 높다, 낮다, 크다, 적다처럼 정도를 나타내는 말과 자주 써요. 수치 자체는 N(으)로 나타나다, 정도는 -게 나타나다로 구분해요.
ne: It often pairs with words of degree, such as high, low, big or few. Use N(으)로 나타나다 for the figure itself and -게 나타나다 for the degree.
ex: The share of men came out lower.
서울에서 사는 사람의 수가 많게 나타났어요.
The number of people living in Seoul came out high.
The difference between schools was large.
The satisfaction of the two companies came out similar.
나이가 어릴수록 인터넷 사용 시간이 길게 나타났어요.
The younger the age, the longer the internet use time.
cz: 조사 결과 아침에 운동하는 사람이 ___ 나타났어요. (적다)
The survey showed that few people exercise in the morning.
The test scores of the two classes came out the same.

fe: This place is a market and a tourist spot.
xk: 명사 뒤에 '이며'를 붙여요. 글이나 발표에서 두 정보를 나란히 이어요. '이고'와 뜻이 같아요.
xe: Add 이며 after a noun to link two pieces of information in writing or a presentation. It means the same as 이고 (and).
nk: 글말·발표 느낌이 나요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '이고'를 더 많이 써요. 받침이 있어도 없어도 '이며'예요. 동사·형용사 뒤에는 '-(으)며'를 써요.
ne: It sounds written or presentation-style. In everyday talk with friends, 이고 is more common. It is always 이며, with or without a final consonant. After verbs and adjectives, use -(으)며.
ex: Minsu is a university student and works on weekends.
This shop is a bakery and a café.
서울은 한국의 수도이며 가장 큰 도시예요.
Seoul is the capital of Korea and its biggest city.
이 공원은 시민의 쉼터이며 운동 장소예요.
This park is a resting place for citizens and a place to exercise.
지민은 제 친구이며 같은 반 학생이에요.
Jimin is my friend and a student in my class.
cz: That person is my teacher and my neighbor. (formal, written 'and')
This place is a museum and an art gallery. (formal, written 'and')

fe: The sunset on Jeju was really beautiful, I found.
xk: 전에 직접 보고 새로 알게 된 것을 떠올리며 말해요. 어간 뒤에 '-더군요'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to recall something you saw yourself and learned. Attach -더군요 to the stem.
nk: 감탄이 담긴 존댓말이에요. 밖에서 본 일에 써요. 내 기분이나 내 상태에는 보통 안 써요. 지난 일을 떠올리는 뜻이 이미 들어 있어서 보통 -더군요를 써요. 이미 끝난 일을 말할 때는 '그 사람은 벌써 떠났더군요'처럼 -았/었더군요도 써요.
ne: A polite form with a note of surprise. Use it for things you observed from outside. It is not usually used for your own feelings or state. It already carries a sense of recalling the past, so -더군요 is usually enough. For something already finished, -았/었더군요 is also used, as in '그 사람은 벌써 떠났더군요'.
ex: Everyone in that village was kind, I found.
어제 시장에 갔는데 사람이 정말 많더군요.
I went to the market yesterday and it was really crowded.
That temple turned out to be up on the mountain.
I noticed Minsu exercises every morning.
I saw the craft exhibition and the works were amazing.
cz: The bread at that shop is still really cheap, I found. (polite, with surprise)
I climbed the mountain yesterday and the air was really clean. (polite, with surprise)

fe: Everyone's singing that song these days, I noticed.
xk: 전에 직접 보고 알게 된 것을 친구에게 반말로 말해요. 어간 뒤에 '-더라'를 붙여요.
xe: Tell a friend casually about something you saw yourself. Attach -더라 to the stem.
nk: 친한 친구나 아랫사람에게만 써요. 선생님이나 윗사람에게는 '-더군요'나 '-더라고요'를 써요. 내가 본 일을 전하는 말이라 내 기분에는 보통 안 써요.
ne: Only for close friends or people younger than you. To a teacher or someone older, use -더군요 or -더라고요. It reports what you observed, so it is not usually used for your own feelings.
ex: 민수 집에 갔는데 고양이가 세 마리나 있더라.
I went to Minsu's place and there were three cats!
새로 생긴 카페는 사람이 별로 없더라.
The new café didn't have many people.
Hajun's been getting up early lately, I noticed.
The seats at that cinema were more comfortable than I expected.
Jiu eats spicy food well, too.
cz: Seoyeon, who I met yesterday, was really tall. (casual, I saw it myself)
That book's content was a bit hard. (casual, I read it myself)

fe: The cake was so big that my mouth dropped open.
xk: 너무 놀라거나 감탄할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 글자 그대로는 '입이 열리다'예요.
xe: Said when you are amazed or in awe. Literally, 'the mouth opens.'
nk: 크고 멋진 것, 뜻밖의 일을 볼 때 써요. '쩍'이나 '떡'을 넣으면 더 강해요. 나쁜 일에 놀랄 때는 잘 안 써요.
ne: Use it for big, impressive or surprising things. Adding '쩍' or '떡' makes it stronger. It is not usually used for shock at bad news.
ex: 새 집이 너무 예뻐서 지민은 입이 벌어졌어요.
The new house was so pretty that Jimin was left open-mouthed.
가격을 들었을 때 저는 입이 벌어졌어요.
When I heard the price, my jaw dropped.
민수의 노래를 들으면 입이 벌어질 거예요.
If you hear Minsu's singing, you'll be amazed.
호텔 방이 아주 넓네요. 서연은 입이 벌어졌어요.
The hotel room is really big. Seoyeon was left open-mouthed.
마이크가 한 번에 열 개를 먹어서 모두 입이 벌어졌어요.
Mike ate ten at once, so everyone was left open-mouthed.
cz: The mountain was so high that Sara was left open-mouthed.
이 영화는 정말 놀라워요. 보면 ___ (입이 벌어지다).
This movie is really amazing. When you watch it, your jaw will drop.

fk: 안나 말에 따르면 그 식당이 이번 주에 문을 닫는대요.
fe: According to Anna, that restaurant is closing this week.
xk: 다른 사람에게 들은 내용을 전해요. 'N에 따르면'으로 들은 곳을 말하고, 끝에 -ㄴ/는대요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to pass on something you heard. Name the source with 'N에 따르면' and end with -ㄴ/는대요.
nk: -대요는 '-ㄴ/는다고 해요'를 줄인 말이에요. 내가 직접 확인한 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 동사는 -ㄴ/는대요, 형용사는 -대요, 명사는 -(이)래요, 과거는 -았/었대요예요.
ne: -대요 is a short form of '-ㄴ/는다고 해요'. Don't use it for things you checked yourself. Verbs take -ㄴ/는대요, adjectives -대요, nouns -(이)래요, and the past is -았/었대요.
ex: 일기 예보에 따르면 주말에 눈이 온대요.
According to the weather forecast, it will snow this weekend.
민수 말로는 이 가게 빵이 아주 맛있대요.
Minsu says the bread at this shop is really good.
선생님 말씀에 따르면 시험이 어렵지 않대요.
According to the teacher, the test isn't hard.
I heard Jiu caught a cold yesterday.
They say this book is popular abroad too.
저기 있는 분이 하준 씨 형이래요.
I heard the person over there is Hajun's older brother.
cz: Sara says the coffee at that shop is cheap (I heard it from her).
도현 씨에 따르면 마이크는 다음 달에 한국에 ___ (오다).
According to Dohyeon, Mike is coming to Korea next month.

f: V-는 것으로 / A-(으)ㄴ 것으로 / 과거 -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났어요
fk: 조사 결과 학생의 절반이 아침을 먹지 않는 것으로 나타났어요.
fe: The survey found that half of the students don't eat breakfast.
xk: 조사·연구·검사의 결과를 알릴 때 써요. 동사는 -는 것으로, 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ 것으로 나타났어요.
xe: Use it to report the result of a survey, study, or test. Verbs take -는 것으로, adjectives -(으)ㄴ 것으로, then 나타났어요.
nk: 결과가 분명한 근거라서 '-것 같아요'처럼 약한 말을 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스·발표·보고서에서 많이 써요. 보통 과거 '나타났어요'로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
ne: A result is solid evidence, so don't weaken it with '-것 같아요'. It sounds like news, a talk, or a report. It is usually in the past, 나타났어요. People rarely use it in casual talk.
ex: 연구 결과 잠을 잘 자는 사람이 기분이 좋은 것으로 나타났어요.
The study found that people who sleep well are in a better mood.
설문 조사에서 직장인 대부분이 버스를 타는 것으로 나타났어요.
The survey showed that most office workers take the bus.
검사 결과 이 물은 깨끗한 것으로 나타났어요.
The test showed that this water is clean.
조사 결과 아이들이 책을 읽는 시간이 줄어든 것으로 나타났어요.
The survey found that the time children spend reading has gone down.
수사 결과 그 사람은 현장에 없었던 것으로 나타났어요.
The investigation showed that he was not at the scene.
cz: 조사 결과 많은 학생이 방학에 여행을___ (가다·나타나다).
The survey found that many students travel during vacation.
The experiment showed that this method is easier.

fk: 민수 씨가 오늘 기분이 좋아 보여요.
fe: Minsu looks like he's in a good mood today.
xk: 눈으로 본 모습으로 느낌을 말해요. 형용사 어간에 -아/어 보여요를 붙여요.
xe: Say how something looks to you. Attach -아/어 보여요 to an adjective stem.
nk: 직접 보고 하는 말에 써요. 들은 말에는 -대요를 써요. 동사에는 붙이지 않아요. 과거는 '보였어요'예요.
ne: Use it for what you see yourself. For what you heard, use -대요. It doesn't attach to verbs. The past is '보였어요'.
ex: 머리를 자르니까 사라 씨가 젊어 보여요.
Sara looks younger after cutting her hair.
이 방은 불을 켜니까 더 넓어 보여요.
This room looks bigger with the light on.
시험 때문에 서연 씨가 조금 힘들어 보여요.
Seoyeon looks like she's having a hard time because of the exam.

f: V-는 것은 아니에요, A-(으)ㄴ 것은 아니에요, N인 것은 아니에요
fk: 한국 음식이 모두 매운 것은 아니에요.
fe: Not all Korean food is spicy.
xk: 앞의 내용이 늘 맞는 것은 아니라고 말해요. 동사는 -는, 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ, 명사는 -인 뒤에 '것은 아니에요'를 붙여요.
xe: Say that something is not always true. After a verb use -는, after an adjective -(으)ㄴ, after a noun -인, then '것은 아니에요'.
nk: 오해나 지나친 결론을 풀 때 써요. '안 -아요'는 그냥 부정이고, 이 문형은 '꼭 그런 뜻은 아니다'라는 느낌이에요. 말할 때는 '건 아니에요'로 줄여요.
ne: Use it to clear up a misunderstanding or an overly broad conclusion. Plain '안 -아요' just negates; this means 'that's not necessarily the case'. In speech it shortens to '건 아니에요'.
ex: 저는 주말에 집에만 있어요. 하지만 친구를 안 좋아하는 것은 아니에요.
I stay home on weekends. But it's not that I don't like my friends.
저는 매일 늦게 자는 것은 아니에요.
I don't go to bed late every day.
물건이 싸다고 다 나쁜 것은 아니에요.
하준 씨가 화를 내는 것은 아니에요.
It's not that Hajun is angry.
이 길이 가장 빠른 것은 아니에요.
This road isn't necessarily the fastest.
That person isn't necessarily a doctor.
cz: 저는 운동을 자주 안 해요. 하지만 운동이 ___ (싫다 + -는/(으)ㄴ 것은 아니다).
I don't exercise often. But it's not that I dislike it.
Not every big house is comfortable.

f: V-는 듯해요, A-(으)ㄴ 듯해요, V-(으)ㄴ 듯해요(과거), V/A-(으)ㄹ 듯해요, N인 듯해요
fe: It seems like there's no one in the room.
xk: 보거나 느낀 것으로 조심스럽게 짐작해요. 동사 현재는 -는 듯해요, 과거는 -(으)ㄴ 듯해요, 형용사는 -(으)ㄴ 듯해요. 단, 있다·없다로 끝나는 말(맛있다, 재미없다)은 형용사처럼 보여도 -는 듯해요를 써요.
xe: Make a careful guess from what you see or feel. Present verbs take -는 듯해요, past -(으)ㄴ 듯해요, adjectives -(으)ㄴ 듯해요. Exception: words ending in 있다/없다 (맛있다, 재미없다) take -는 듯해요.
nk: '-것 같다'보다 조금 더 조심스럽고 글말 느낌이 나요. 확실한 사실에는 쓰지 않아요. 내가 본 겉모습은 -아/어 보이다, 들은 말은 -대요가 더 자연스러워요.
ne: It is a little more cautious and bookish than '-것 같다'. Don't use it for sure facts. For a look you saw, -아/어 보이다 is more natural; for hearsay, -대요.
ex: My friend seems not to have arrived yet.
이 식당은 사람이 많아서 음식이 맛있는 듯해요.
This restaurant is crowded, so the food seems good.
Seoyeon seems to be sleeping now.
That shop seems to be closing.
This road seems a bit narrow.
Hajun seems to be a student.
cz: The child is crying. He seems to be hungry.
책상 위에 빈 컵이 있어요. 손님이 차를 ___ (마시다 + -는/-(으)ㄴ 듯하다).
There's an empty cup on the desk. The guest seems to have had tea.

f: V-는 듯 / A-(으)ㄴ 듯 / V-(으)ㄴ 듯 + 행동
fk: 민수 씨가 아무 일도 없는 듯 웃고 있어요.
fe: Minsu is smiling as if nothing were wrong.
xk: 앞의 모습인 것처럼 뒤의 행동을 해요. 동사는 -는 듯, 형용사와 과거는 -(으)ㄴ 듯으로 써요.
xe: Do the next action as if the first part were true. Use -는 듯 after verbs, and -(으)ㄴ 듯 after adjectives and for the past.
nk: '듯해요'처럼 끝맺지 않고 문장 가운데에서 뒤 말을 꾸며요. 글에서 많이 써요. 실제는 그렇지 않을 수도 있어요.
ne: Unlike '듯해요', it doesn't end the sentence; it sits mid-sentence and describes the action after it. It is common in writing. The real situation may be different.
ex: 아이가 꿈을 꾸는 듯 웃고 있어요.
The child is smiling as if dreaming.
손님은 길을 아는 듯 앞으로 걸어갔어요.
The guest walked ahead as if he knew the way.
유나 씨는 피곤한 듯 하품을 했어요.
Yuna yawned as if she were tired.
그 아이는 아무것도 못 들은 듯 계속 놀았어요.
The child kept playing as if he hadn't heard anything.
도현 씨는 배가 부른 듯 숟가락을 놓았어요.
Dohyeon put down his spoon as if he were full.
cz: 마이크 씨는 아주 ___ 웃었어요 (기쁘다 + -는/-(으)ㄴ 듯, 듯이 ✕).
Mike smiled as if he were very happy.
사라 씨는 잠이 ___ 눈을 비볐어요 (오다 + -는/-(으)ㄴ 듯, 듯이 ✕).
Sara rubbed her eyes as if she were sleepy.

f: V-는 모양이에요, A-(으)ㄴ 모양이에요, V-(으)ㄴ 모양이에요(과거), N인 모양이에요
fe: That shop seems to be popular.
xk: 겉으로 드러난 상황을 보고 짐작해요. 동사 현재는 -는 모양, 형용사와 과거는 -(으)ㄴ 모양이에요.
xe: Guess from the situation you can see. Present verbs take -는 모양, adjectives and the past take -(으)ㄴ 모양이에요.
nk: 눈에 보이는 상황이 근거예요. 내 느낌만으로는 쓰지 않아요. 내 일에는 거의 안 써요. '-것 같다'보다 보이는 근거가 분명할 때 어울려요.
ne: The visible situation is your evidence. Don't use it on just a feeling. It is rarely used about yourself. It suits cases where the evidence is clear, more than '-것 같다'.
ex: Seoyeon seems to still be sleeping.
The kids seem to be having fun playing outside.
하준 씨는 어제 일찍 집에 간 모양이에요.
Hajun seems to have gone home early yesterday.
새 학생이 한국 음식을 좋아하는 모양이에요.
The new student seems to like Korean food.
저 사람은 이 동네 사람인 모양이에요.
That person seems to be from this neighborhood.
The air conditioner seems to be broken.
cz: There are many shoes at the door. It seems guests have come.
유나 씨가 계속 웃어요. 시험을 잘 ___ (보다).
Yuna keeps smiling. She seems to have done well on the test.

fk: 아이가 하품을 하는 걸 보니 곧 잠들 모양이에요.
fe: The child is yawning, so he looks like he's about to fall asleep.
xk: 지금 보이는 모습을 보고 곧 일어날 일을 짐작해요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ 모양이에요를 붙여요.
xe: From what you see now, guess what will happen soon. Attach -(으)ㄹ 모양이에요 to a verb stem.
nk: 곧 일어날 일이나 앞으로의 계획에 써요. 지금 일은 -는 모양이에요를 써요. 근거는 눈에 보이는 상황이에요.
ne: Use it for something about to happen or a plan. For something now, use -는 모양이에요. The evidence is a situation you can see.
ex: 버스가 오지 않으니까 민수 씨가 오늘은 늦을 모양이에요.
The bus isn't coming, so it looks like Minsu will be late today.
재료가 다 떨어져서 가게 문을 일찍 닫을 모양이에요.
The ingredients have run out, so the shop looks set to close early.
사장님이 오늘 회의를 길게 할 모양이에요.
The boss looks like he'll hold a long meeting today.
That player looks like he'll win today.
cz: 친구가 가방을 싸고 있어요. 곧 여행을 ___ (떠나다 + -(으)ㄹ 모양이다).
My friend is packing a bag. It looks like she's about to leave on a trip.
아이가 케이크를 계속 쳐다봐요. 곧 케이크를 ___ (먹다 + -(으)ㄹ 모양이다).
The child keeps staring at the cake. It looks like he's about to eat it.

fe: Yuna talks as if she were singing.
xk: 앞의 모습처럼 뒤의 행동을 해요. 동사 어간에 -듯이를 붙여요. '마치'와 같이 쓰기도 해요.
xe: Do the next action the way the first part looks. Attach -듯이 to a verb stem. It often goes with '마치' (as if).
nk: 'N처럼'은 명사 뒤에 붙고, '-듯이'는 동사 뒤에 붙어요. 비유하는 느낌이 있어요. 줄여서 '-듯'으로도 써요. 과거 일은 -았/었듯이로 말해요.
