fe: I suspect the weather will be cold tomorrow.
xk: '-(으)ㄹ 듯하다'처럼 앞일이나 확실하지 않은 일을 짐작해요. '듯싶다'는 내 느낌이나 생각이 조금 더 들어가요.
xe: Like -(으)ㄹ 듯하다, it guesses about the future or something uncertain. 듯싶다 adds more of my own feeling or hunch.
nk: 말하는 사람의 느낌이 강해요. 객관적인 이유를 보여 줄 때는 '듯하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 보고서에서는 '듯하다'를 더 많이 써요.
ne: The speaker's own impression is stronger. With clear objective grounds, 듯하다 is more natural. Reports use 듯하다 more often.
ex: I suspect it will snow this weekend.
그 사람은 지금 집에 없을 듯싶어요.
I suspect he isn't home right now.
This bag seems like it would be handy for travel.
감독님이 내년에 새 영화를 만들 듯싶습니다.
I suspect the director will make a new film next year.
I suspect the test will be hard, so I'm worried.
cz: I suspect young people will like this song.
I suspect the wind will be strong tomorrow.

fe: He failed the test, so it's understandable that he's upset.
xk: '그럴 수 있다, 이해가 된다'는 뜻이에요. 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 법하다'를 붙여요. 이유가 있어서 그런 일이 자연스러울 때 써요.
xe: It means 'it makes sense that…' or 'it's quite natural that…'. Add -(으)ㄹ 법하다 to the stem when a reason makes the situation natural.
nk: 짐작이 아니라 '그럴 수 있는 일'이라고 인정하는 말이에요. '-(으)ㄹ 듯하다'는 앞일을 짐작하고, '법하다'는 이유를 보고 이해해요. 앞에 이유가 되는 말이 자주 와요.
ne: It isn't a guess; it accepts something as reasonable. -(으)ㄹ 듯하다 guesses; 법하다 understands from a reason. A reason usually comes before it.
ex: 그 식당은 맛이 좋아서 유명할 법해요.
The food is good there, so it makes sense that it's famous.
일을 이렇게 많이 했으니 피곤할 법합니다.
You've worked this much, so it's natural to be tired.
혼자 여행을 가면 심심할 법한데 괜찮아요?
Travelling alone could get boring. Are you okay?
민수가 화를 낼 법도 한데 웃고 있었어요.
Minsu had every reason to get angry, but he was smiling.
한 달 동안 열심히 공부했으니 합격할 법하다.
She studied hard for a month, so passing is quite plausible.
cz: 매일 열 시간씩 일하면 몸이 ___ (아프다 + -(으)ㄹ 법하다)
If you work ten hours every day, it's natural for your body to hurt.
He got a present, so it makes sense that the child is happy.

fe: It looks like it's about to rain.
xk: 눈앞의 모습을 보고 '곧 그럴 모양이다' 하고 짐작해요. 동사 어간에 -(으)려나 봐요를 붙여요.
xe: You see something now and guess that something is about to happen. Add -(으)려나 봐요 to a verb stem.
nk: 지금 보이는 모습이 단서예요. 앞으로 일어날 일을 말할 때 써요. 지난 일을 짐작할 때는 '-았/었나 봐요'를 써요. 혼잣말처럼 가볍게 말할 때도 많아요.
ne: What you see right now is the clue, and you use it for something that is about to happen. For past events, use -았/었나 봐요 instead. It is often said casually, almost to yourself.
ex: 아이가 자꾸 하품하니까 이제 자려나 봐요.
The child keeps yawning, so it looks like he's about to go to sleep.
사람들이 자리에 앉으니까 시상식이 시작되려나 봐요.
People are taking their seats, so the awards ceremony seems about to start.
사장님이 청소를 시작하시니까 문을 닫으려나 봐요.
The owner has started cleaning, so it looks like they're about to close.
엄마가 장바구니를 들고 나가시니까 시장에 가시려나 봐요.
Mom is going out with a shopping bag, so she seems to be heading to the market.
사람들이 회의실에서 자꾸 시계를 보니까 회의가 곧 끝나려나 봐요.
People keep checking the clock in the meeting room, so the meeting looks like it's about to end.
cz: 친구가 가방을 싸니까 내일 여행을 ___ (떠나다 + -(으)려나 보다).
My friend is packing a bag, so it looks like he's about to leave on a trip tomorrow.
동생이 책을 펴니까 이제 공부를 ___ (하다 + -(으)려나 보다).
My younger brother opened a book, so it looks like he's about to study.

fk: 저 아이가 그 비싼 시계를 살 턱이 없어요.
fe: There's no way that kid can buy that expensive watch.
xk: 어떤 일이 일어날 이유가 전혀 없다고 강하게 말해요. 어간에 -(으)ㄹ 턱이 없다를 붙여요. 지난 일은 -았/었을 턱이 없다예요.
xe: You say there is no reason at all for something to be true. Attach -(으)ㄹ 턱이 없다 to the stem. For the past, use -았/었을 턱이 없다.
nk: '-(으)ㄹ 리가 없다'와 뜻이 같아요. 하지만 더 구어체이고 감정이 세고 조금 거칠어요. 윗사람이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '리가 없다'가 안전해요. 보통 '없다'로 끝내요.
ne: It means the same as -(으)ㄹ 리가 없다 but is more colloquial, more emotional, and a bit blunt. To a superior or in formal speech, 리가 없다 is safer. It normally ends in 없다.
ex: 밤새 일했으니까 지금 일어났을 턱이 없어요.
He worked all night, so there's no way he's up already.
저는 이 동네가 처음이라서 맛집을 알 턱이 없어요.
This is my first time in this area, so there's no way I'd know a good restaurant.
이 가게가 싸게 팔 턱이 없어요, 항상 비싸니까요.
There's no way this store sells cheap. It's always expensive.
공부도 안 한 학생이 시험을 잘 봤을 턱이 없죠.
A student who didn't even study couldn't possibly have done well on the test.
팀장님이 그런 큰 실수를 모르실 턱이 없어요.
There's no way the team leader doesn't know about such a big mistake.
그렇게 작은 방이 편할 턱이 없어요.
There's no way such a small room is comfortable.
cz: 한국어를 안 배운 사람이 이 글을 ___ (읽다 - 턱).
There's no way someone who hasn't learned Korean can read this text.
아침도 안 먹은 아이가 배가 ___ (부르다 - 턱).
There's no way a kid who skipped breakfast is full.

fe: Surely it's not going to rain?
xk: 믿을 수 없는 일을 듣고 '정말 그럴까요?' 하고 되물어요. '설마'와 함께 동사 어간에 -(으)려고요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to question something you find hard to believe. Add -(으)려고요 to a verb stem, together with '설마'.
nk: 말하는 사람은 '그럴 리 없다'고 생각해요. 그래서 끝을 올려서 물어요. 이 문형은 앞으로 할 일이나 지금 하려는 일을 되묻는 말이라, 지난 일은 '설마 -았/었겠어요?'로 되물어요. -(으)ㄹ 턱이 없다는 '없다'고 말하는 문형이고, 이 문형은 되묻는 문형이에요.
ne: The speaker thinks 'there's no way that's true', so the ending rises as a question. This pattern questions something about to be done or planned; for a past event, ask back with 설마 -았/었겠어요?. -(으)ㄹ 턱이 없다 states 'no way'; this one asks back in doubt.
ex: Surely the shop isn't going to close?
Surely Sarah isn't going to go alone?
Surely Hajun isn't going to cancel the appointment?
설마 이 큰 케이크를 다 먹으려고요?
Surely you're not going to eat this whole big cake?
Surely you're not going to call this late at night?
cz: Surely Dohyun isn't going to quit the company?
설마 비 오는 날에 이 하얀 신발을 ___ (신다)?
Surely you're not going to wear these white shoes on a rainy day?

fe: There's not a single vegetable in the fridge.
xk: N(이)라고는 뒤에 '없다'나 '-지 않다'를 써요. 그런 것이 하나도 없다는 뜻이에요. 받침이 없으면 라고는, 있으면 이라고는을 붙여요.
xe: Follow N(이)라고는 with '없다' or '-지 않다'. It means there is none of that kind at all. Use 라고는 after a vowel and 이라고는 after a consonant.
nk: '하나도', '한 번도', '전혀'와 자주 써요. N밖에 없다는 '그것만 있다'는 뜻이고, N(이)라고는 없다는 '그런 것이 하나도 없다'는 뜻이에요. 전부 없다고 강하게 말할 때 써요.
ne: Often used with '하나도', '한 번도', '전혀'. N밖에 없다 means 'only that is there'; N(이)라고는 없다 means 'there is nothing of that kind at all'. It is a strong, total negation.
ex: There isn't a single park in this neighborhood.
그 사람은 거짓말이라고는 한 번도 하지 않았어요.
That person has never told a single lie.
우리 반에는 남학생이라고는 한 명도 없어요.
There isn't a single boy in our class.
There wasn't a single convenience store in the country village.
하준 씨는 운동이라고는 전혀 하지 않아요.
cz: There isn't a single umbrella in my house.
사라는 아침에 커피라고는 한 잔도 ___ (마시다 + -지 않다).
Sarah doesn't drink even a single cup of coffee in the morning.

fk: 만에 하나 불이 나면 어떻게 해요?
fe: What do we do in the unlikely event of a fire?
xk: 거의 일어나지 않지만, 혹시 일어난다면 어떨지 말할 때 써요. 보통 문장 맨 앞에 와요.
xe: Use it for something that almost never happens, but might. It usually comes at the start of the sentence.
nk: 글자 뜻은 '만 번 중 한 번'이에요. 나쁜 일이나 걱정되는 일을 준비할 때 많이 써요. 뒤에는 '-(으)면', '-더라도', '-(으)ㄹ지라도'가 자주 와요. 일어날 가능성이 꽤 있으면 안 써요.
ne: Literally it means 'one in ten thousand'. It is often used when preparing for bad or worrying things. It is usually followed by -(으)면, -더라도, or -(으)ㄹ지라도. Do not use it when the chance is fairly high.
ex: 만에 하나 지갑을 잃어버리면 바로 카드를 멈추세요.
In the unlikely event you lose your wallet, stop your card right away.
Even in the unlikely case you fail, don't give up.
만에 하나 큰 사고가 나면 이 문으로 나가요.
If a serious accident ever happens, go out through this door.
만에 하나 표를 잃어버리면 바로 말해 주세요.
If by any chance you lose your ticket, please tell me right away.
Even if, in the unlikely case, you fail the exam, it's okay.
cz: ___ 차가 고장 나면 이 번호로 전화하세요.
In the unlikely event the car breaks down, call this number.
Even in the unlikely case I can't keep the promise, please understand.

fk: 하준은 싸움을 말리다 못해 엄마를 불렀어요.
fe: Hajun tried to break up the fight but couldn't take it any longer and called Mom.
xk: 어떤 일을 계속하다가 더는 못 견뎌서 다른 행동을 해요. 동사 어간에 -다 못해를 붙여요. 뒤에는 새로운 행동이 와요.
xe: You kept doing something but couldn't stand it any longer, so you did something else. Attach -다 못해 to a verb stem. A new action follows.
nk: 오래 참거나 애쓴 뒤에 '결국' 하는 행동에 써요. 뒤 행동은 보통 크거나 갑작스러워요. 앞뒤에 같은 동사를 쓰면 안 돼요.
ne: Use it for what you finally do after a long time of putting up with something or trying. The next action is usually big or sudden. Do not repeat the same verb in both parts.
ex: 열쇠를 찾다 못해 새 열쇠를 샀어요.
I searched for the key for so long that I finally bought a new one.
동료가 계속 떠들어서 마이크는 듣다 못해 조용히 하라고 했어요.
A coworker kept chatting, and Mike couldn't listen any longer and told them to be quiet.
에밀리는 혼자 고민하다 못해 친구에게 이야기했어요.
Emily worried alone for so long that she finally talked to a friend.
유나는 달래다 못해 아이를 안고 밖으로 나갔어요.
Yuna tried to calm the child for a long time, then picked the child up and went outside.
도현은 공부하다 못해 책을 덮고 잤어요.
Dohyun studied until it got to be too much, closed the book and went to sleep.
cz: I couldn't hold out in the cold room any longer, so I turned on the heater.
After trying to fix the computer for a long time without success, Mike gave up and called an expert.

fk: 우리 집은 좁다 못해 숨이 막혀요.
fe: Our house is so small it's beyond cramped; it feels suffocating.
xk: 어떤 상태가 너무 심해서, 그보다 더 센 다른 상태가 돼요. 형용사 어간에 -다 못해를 붙여요. 뒤에는 더 심한 상태가 와요.
xe: A state is so extreme that it turns into an even stronger one. Attach -다 못해 to an adjective stem. A more extreme state follows.
nk: '매우 ~하다, 그것을 넘어서'라는 뜻이에요. 뒤 상태가 앞 상태보다 더 심해야 해요. 앞뒤가 비슷한 정도면 어색해요.
ne: It means 'very ..., and even beyond that'. The second state must be stronger than the first. If both are about the same level, it sounds odd.
ex: 이 국은 짜다 못해 쓴맛이 나요.
This soup is so salty it tastes bitter.
밤길이 어둡다 못해 아무것도 안 보여요.
The night road is so dark that I can't see anything.
회의가 길다 못해 끝이 안 보여요.
The meeting is so long that there's no end in sight.
아이 방이 지저분하다 못해 걸을 곳이 없어요.
The kid's room is so messy there's no place to walk.
혼자 걷는 밤길이 무섭다 못해 다리가 떨렸어요.
The night walk alone was so scary my legs shook.
cz: 이 문제는 ___ 풀 수가 없어요 (어렵다, -다 못해).
This problem is beyond hard; I can't even solve it.
The midsummer weather is beyond hot; it's scorching.

fk: 나는 이번 주말에 방을 꼭 치울 테다.
fe: I'm going to clean my room this weekend, no matter what.
xk: 내가 꼭 하겠다는 굳은 마음을 말해요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ 테다를 붙여요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄹ 테다, 받침이 있으면 -을 테다예요. ㄹ받침 동사는 ㄹ을 더하지 않고 '테다'만 붙여요(열다→열 테다).
xe: It states a firm decision: I will definitely do it. Attach -(으)ㄹ 테다 to a verb stem. Use -ㄹ 테다 after a vowel and -을 테다 after a final consonant. For verbs ending in ㄹ, add only 테다 without another ㄹ (열다 → 열 테다).
nk: 혼잣말이나 친한 사이에서 써요. 윗사람에게는 잘 안 써요. 주어는 보통 '나'예요. '-(으)ㄹ 거예요'보다 의지가 더 강해요.
ne: Use it in self-talk or with close friends, not to elders. The subject is usually 'I'. The will is stronger than with -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
ex: 이번 달부터는 매일 아침 일찍 일어날 테다.
From this month, I'm going to get up early every morning.
이 책은 오늘 안에 다 읽을 테다.
I'm going to finish this whole book today.
I will never tell a lie again.
나는 꼭 내 가게를 열 테다.
I'm determined to open my own shop.
누가 뭐라고 해도 나는 끝까지 달릴 테다.
No matter what anyone says, I'll run to the end.
cz: 나는 오늘 저녁에 맛있는 국을 꼭 ___ (끓이다, -(으)ㄹ 테다).
I'm definitely going to make a tasty soup tonight.
다음 주에는 새 친구를 꼭 ___ (사귀다, -(으)ㄹ 테다).
Next week I'm determined to make a new friend.

fe: Go ahead and beat me if you can.
xk: '하고 싶으면 해 봐, 나는 안 무서워'라는 뜻으로 상대에게 맞서요. 같은 동사를 두 번 써요. 앞은 -(으)ㄹ 테면, 뒤는 -아/어 봐예요.
xe: It means 'do it if you want, I'm not afraid', standing up to someone. Use the same verb twice: -(으)ㄹ 테면 first, then -아/어 봐.
nk: 화가 났거나 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 친한 친구나 아랫사람에게 반말로 써요. 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례해요.
ne: It sounds angry or teasing. Use it in casual speech with close friends or juniors. It is rude to elders.
ex: 올 테면 와 봐. 나는 하나도 안 무서워.
Come if you dare. I'm not scared at all.
먹을 테면 먹어 봐. 이 고추는 정말 매워.
Eat it if you dare. This pepper is really hot.
던질 테면 던져 봐. 나는 다 받을게.
Throw it if you want. I'll catch everything.
웃을 테면 웃어 봐. 나는 끝까지 할 거야.
Laugh if you want. I'll do it to the end.
막을 테면 막아 봐. 나는 꼭 갈 거야.
Try to stop me if you can. I'm going no matter what.
cz: 내가 싫으면 ___ 나는 괜찮아 (떠나다, -(으)ㄹ 테면 -아/어 봐).
If you don't like me, go ahead and leave. I'm fine.
그 상자를 ___ 안에는 아무것도 없어 (열다, -(으)ㄹ 테면 -아/어 봐).
Go ahead and open that box if you dare. There's nothing inside.

fk: 그 소식을 듣고 슬프기 짝이 없었어요.
fe: I was unbelievably sad when I heard the news.
xk: '그보다 더할 수 없을 만큼 아주 심해요'라는 뜻이에요. 형용사 어간 뒤에 '-기 짝이 없다'를 붙여요.
xe: It means 'so extreme that nothing could be more.' Add -기 짝이 없다 after an adjective stem.
nk: 주로 부정적인 평가에 많이 써요(지루하다, 무섭다, 시끄럽다). '기쁘기 짝이 없다', '고맙기 짝이 없다'처럼 좋은 느낌에도 쓸 수 있어요. 형용사 '-다 못해'는 뒤에 더 심한 상태가 오고, '-기 짝이 없다'는 정도가 극단적이라고만 말해요.
ne: Mostly used for negative judgments (boring, scary, noisy), but it can also express good feelings, as in 기쁘기 짝이 없다 or 고맙기 짝이 없다. With adjectives, -다 못해 is followed by an even stronger state; -기 짝이 없다 only says the degree is extreme.
ex: This room is filthy beyond belief.
여행 첫날 길이 복잡하기 짝이 없어서 길을 잃었어요.
On the first day of the trip the roads were so confusing that I got lost.
cz: This chair is extremely uncomfortable to sit in.
When I'm alone every night, I feel unbelievably lonely.

fe: His friends turned their backs on him.
xk: 가깝던 사람이나 곳에서 마음이 떠나 멀어질 때 써요. 'N에(게) 등을 돌리다'로 말해요. 사람에게는 '에게', 가게나 회사에는 '에'를 써요.
xe: Use it when you stop supporting a person or group you were close to and turn away from them. Use '에게' for a person and '에' for a shop or company.
nk: 사람이 사람에게, 손님이 가게에, 사람들이 회사에 쓸 수 있어요. 보통 믿음이 깨져서 떠난다는 나쁜 느낌이에요. 그냥 화가 난 것만으로는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: A person can turn on a person, customers on a shop, or people on a company. It usually has a negative feeling: trust broke and they left. Being a little angry is not enough to use it.
ex: The customers turned their backs on that shop.
거짓말을 많이 해서 가족도 그에게 등을 돌렸어요.
Because he lied a lot, even his family turned away from him.
회사가 약속을 안 지키면 고객들이 등을 돌릴 수 있어요.
If a company doesn't keep its promises, customers can turn away.
어려운 일이 생기면 쉽게 친구에게 등을 돌리는 사람이 있어요.
Some people easily turn their backs on friends when trouble comes.
서연은 오래된 동료에게 등을 돌렸지만 곧 후회했어요.
Seoyeon turned her back on an old coworker, but soon regretted it.
cz: The team members turned their backs on the team leader who lied.
저는 힘든 친구에게 절대 ___ 않아요. (등을 돌리다)
I never turn my back on a friend in trouble.

fe: The team leader says they'll be late today.
xk: 들은 말을 동료에게 짧게 전해요. 동사는 '간대요, 먹는대요', 형용사와 과거는 '크대요, 했대요', 명사는 '학생이래요'예요.
xe: Passes on something you heard, briefly, to a colleague. Verbs: 간대요/먹는대요. Adjectives and past: 크대요/했대요. Nouns: 학생이래요.
nk: 동료나 친한 사람에게 써요. 팀장님께 보고할 때는 '-다고 합니다'로 풀어요. 확인 안 된 말은 '아직 확인은 안 됐는데'를 먼저 말해요.
ne: Use it with colleagues and friends. When reporting to a boss, spell it out as -다고 합니다. For unconfirmed news, say first that it isn't confirmed yet.
ex: I heard the client's office is far.
I heard Seoyeon is on vacation this week.
They say the new program is very easy to use.
Hajun says they're in a meeting right now.
I heard the restaurant is crowded.
I heard Jimin left work early yesterday.
cz: Minsu says they're going to the client tomorrow.
I heard this bag is very heavy.

fe: The team leader says to send the materials first.
xk: 다른 사람이 시킨 일을 전해요. 받침이 없으면 '가래요', 받침이 있으면 '먹으래요'예요. 하지 말라는 말은 '-지 말래요'예요.
xe: Passes on an order someone gave. No final consonant: 가래요. With one: 먹으래요. For 'don't', use -지 말래요.
nk: 명령을 전하는 말이에요. '내래요'가 맞는 자리에 '낸대요'를 쓰면 뜻이 달라져요. 상사에게는 '-라고 하셨습니다'로 풀어요.
ne: This relays an order. Saying 낸대요 where 내래요 is right changes the meaning. To a boss, spell it out as -라고 하셨습니다.
ex: The manager says to book the meeting room.
The client says to submit the documents by tomorrow.
Seoyeon says to go home early today.
The manager says not to contact the client yet.
하준 씨가 메일을 다시 확인해 보래요.
Hajun says to check the email again.
의사 선생님이 약을 하루 세 번 먹으래요.
The doctor says to take the medicine three times a day.
cz: Sara says to open the file now.
The team leader says to be sure to keep the appointment time.

fe: The client is asking when the sample will arrive.
xk: 다른 사람이 물은 말을 전해요. '오냬요, 있냬요, 했냬요', 명사는 '얼마냬요'처럼 써요.
xe: Passes on a question someone asked: 오냬요, 있냬요, 했냬요. Nouns: 얼마냬요.
nk: 물어본 내용을 짧게 옮겨요. 말할 때 끝을 올리지 않아요. 상사에게는 '-냐고 하셨습니다'나 '-냐고 물으셨습니다'로 풀어요.
ne: A short way to relay a question. Your voice doesn't rise at the end. To a boss, spell it out as -냐고 하셨습니다 or -냐고 물으셨습니다.
ex: The team leader asks if you can talk on the phone now.
Sara asks if you saw the meeting material.
The customer asks how much this item is.
도현 씨가 점심에 뭐 먹을 거냬요.
Dohyun asks what you will eat for lunch.
The guest asks whether this room is quiet.
The teacher asks whether you finished all the homework.
cz: Emily asks whether you already ate lunch.
Jun asks whether this coffee is tasty.

fe: Hajun suggests we eat lunch together.
xk: '같이 하자'는 말을 전해요. 받침이 있어도 없어도 어간에 '재요'만 붙여요. 예: 가재요, 먹재요.
xe: Passes on a 'let's do it together' suggestion. Just add 재요 to the stem, with or without a final consonant: 가재요, 먹재요.
nk: 말한 사람도 같이 하는 일이에요. 상대만 하라는 말은 '-래요'예요. 상사에게는 '-자고 하셨습니다'로 풀어요.
ne: The speaker joins in the action. If only you should do it, use -래요. To a boss, spell it out as -자고 하셨습니다.
ex: 팀장님이 이번 주 회의를 금요일에 하재요.
The team leader suggests holding this week's meeting on Friday.
서연 씨가 회의 전에 커피 한 잔 마시재요.
Seoyeon suggests having a cup of coffee before the meeting.
The client suggests meeting again tomorrow.
지민 씨가 이 일을 같이 해 보재요.
Jimin suggests we try this work together.
My coworkers suggest going to eat dinner after work.
Mike suggests we finish early today.
cz: Dohyun suggests we order bibimbap for lunch.
Sujin suggests we gather early tomorrow morning.

fe: Applications are accepted in accordance with the relevant laws.
xk: 일을 하는 근거를 말할 때 써요. 법·규정·계약서 같은 말 뒤에 붙여요. 공문에서 읽는 표현이에요.
xe: Use it to state the basis for an action, after words like law, rule or contract. It's an expression you read in official letters.
nk: 'N에 따라'보다 딱딱하고 근거가 분명한 느낌이에요. 법이나 규정처럼 정해진 문서에만 써요. 말로 할 때는 'N에 따라'로 풀어서 말해요.
ne: It's stiffer than N에 따라 and implies a clear, fixed basis. Use it only with set documents such as laws and rules. In speech, say it as N에 따라.
ex: 내부 규정에 의거하여 직원 휴가를 승인합니다.
In accordance with internal regulations, staff leave is approved.
조례에 의거하여 이 건물은 3층까지만 지을 수 있습니다.
Under the local ordinance, this building can only be built up to three floors.
훈령에 의거하여 모든 부서는 보고서를 제출합니다.
Under the directive, every department submits a report.
관련 규정에 의거하여 접수 기간은 이번 달 말까지입니다.
In accordance with the relevant regulations, the application period runs until the end of this month.
Based on the contract, the penalty is calculated.
cz: ___ 이 서류는 비공개로 합니다. (지침 + 에 의거하여)
In accordance with the guidelines, this document is kept confidential.
Under the public notice, fees go up from this month.

fk: 회원에 한하여 무료로 입장할 수 있습니다.
fe: Only members can enter for free.
xk: 범위를 하나로 줄일 때 써요. 'N만'이라는 뜻이고, 뒤에는 허락이나 지원이 와요. 공문에서 읽는 표현이에요.
xe: Use it to narrow the scope to one group. It means 'only N', and what follows is usually permission or support. It's an expression you read in official letters.
nk: 'N만'보다 딱딱하고 규칙처럼 들려요. '한하여' 하나로 제한이 끝나니까 '만'을 같이 쓰지 않아요. 말로 할 때는 'N만'이 자연스러워요.
ne: It sounds stiffer and more rule-like than N만. 한하여 alone sets the limit, so don't add 만 as well. In speech, N만 is more natural.
ex: 만 20세 이상에 한하여 신청할 수 있습니다.
Only those aged 20 or older may apply.
이번 달 구매 고객에 한하여 사은품을 드립니다.
Gifts are given only to customers who buy this month.
본인 확인이 가능한 경우에 한하여 서류를 발급합니다.
Documents are issued only when identity can be verified.
소규모 업체에 한하여 비용의 절반을 지원합니다.
Half the cost is supported only for small businesses.
산하 기관에 한하여 이 자료를 공개합니다.
This data is disclosed only to affiliated organizations.
cz: Only employees can use the parking lot.
신분증을 가져온 ___ 입장할 수 있습니다. (사람 + 한하다)
Only people who brought ID can enter.

fe: We made a request last month, and there is still no reply.
xk: 앞에 일어난 일을 말하고, 그 일을 근거로 뒤의 말을 이어요. 과거는 '-(으)ㄴ바', 현재는 '-는바'예요. 공문에서 읽는 표현이에요.
xe: It states a fact first, then continues with something based on it. Use -(으)ㄴ바 for the past and -는바 for the present. It's an expression you read in official letters.
nk: '-는데'와 비슷하지만 글에서만 써요. 뒤에 확인한 결과나 요청이 자주 와요. 이 카드의 '-(으)ㄴ바'는 앞말에 붙여 쓰는 연결어미예요. '요청한 바 있다', '밝힌 바 있다'의 '바'는 띄어 쓰는 의존명사라서 다른 쓰임이에요.
ne: It's like -는데 but used only in writing. A result you found or a request often follows. The -(으)ㄴ바 on this card is a connective ending written attached to the word before it. The '바' in '요청한 바 있다' or '밝힌 바 있다' is a dependent noun written with a space, which is a different use.
ex: 관련 규정을 확인한바 해당 사항이 없었습니다.
We checked the relevant regulations and found nothing applicable.
We inspected the site and found no safety problems.
자료를 검토한바 일부 숫자가 맞지 않았습니다.
We reviewed the materials and found some figures didn't match.
신청서를 접수한바 서류 두 장이 빠져 있었습니다.
We received the application and found two documents missing.
As we are preparing this year's event, we ask for your cooperation.
cz: We read the contract and found the dates were wrong.
We opened the box and found it empty.

fk: 중요한 회의이니만큼 서류를 꼭 준비해 주세요.
fe: Since it's an important meeting, please prepare the documents without fail.
xk: 앞 내용이 뒤의 판단이나 부탁의 근거가 될 때 써요. 명사에는 '이니만큼', 형용사에는 '-(으)니만큼', 과거는 '-았/었으니만큼'을 붙여요.
xe: Use it when the first part is the ground for the judgment or request that follows. Add 이니만큼 to nouns, -(으)니만큼 to adjectives, and -았/었으니만큼 for the past.
nk: '그 정도이니 마땅히 이렇게 해야 한다'는 느낌이에요. 뒤에는 부탁, 판단, 다짐이 자주 와요. 공문이나 안내문 같은 격식 있는 글에서 많이 써요. 단순한 이유만 말할 때는 '-기 때문에'가 더 자연스러워요.
ne: It means 'because it is this serious, it is natural to act this way.' A request, judgment, or resolve usually follows. It is common in formal writing such as official letters and notices. For a plain reason, -기 때문에 sounds more natural.
ex: 기한이 짧으니만큼 오늘 안에 보내야 합니다.
Since the deadline is short, we must send it today.
처음 하는 일이니만큼 실수하지 않도록 조심해요.
Since it's my first time doing this, I'm careful not to make mistakes.
Since it's cold out, please dress warmly before you go.
Since you prepared so hard, the result will be good.
아이들이 보는 프로그램이니만큼 말을 조심해야 해요.
Since children watch this program, we have to watch our words.
cz: Since the exam is close, I'm going to bed early today.
Since it's a big event, we prepare thoroughly.

fk: 솔직히 말씀드리면 예전에는 일을 혼자 끌어안는 편이었습니다.
fe: To be honest, I used to take on work all by myself.
xk: 어려운 이야기를 정직하게 시작할 때 써요. 문장 맨 앞에 두고, 듣는 사람을 높여서 말해요.
xe: Use it to start an honest answer to a hard question. Put it at the start of the sentence; it is respectful to the listener.
nk: 약점이나 실패를 인정할 때 써요. 친구에게는 '솔직히 말하면'을 써요. 이 말 뒤에는 숨기지 않고 사실을 말해야 해요.
ne: Used when admitting a weakness or failure. With friends, use 솔직히 말하면. What follows should be a plain fact, not an excuse.
ex: 솔직히 말씀드리면 그 일은 제게 아직 어렵습니다.
To be honest, that task is still hard for me.
솔직히 말씀드리면 첫 프로젝트에서 실수를 했습니다.
To be honest, I made a mistake in my first project.
To be honest, I was not well prepared at that time.
솔직히 말씀드리면 저는 발표가 미숙한 편입니다.
To be honest, I am not very skilled at presenting.
cz: 솔직히 ___ 저는 숫자를 확인하는 일이 서툴렀습니다. (말씀드리다)
To be honest, I was weak at checking numbers.
마감을 지키지 못한 적이 있다는 것을 ___ 말씀드리겠습니다. (솔직하다)
I will tell you honestly that there was a time I could not meet a deadline.

fk: 꼼꼼하기는 하지만 그 때문에 마감이 늦어진 적이 있습니다.
fe: I am thorough, but that has sometimes made me miss deadlines.
xk: 앞 내용을 인정하고, 뒤에서 다른 면을 말해요. 어간에 '-기는 하지만'을 붙여요.
xe: You accept the first part, then give the other side. Add -기는 하지만 to the stem.
nk: '-지만'보다 앞말을 한 번 인정해 주는 느낌이에요. 면접에서 장점을 말하고 약점을 이어 말할 때 좋아요. 뒤에는 약점이나 한계를 이어 말해요.
ne: Compared with -지만, it first grants the earlier point. Good in interviews for stating a strength and then a weakness. Follow with the weakness or limit.
ex: 일이 빠르기는 하지만 가끔 실수가 있습니다.
I work fast, but I sometimes make mistakes.
저는 의견을 말하기는 하지만 끝까지 설명하지 못합니다.
I do share my opinion, but I can't explain it to the end.
계획을 세우기는 하지만 확인이 늦을 때가 있습니다.
I do make plans, but my checking is sometimes late.
사람들과 일하기는 하지만 혼자 정하는 일이 많았습니다.
I do work with people, but I often decided things alone.
cz: I do collect materials, but I'm slow to organize them.
저는 친절하다는 말을 자주 ___ 거절을 잘 못합니다 (듣다 + -기는 하지만).
I do often hear that I'm kind, but I'm not good at saying no.

fe: I speak Korean as well as Minsu.
xk: 명사 뒤에 '만큼'을 붙여요. 앞 말과 뒤 말의 정도가 같다는 뜻이에요.
xe: Attach 만큼 after a noun. It means the degree is about the same as that noun.
nk: 'N처럼'은 모양이나 모습이 같을 때도 쓰지만, 'N만큼'은 정도·양이 같을 때 써요. 뒤에는 '잘하다, 넓다, 맛있다'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말이 와요. '만큼'은 명사에 붙여 써요.
ne: N처럼 can mean 'in the same way', but N만큼 stresses the same degree or amount. It is followed by words of degree such as 잘하다 or 넓다. 만큼 is attached directly to the noun.
ex: Today is not as cold as yesterday.
Seoyeon sings as well as a singer.
This room is as big as the living room.
The office is as close as home, so I walk.
저는 사라만큼 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.
I can't eat spicy food as well as Sara.
cz: This book is as thick as a dictionary.
저는 하준___ 많이 먹을 수 없어요. (하준 + 'as much as')
I can't eat as much as Hajun.

fk: 열심히 연습한 만큼 결과가 좋을 거예요.
fe: The results will be good in proportion to how hard you practiced.
xk: 앞 말의 정도에 맞게 뒤 말도 그렇다는 뜻이에요. 동사 과거는 '-(으)ㄴ 만큼', 현재는 '-는 만큼', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ 만큼'이에요. '만큼'은 띄어 써요.
xe: The second part matches the degree of the first. Verb past: -(으)ㄴ 만큼, present: -는 만큼, adjective: -(으)ㄴ 만큼. Write 만큼 as a separate word.
nk: '노력한 만큼 얻는다'처럼 양이나 정도가 서로 맞는다는 느낌이에요. 이유로도 읽혀서 '일이 많은 만큼 월급도 높다'처럼 써요. 단순한 원인 하나만 말할 때는 '-아/어서'가 더 자연스러워요.
ne: It feels like two amounts matching each other, as in 'you get what you put in'. It can also read as a reason: 'there is a lot of work, so the pay is high too'. For a plain single cause, -아/어서 is more natural.
ex: The pay is high in line with how much work there is.
You gain weight in proportion to how much you eat.
요리 실력이 좋은 만큼 손님도 많아요.
There are many customers in proportion to how good the cooking is.
You can get as much as you put in.
The child's shoes got too small in line with how much the child grew.
cz: The rent is expensive in proportion to how big the room is.
There are plenty of places to clean in proportion to the size of the house.

fe: Laughter is good for your health.
xk: 동사나 형용사 어간에 받침이 없으면 ㅁ, 있으면 음을 붙여서 명사를 만들어요. 웃다는 웃음이 돼요.
xe: Add ㅁ after a vowel or 음 after a consonant to a verb or adjective stem to make a noun. 웃다 becomes 웃음.
nk: 모든 말이 명사가 되지는 않아요. 기쁨, 슬픔, 꿈, 웃음처럼 자주 쓰는 말은 하나의 단어로 외워요. ㄹ 받침 말은 삶(살다)처럼 ㅁ만 붙는 말도 있고, 졸음(졸다)처럼 음이 붙는 말도 있어요.
ne: Not every verb or adjective can become a noun this way. Common ones like 기쁨, 슬픔, 꿈, 웃음 are learned as separate words. Some ㄹ-final stems take only ㅁ, as in 삶 (from 살다), while others take 음, as in 졸음 (from 졸다).
ex: The child felt joy after getting a present.
I feel great sadness because I said goodbye to my friend.
My dream is to be a teacher.
If drowsiness comes while you drive, take a rest.
That person's life was not easy.
My friend's trust meant a lot to me.
cz: The pain in my leg was bad, so I went to the hospital.

fe: I found out that he had told a lie.
xk: 문장 뒤에 ㅁ/음을 붙여서 '~는 것'이라는 뜻의 덩어리를 만들어요. 보통 목적어로 쓰니까 '했음을'처럼 조사 '을'을 붙여서 알다, 보다, 느끼다 같은 말과 함께 써요. 주어로 쓸 때는 '했음이'처럼 '이'를 붙여요.
xe: Attach ㅁ/음 to the end of a clause to make it mean 'the fact that...'. It is mostly used as an object, so add the particle 을 and use it with verbs like 알다, 보다, 느끼다, as in 했음을. As a subject, add 이, as in 했음이.
nk: 주로 글에서 써요. 과거는 앞에 -았/었-을 붙여 -았/었음을처럼 써요. 말할 때는 '-다는 것을'이나 '-는지'를 더 많이 써요.
ne: Mostly used in writing. For the past, put -았/었- before it, as in -았/었음을. In speech, people use '-다는 것을' or '-는지' more often.
ex: I learned later that my friend had been sick.
저는 이 일이 어려움을 알고 시작했어요.
I started this job knowing that it was hard.
I saw that the door was closed and came back.
I didn't know that Sujin had gone to school.
I admit that I was wrong.
cz: I didn't know that Hajun had already come.
I was surprised to learn that this room is wide.

fe: The library is closed today. (notice style)
xk: 공지, 메모, 기록에서 문장을 짧게 끝낼 때 어간에 ㅁ/음을 붙여요. '~해요' 대신 써요.
xe: In notices, memos, and records, add ㅁ/음 to the stem to end a sentence in short form, instead of '~해요'.
nk: 글에서만 써요. 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요. 과거는 -았/었음, '~이다'는 -임이 돼요.
ne: Only used in writing, never in speech. The past is -았/었음, and '~이다' becomes -임.
ex: 내일 오전 열 시에 모임이 있음.
There is a meeting at 10 a.m. tomorrow.
교실에 들어갈 때 신발을 벗어야 함.
You must take off your shoes when entering the classroom.
All the homework was handed in.
Lunch time is from 12 to 1 o'clock.
The game was cancelled because of rain.
cz: Memo: Bought two cartons of milk.
공지: 이 문은 밤 열 시에 ___. (닫히다)
Notice: This door closes at 10 p.m.

fe: I don't even need to watch that movie to know it's boring.
xk: 하든 안 하든 결과가 같을 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -(으)나 마나를 붙여요. 받침이 있으면 -으나 마나예요.
xe: Use it when the result is the same whether you do something or not. Add -(으)나 마나 to a verb stem. After a consonant, use -으나 마나.
nk: 결과가 뻔해서 해도 소용없다는 느낌이에요. 뒤에는 보통 안 좋은 일이나 뻔한 일이 와요. '-아/어 봤자'와 비슷하지만, 이 말은 '하든 안 하든'이라는 뜻이 더 강해요.
ne: It feels like 'the result is obvious, so it's pointless.' What follows is usually bad or predictable. Similar to '-아/어 봤자', but this one stresses 'whether you do it or not'.
ex: This medicine makes no difference whether I take it or not.
지금 그 가게에 가 보나 마나 문을 닫았을 거예요.
There's no point in going to that shop now; it will have closed.
회의 전에 메일을 보내나 마나 사장님이 안 읽어요.
Whether I send the email before the meeting or not, the boss doesn't read it.
Whether you use an umbrella or not, you get soaked.
그 학생은 물어보나 마나 숙제를 안 했을 거예요.
There's no need to ask; that student didn't do the homework.
cz: It's so hot in the room. It's the same whether I turn on the fan or not.
The road is jammed, so whether you leave now or not, you'll be late.

fk: 비가 오건 눈이 오건 저는 갈 거예요.
fe: Whether it rains or snows, I will go.
xk: 반대되거나 비슷한 두 말을 -건으로 이어서 '어느 쪽이든'이라는 뜻을 나타내요. 뒤에는 같은 결과나 행동이 와요.
xe: Join two opposite or similar words with -건 to mean 'either way.' The result or action that follows stays the same.
nk: '-든지 -든지'와 뜻이 같아요. -건은 조금 더 글 같고 단단한 느낌이에요. 뒤에는 '그래도 한다'는 말이 자주 와요.
ne: It means the same as '-든지 -든지'. -건 sounds a bit more written and firm. What follows is often 'I'll do it anyway.'
ex: 좋건 싫건 이 일은 해야 해요.
Whether you like it or not, you have to do this job.
싸건 비싸건 저는 이 가방을 살 거예요.
Cheap or expensive, I will buy this bag.
늦게 자건 일찍 자건 아침에는 일어나야 해요.
Whether you go to bed late or early, you have to get up in the morning.
공부를 잘하건 못하건 우리 반 친구는 모두 소중해요.
Whether they study well or not, every friend in my class is precious.
손님이 많건 적건 가게는 열 시에 열어요.
Whether there are many customers or few, the shop opens at ten.
cz: Whether the food is tasty or not, I eat it all.
차가 ___ 안 막히건 저는 지하철로 가요. (막히다)
Whether the traffic is jammed or not, I take the subway.

fk: 학생이건 선생님이건 이 규칙을 지켜야 해요.
fe: Whether you are a student or a teacher, you must follow this rule.
xk: 명사 두 개를 N(이)건 N(이)건으로 이어서 '무엇이든 같다'는 뜻을 나타내요. 받침이 있으면 -이건, 없으면 -건을 써요.
xe: Join two nouns as N(이)건 N(이)건 to mean 'it's the same either way.' After a consonant use -이건; after a vowel, the 이 drops and you use just -건, as in 커피건.
nk: 사람, 때, 장소를 나눠서 '모두 포함'이라고 말할 때 좋아요. '-든지 -든지'와 같은 뜻이에요. 뒤에는 같은 규칙이나 행동이 와요.
ne: Good for covering all people, times, or places. It means the same as '-든지 -든지'. The same rule or action follows.
ex: 낮이건 밤이건 이 거리는 사람이 많아요.
Day or night, this street is full of people.
Whether it's Korea or America, people love their families.
Coffee or tea, I like it as long as it's warm.
주말이건 평일이건 그 가게는 항상 열려 있어요.
Weekend or weekday, that shop is always open.
Whether it's a friend or family, you must keep your promises.
cz: I like reading, whether it's a book or a magazine.
Whether it's money or time, it's good to save.

fk: 그렇게 빨리 먹으면 체하는 수가 있어요.
fe: If you eat that fast, you might get indigestion.
xk: 동사 어간에 -는 수가 있다를 붙여요. 가끔 안 좋은 일이 생길 수 있으니 조심하라는 뜻이에요.
xe: Add -는 수가 있다 to a verb stem. It means a bad thing can happen sometimes, so be careful.
nk: '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다'보다 '조심해요'라는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 안 좋은 일에 써요. 좋은 일에는 잘 안 써요. 앞에 '-(으)면'이 자주 와요.
ne: It carries a stronger 'watch out' feeling than '-(으)ㄹ 수 있다'. It is usually for bad results and rarely for good ones. '-(으)면' often comes before it.
ex: The road is slippery, so you might fall.
약속에 자주 늦으면 친구를 잃는 수가 있어요.
If you are often late for appointments, you might lose a friend.
컴퓨터를 오래 쓰면 눈이 나빠지는 수가 있어요.
If you use a computer for a long time, your eyes might get worse.
회의 자료를 안 저장하면 파일이 사라지는 수가 있어요.
If you don't save the meeting materials, the file might disappear.
한 번에 많이 사면 돈이 모자라는 수가 있어요.
If you buy a lot at once, you might run short of money.
cz: 비 오는 날 빨리 달리면 차가 ___ 수가 있어요. (미끄러지다 + -는 수가 있다)
If you drive fast on a rainy day, the car might skid.
일이 많으면 약속을 ___ 수가 있어요. (잊다 + -는 수가 있다)
If you are busy, you might forget an appointment.

f: V 어간+(으)ㄹ 게 아니라 + 다른 행동
fk: 그냥 기다릴 게 아니라 직접 가 봐요.
fe: Instead of just waiting, let's go and see for ourselves.
xk: 앞 행동은 하지 말고 뒤 행동을 하자고 말할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 게 아니라'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to say 'don't do the first thing; do the second thing instead.' Add -(으)ㄹ 게 아니라 to a verb stem.
nk: 앞 행동이 맞지 않으니 뒤 행동이 더 낫다는 뜻이에요. 뒤에는 권유나 명령이 자주 와요. '-지 말고'와 비슷하지만 앞 행동이 틀렸다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
ne: It suggests the first action is not right and the second is better. A suggestion or command often follows. It is close to '-지 말고', but it feels more like the first action is a mistake.
ex: 혼자 고민할 게 아니라 친구에게 물어봐요.
Instead of worrying alone, ask a friend.
집에서 쉴 게 아니라 같이 운동하러 가요.
Instead of resting at home, let's go exercise together.
말로만 할 게 아니라 지금 시작해야 해요.
Instead of just talking, you have to start now.
가방을 새로 살 게 아니라 이 가방을 고쳐 써요.
Instead of buying a new bag, fix this one and use it.
회의에서 가만히 있을 게 아니라 의견도 말하세요.
Instead of sitting quietly in the meeting, share your opinion too.
cz: Instead of taking the bus, let's walk.
혼자 청소를 ___ 같이 해요. (하다 + -(으)ㄹ 게 아니라)
Instead of cleaning alone, let's do it together.

f: V 어간+는 한편, A 어간+(으)ㄴ 한편
fk: 지민은 학교에 다니는 한편 가게에서 일해요.
fe: Jimin goes to school and, at the same time, works at a shop.
xk: 한 사람이나 일에 두 가지 면이 있을 때 써요. 동사는 '-는 한편', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ 한편'이에요.
xe: Use it when one person or thing has two sides or does two things. Verbs take -는 한편; adjectives take -(으)ㄴ 한편.
nk: 두 일을 함께 하거나, 좋은 면과 나쁜 면을 같이 말할 때 써요. 주로 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 써요. '-는 반면에'는 두 면이 서로 반대일 때 더 잘 어울려요.
ne: It joins two things done together, or a good side and a bad side. It is mostly used in writing or formal speech. '-는 반면에' fits better when the two sides are clearly opposite.
ex: 이 가게는 값이 싼 한편 서비스도 좋아요.
This shop is cheap and the service is good too.
This job is fun, but it is also hard.
사라는 한국어를 배우는 한편 한국 요리도 만들어요.
Sarah studies Korean and also cooks Korean food.
The city is convenient, but it is also noisy.
마이크는 회사에서 일하는 한편 밤에 공부해요.
Mike works at a company and studies at night.
cz: 수진은 아침에 신문을 ___ 라디오도 들어요. (읽다 + -는 한편)
Sujin reads the newspaper in the morning and also listens to the radio.
This room is big, but it is also expensive.

fk: 날씨가 추워짐에 따라 사람들이 두꺼운 옷을 입어요.
fe: As the weather gets colder, people wear thick clothes.
xk: 앞의 일이 변하면 뒤의 일도 같이 변할 때 써요. 어간에 '-(으)ㅁ'을 붙이고 '에 따라'를 써요.
xe: Use it when one thing changes and another changes with it. Add -(으)ㅁ to the stem, then 에 따라.
nk: 변화나 움직임을 나타내는 말과 같이 써요. 뒤 문장도 변화를 말해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요. '-(으)ㄹ수록'은 정도가 점점 커질 때 써요.
ne: It goes with words of change or movement, and the second clause also describes a change. It is common in writing and news. -(으)ㄹ수록 is for something that keeps growing in degree.
ex: As people get older, health becomes more important.
학생 수가 줄어듦에 따라 학교가 문을 닫아요.
As the number of students drops, the school closes.
As the internet developed, life became easier.
한국어 실력이 늘어남에 따라 말하기가 쉬워졌어요.
As my Korean improved, speaking became easier.
cz: As prices rise, life gets harder.
As cars increase, the roads get jammed.

fk: 운동도 할 겸 해서 걸어서 가요.
fe: I'll walk there, partly to get some exercise too.
xk: 주된 목적 말고 다른 목적도 하나 더 있을 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 겸 해서'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it when you have one more purpose besides the main one. Add -(으)ㄹ 겸 해서 to a verb stem.
nk: '도'와 같이 써서 '이것도 하고 저것도 하려고'라는 뜻이 돼요. 목적이 가볍고 편한 느낌이에요. 꼭 해야 하는 일에는 잘 안 써요. '-기 위해서'는 더 격식 있고 목적이 분명한 느낌이에요.
ne: With 도, it means 'to do this and that as well.' The purpose feels light and casual. It is not used for things you must do. -기 위해서 is more formal and states the purpose more clearly.
ex: 친구도 만날 겸 해서 시내에 나왔어요.
I came downtown partly to meet a friend too.
책도 살 겸 해서 서점에 가요.
I'm going to the bookstore, partly to buy a book too.
바람도 쐴 겸 해서 공원에 갔어요.
I went to the park, partly to get some fresh air.
점심도 먹을 겸 해서 회사 앞에서 만났어요.
We met in front of the office, partly to have lunch too.
부모님도 뵐 겸 해서 고향에 내려가요.
I'm going down to my hometown, partly to see my parents too.
cz: I'm going to the cafe, partly to drink coffee too.
I take a walk, partly to clear my head too.

fe: It looks like it might rain, but it hasn't started yet.
xk: 어떤 일이 될 듯 말 듯 아슬아슬할 때 써요. 받침이 없으면 '-ㄹ락 말락', 받침이 있으면 '-을락 말락'을 붙여요.
xe: Use it when something is on the edge of happening but not quite. Add -ㄹ락 말락 after a vowel, -을락 말락 after a final consonant.
nk: 일이 지금 막 시작될 것 같지만 아직 아니에요. 눈앞의 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 뻔하다'는 거의 일어날 뻔했지만 안 일어난 지난 일이에요. 이 문형은 지금 그 순간의 아슬아슬함이에요.
ne: The thing seems about to happen, but hasn't yet. It describes what you see right now. -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 is about a past event that almost happened but didn't; this one is about the on-the-edge moment itself.
ex: The child is almost falling asleep.
손이 높은 선반에 닿을락 말락 해요.
My hand can barely reach the high shelf.
꽃이 필락 말락 해서 매일 공원에 가요.
The flowers are about to bloom, so I go to the park every day.
회의 중에 하품이 나올락 말락 했어요.
During the meeting, a yawn almost came out, but didn't quite.
밤에 먼 곳에서 노랫소리가 들릴락 말락 해요.
At night, a song from far away is just barely audible.
cz: The cup is teetering on the edge of the table, about to fall.
The laundry is almost dry, but not quite.

fk: 그 돈은 잃어버린 셈 치고 잊을게요.
fe: I'll treat that money as lost and forget about it.
xk: 실제는 아니지만 '이미 그렇게 됐다'고 생각할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄴ 셈 치다를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to think of something as already done, even though it isn't really. Attach -(으)ㄴ 셈 치다 to a verb stem.
nk: 손해나 아쉬운 일을 마음 편하게 받아들일 때 자주 써요. '-(으)ㄴ 셈이에요'는 사실을 설명하는 말이고, '셈 치다'는 내가 그렇게 생각하기로 한다는 말이에요. 보통 뒤에 '잊다', '쉬다' 같은 행동이 와요.
ne: Often used to accept a loss or disappointment calmly. -(으)ㄴ 셈이다 describes how things amount to something; 셈 치다 means you choose to think of it that way. A decision or action usually follows.
ex: 이번 시험은 연습한 셈 치고 다음에 더 열심히 할게요.
I'll count this test as practice and work harder next time.
안 입는 옷은 친구에게 준 셈 치고 정리해요.
I'll think of my unworn clothes as given to a friend and sort them out.
일이 남았지만 오늘은 다 한 셈 치고 쉴게요.
There's work left, but I'll treat today's work as done and rest.
비가 와서 못 나갔지만 하루 푹 쉰 셈 치기로 했어요.
I couldn't go out in the rain, so I decided to count it as a day of good rest.
동생이 쓴 돈은 용돈을 준 셈 칠게요.
I'll treat the money my brother spent as pocket money I gave him.
cz: 버스를 놓쳐서 걸어요. 운동을 ___ (하다 + 셈 치다).
I missed the bus, so I'm walking. I'll count it as exercise.
휴가를 못 갔어요. 집에서 ___ (여행하다 + 셈 치다).
I couldn't go on vacation. I'll pretend staying home is a trip.

fk: 속는 셈 치고 한번 먹어 봐요.
fe: Pretend you're being fooled and just try it once.
xk: '그렇다고 생각하고' 뒤의 일을 해 보자고 말할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -는 셈 치고를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to say "think of it as X and go ahead." Attach -는 셈 치고 to a verb stem.
nk: 상대에게 부담 없이 해 보라고 권할 때 많이 써요. 뒤에는 '해 보세요', '같이 가요' 같은 말이 자주 와요. 하기 싫거나 망설이는 사람에게 쓰기 좋아요.
ne: Good for gently urging someone who is hesitant to just try. It is often followed by a suggestion like 해 보세요 or 같이 가요.
ex: 놀러 가는 셈 치고 같이 가요.
Think of it as an outing and come along.
친구한테 말하는 셈 치고 편하게 이야기해 보세요.
Pretend you're talking to a friend and speak comfortably.
산책하는 셈 치고 한 정거장 걸어요.
Let's walk one stop and call it a stroll.
공짜로 받는 셈 치고 이 가방을 가져가세요.
Think of it as free and take this bag.
휴가를 쓰는 셈 치고 오늘은 일찍 퇴근해요.
I'll pretend I'm taking a day off and leave work early today.
cz: 저를 ___ 한 번만 해 보세요. (믿다 + 셈 치다)
Just trust me and give it a try once.
피곤하지만 저를 ___ 같이 가 줘요. (돕다 + 셈 치다)
I know you're tired, but think of it as helping me and come along.

fe: I started my homework and stopped halfway.
xk: 일을 시작했지만 끝내지 않고 중간에 그만둘 때 써요. 동사 어간에 -다 말다를 붙여요.
xe: Use it when you start something and quit partway without finishing. Attach -다 말다 to a verb stem.
nk: 끝까지 하지 못했다는 아쉬움이 있어요. 이유는 보통 앞이나 뒤에 말해요. 'V-다가'는 다른 일로 바뀐다는 뜻이고, '-다 말다'는 그냥 멈춘다는 뜻이 강해요.
ne: It carries a sense of not having finished. The reason is usually given before or after. V-다가 focuses on switching to something else; -다 말다 stresses that you simply stopped.
ex: The movie was boring, so I stopped watching halfway.
The food was too spicy, so I stopped eating halfway.
I stopped writing the email halfway, but I'll finish it tomorrow.
My throat hurt, so I stopped singing halfway.
길이 너무 멀어서 산에 오르다 말았어요.
The trail was too long, so I gave up climbing partway.
cz: I was so sleepy that I stopped folding the laundry halfway.
The test questions were too hard, so I quit solving them partway.

use: 하던 일을 두고 다른 일 하기
fe: I woke up in the middle of sleeping and drank some water.
xk: 하던 일을 중간에 그만두고 다른 일을 할 때 써요. '-다 말고' 뒤에 새로 한 일을 말해요.
xe: Use it when you drop what you were doing and do something else. The new action comes after -다 말고.
nk: 갑자기 다른 일이 생겼을 때 자주 써요. 앞의 일은 끝나지 않았고, 뒤의 일이 더 급하거나 갑작스러워요. 뒤에는 보통 과거나 현재 행동이 와요.
ne: Often used when something suddenly comes up. The first action is left unfinished and the second feels more urgent or sudden. A concrete action follows.
ex: 회의 중에 이야기를 듣다 말고 전화를 받으러 나갔어요.
I left the meeting halfway through listening to take a phone call.
The child stopped playing and ran to his mother.
손님이 물건을 고르다 말고 그냥 나갔어요.
The customer stopped picking things out and just walked out.
I stopped walking and looked up at the sky.
My friend stopped in the middle of talking and suddenly laughed.
cz: I stopped reading my book halfway and opened the window.
I stopped cooking halfway and went to the store.

use: 나쁜 일은 감수해도 그 일은 절대 안 한다고 말하기
fe: I may go hungry, but I won't tell a lie.
xk: 앞의 나쁜 일은 받아들이지만, 뒤에는 하지 않겠다는 뜻이나 반대되는 내용이 와요. 받침이 있으면 '-을지언정', 없으면 '-ㄹ지언정'이에요. 명사에는 'N일지언정'을 써요.
xe: Use it to accept a bad situation in the first part, but firmly refuse something in the second. Use -을지언정 after a final consonant, -ㄹ지언정 after a vowel, and N일지언정 with nouns.
nk: 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 강한 뜻을 낼 때 써요. 뒤에는 보통 '않다', '안 하다'처럼 하지 않겠다는 말이 와요. '-(으)ㄹ지라도'는 그냥 '그래도'라는 뜻이라 더 가볍고 뒤 내용에 제한이 없어요. 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 써요.
ne: It sounds strong and fairly formal or written. The second part usually states a refusal, like 않다 or 안 하다. -(으)ㄹ지라도 just means "even if" and is lighter, with no limit on what follows. It is rare in everyday talk.
ex: 차라리 늦을지언정 위험한 길로는 가지 않을 거예요.
I'd rather be late than take the dangerous road.
My body may be tired, but my mind is at ease.
It may be a small shop, but it is always kind to customers.
시간이 오래 걸릴지언정 이 일은 제가 끝낼 거예요.
Even if it takes a long time, I will finish this work myself.
비를 맞을지언정 남의 우산은 쓰지 않아요.
I may get wet in the rain, but I don't use other people's umbrellas.
cz: My feet may hurt, but I'll walk to the end.
I may have no money, but I will keep my promise.

use: 상태가 너무 심해서 거의 ~할 정도라고 말하기
fe: I'm so hungry I'm about to collapse.
xk: 상태가 아주 심해서 거의 그렇게 될 정도라는 뜻이에요. 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 지경이다'를 붙여요. 앞에 '-아/어서'로 이유를 자주 말해요.
xe: Means a state is so extreme that you are close to doing or being something. Add -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 to the stem. It often comes after a reason with -아/어서.
nk: 정말로 그렇게 되었다는 뜻이 아니라, 상태가 아주 심하다는 것을 강조해요. 보통 힘들거나 나쁜 상태에 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 뻔하다'는 거의 일어날 뻔한 일이고, '-(으)ㄹ 지경이다'는 지금의 심한 상태예요.
ne: It does not mean the thing really happens. It stresses how extreme the state is, mostly a hard or bad one. -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 is about something that almost happened; -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 is about how bad things are right now.
ex: 요즘 일이 너무 많아서 죽을 지경이에요.
I have so much work lately that I'm about to die.
시험 결과가 궁금해서 잠을 못 잘 지경이었어요.
I was so curious about the test result that I could hardly sleep.
It's so funny that I'm about to cry from laughing.
In summer it's so hot that I can hardly breathe.
The road is jammed, and I'm about to be late for my appointment.
cz: It's so cold that my hands are about to freeze.
큰 소리에 너무 놀라서 심장이 ___ (멈추다 + -(으)ㄹ 지경이다)
I was so shocked by the loud noise that my heart was about to stop.

use: 증거를 보고 분명히 그렇다고 강하게 추측하기
fk: 불이 켜져 있으니까 지우는 집에 있음에 틀림없어요.
fe: The light is on, so Jiwoo must be at home.
xk: 증거를 보고 '분명히 그렇다'고 강하게 말할 때 써요. 어간에 -(으)ㅁ을 붙이고 '에 틀림없다'를 써요. 과거는 '-았/었음에', 명사는 'N임에'예요.
xe: Use it to say 'it is certainly so' based on evidence. Add -(으)ㅁ to the stem, then 에 틀림없다. Past is -았/었음에; for nouns, N임에.
nk: 그렇게 믿는 마음이 아주 강해요. 글이나 격식 있는 말에 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '-것 같다'나 '-나 보다'를 더 많이 써요. '-것 같다'보다 확신이 훨씬 강해요.
ne: Your belief is very strong. It fits writing and formal speech. In daily talk, people use -것 같다 or -나 보다 more. It shows much more certainty than -것 같다.
ex: 이 그림은 유명한 화가가 그렸음에 틀림없습니다.
This painting must have been painted by a famous artist.
길이 많이 막혀요. 사고가 났음에 틀림없어요.
The road is very jammed. There must have been an accident.
이 가게는 맛집임에 틀림없어요. 사람이 아주 많아요.
This shop must be a great place to eat. There are so many people.
서연이는 시험공부를 열심히 했음에 틀림없다. 점수가 아주 좋았다.
Seoyeon must have studied hard for the test. Her score was very good.
아이가 방에서 울고 있어요. 장난감이 망가졌음에 틀림없어요.
The child is crying in the room. The toy must be broken.
cz: 마이크가 계속 기침을 해요. 감기에 ___ (걸리다 + -(으)ㅁ에 틀림없다)
Mike keeps coughing. He must have caught a cold.
문이 열려 있어요. 누가 방에 ___ (들어오다 + -(으)ㅁ에 틀림없다)
The door is open. Someone must have come into the room.

use: 나쁜 일은 인정해도 뒤의 일은 꼭 한다고 말하기
fe: I may collapse, but I won't give up.
xk: 앞의 나쁜 일을 인정해도, 뒤에서는 그와 반대로 말하거나 더 중요한 것을 말할 때 써요. 어간에 바로 '-(으)ㄹ망정'을 붙여요.
xe: You accept a bad thing in the first part, but the second part goes against it or names something more important. Attach -(으)ㄹ망정 right to the stem.
nk: '나쁜 일이 있어도 이것만은 한다'는 단단한 마음을 보여 줘요. 뒤에 '-(으)ㄹ 거예요' 같은 의지의 말이 자주 와요. 글말 느낌이 있어요. '-(으)ㄹ지라도'와 비슷한데, 더 강하고 극단적인 예를 들어요.
ne: It shows a firm will: 'even if the worst happens, I will still do this.' Words of will like -(으)ㄹ 거예요 often follow. It feels written. It is close to -(으)ㄹ지라도, but it usually gives a stronger, more extreme example.
ex: My body may be tired, but my heart is at ease.
비가 올망정 우리는 약속을 지킬 거예요.
Even if it rains, we will keep our promise.
하준이는 가난할망정 남에게 도움을 부탁하지 않았어요.
Hajun was poor, but he never asked others for help.
회사에서 늦게까지 일할망정 가족과 저녁은 꼭 먹어요.
I may work late at the office, but I always have dinner with my family.
집이 작을망정 우리 가족에게는 가장 따뜻한 곳이에요.
Our house may be small, but it is the warmest place for our family.
cz: The road may be far, but I will walk to the end.
돈이 ___ 친구 선물은 좋은 것으로 살 거예요. (없다 + -(으)ㄹ망정)
I may have no money, but I'll buy a good gift for my friend.

use: 그 일이 있어서 다행이고, 없었으면 나쁜 일이 생길 뻔했다고 말하기
fk: 우산을 가져왔기에 망정이지 비를 다 맞을 뻔했어요.
fe: Thank goodness I brought my umbrella, or I would have gotten soaked.
xk: 좋은 일이 있어서 다행이라는 뜻이에요. 그 일이 없었다면 나쁜 일이 생길 뻔했다고 말해요. 보통 '-았/었기에 망정이지' 뒤에 '-(으)ㄹ 뻔했다'를 써요.
xe: It means 'it's lucky that this good thing happened.' Without it, something bad would have happened. Usually -았/었기에 망정이지 is followed by -(으)ㄹ 뻔했다.
nk: 앞은 실제로 있었던 좋은 일이고, 뒤는 일어나지 않은 나쁜 결과예요. 안심하는 마음이 들어 있어요. '-덕분에'는 고마움만 말하지만, 이 문형은 '안 그랬으면 큰일'이라는 뜻이 더 강해요.
ne: The first part is a good thing that really happened; the second part is a bad result that did not happen. It carries a feeling of relief. -덕분에 only says thanks, but this pattern stresses 'otherwise it would have been bad.'
ex: 친구가 도와줬기에 망정이지 숙제를 못 끝낼 뻔했어요.
Thank goodness my friend helped me, or I couldn't have finished my homework.
일찍 일어났기에 망정이지 기차를 놓칠 뻔했어요.
Thank goodness I got up early, or I would have missed the train.
지갑을 찾았기에 망정이지 오늘 집에 못 갈 뻔했어요.
Thank goodness I found my wallet, or I couldn't have gone home today.
택시가 빨리 왔기에 망정이지 회의에 늦을 뻔했습니다.
Thank goodness the taxi came quickly, or I would have been late for the meeting.
의사 선생님이 계셨기에 망정이지 큰일 날 뻔했어요.
Thank goodness the doctor was there, or it could have been serious.
cz: Thank goodness I set the alarm, or I would have been late for school.
사라가 이 동네를 ___ 우리는 길을 잃을 뻔했어요. (알다 + -기에 망정이지)
Thank goodness Sarah knew this area, or we would have gotten lost.

use: 이왕 할 거라면 더 좋게 하라고 권하기
fe: If you're going to go anyway, go early.
xk: '어떤 일을 할 마음이 있으면'이라는 뜻이에요. 동사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 양이면'을 붙여요. 받침이 없으면 '-ㄹ 양이면', 있으면 '-을 양이면'이에요.
xe: It means 'if you have decided to do something'. Attach it to a verb stem: '-ㄹ 양이면' after a vowel, '-을 양이면' after a consonant.
nk: 뒤에는 보통 '더 좋게 하세요' 같은 권유나 제안이 와요. 그냥 조건을 말하는 '-(으)면'과 달라요. 이미 하기로 한 일에 '이왕 할 거라면'이라는 느낌이 있어요. '-(으)려면'은 목적을 이루는 방법을 말하고, '-(으)ㄹ 양이면'은 하기로 한 일을 더 잘하라고 권해요.
ne: The clause after it is usually advice or a suggestion, like 'do it well'. Plain '-(으)면' only states a condition. '-(으)ㄹ 양이면' has the feeling of 'since you are going to do it anyway'. '-(으)려면' tells the way to reach a goal, while '-(으)ㄹ 양이면' urges you to do a thing you already decided on even better.
ex: If you're going to buy shoes, buy good ones.
If you're going to exercise, you have to do it every day.
여행을 떠날 양이면 한 달 동안 다녀오세요.
If you're going to travel, go for a whole month.
If you're going to study, do it in a quiet library.
If we're going to meet, let's meet early and talk.
cz: 집에서 ___ 아무 일도 하지 마세요. (쉬다 + -(으)ㄹ 양이면)
If you're going to rest at home, don't do any work.
If you're going to learn dance, do it properly.

fk: 이 김치는 너무 매워서 눈물이 날 정도예요.
fe: This kimchi is so spicy that I almost cry.
xk: 어떤 일이 얼마나 심한지 보여 줘요. 동사나 형용사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 정도이다'를 붙여요. 문장 가운데에서는 '-(으)ㄹ 정도로'를 써요.
xe: It shows how extreme something is. Attach '-(으)ㄹ 정도이다' to a verb or adjective stem. In the middle of a sentence, use '-(으)ㄹ 정도로'.
nk: 실제로 그런 일이 생기지는 않아도 그만큼 심하다는 말이에요. 앞에는 눈물이 나다, 잠이 오다처럼 눈에 보이는 모습을 많이 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 만큼'과 비슷하지만 '정도이다'는 문장을 끝낼 수 있어요.
ne: It does not mean the thing really happens. It means the state is that extreme. Visible results like crying or falling asleep are common before it. It is close to '-(으)ㄹ 만큼', but '정도이다' can end a sentence.
ex: Today it is so hot that it is hard to breathe.
그 영화는 친구들이 모두 울 정도로 슬퍼요.
That movie is so sad that all my friends cry.
요즘 너무 바빠서 밥 먹을 시간도 없을 정도예요.
I'm so busy these days that I don't even have time to eat.
민수는 한국어를 한국 사람처럼 말할 정도예요.
Minsu speaks Korean to the point of sounding like a Korean person.
가게 앞에 줄이 길어서 한 시간 기다릴 정도예요.
The line in front of the shop is so long that you'd wait an hour.
cz: I'm so sleepy that I could fall asleep right now.
짐이 너무 많아서 이사하는 데 하루가 ___. (걸리다)
There is so much stuff that moving takes a whole day.

fk: 그 가수는 깜짝 놀랄 만큼 노래를 잘해요.
fe: That singer sings so well it's astonishing.
xk: 뒤에 오는 말이 얼마나 심한지 말해요. 동사나 형용사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 만큼'을 붙여요. '~할 정도로'와 비슷해요.
xe: It tells how extreme the following state is. Attach '-(으)ㄹ 만큼' to a verb or adjective stem. It is close to '~할 정도로' (to the degree that).
nk: 앞말은 뒷말의 기준이 돼요. '놀랄 만큼 예뻐요'는 놀랄 정도로 예쁘다는 뜻이에요. 문장을 이 말로 끝내지 않고 뒤에 꼭 다른 말이 와요.
ne: The first part is the measure for the second part. '놀랄 만큼 예뻐요' means 'pretty enough to surprise you'. The sentence does not end with it; another clause always follows.
ex: The sky is so clear it dazzles the eyes.
동생은 말을 못 할 만큼 피곤해 보여요.
My younger brother looks so tired he can't even speak.
이 사과는 누구나 좋아할 만큼 맛있어요.
These apples are tasty enough for anyone to like.
그 책은 밤을 새울 만큼 재미있어요.
That book is so fun that you'd stay up all night.
cz: Sara is so pretty that everyone envies her.
그 영화는 한 번 더 보고 ___ 재미있어요. (싶다)
That movie is so fun that I want to watch it once more.

fe: Put only as much on your plate as you will eat.
xk: '그 양만큼'이라는 뜻이에요. 동사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 만큼'을 붙여서 양을 말해요. '만큼만'은 '그만큼만'이라는 뜻이에요.
xe: It means 'as much as that'. Attach '-(으)ㄹ 만큼' to a verb stem to state an amount. '만큼만' means 'only that much'.
nk: 자기가 쓰거나 먹을 양을 정할 때 써요. '필요한 만큼'처럼 형용사 뒤에는 '-(으)ㄴ 만큼'을 써요. 이 카드의 '-(으)ㄹ 만큼'은 동사 뒤에 와요.
ne: Use it to set the amount you will use or eat. After an adjective such as '필요하다', the form is '-(으)ㄴ 만큼'. This card's '-(으)ㄹ 만큼' follows a verb.
ex: Pour water into the cup as much as you will drink.
Take only as much money as you will pay.
도서관에서 읽을 만큼 책을 빌려 가요.
I borrow as many books as I can read from the library.
Pick out only as many clothes as you will wear.
cz: There is a lot of paper, so take as much as you will use.
Please pour milk as much as the child will drink.

fk: 민수가 그 일을 모를 리가 없어요.
fe: There's no way Minsu doesn't know about that.
xk: '절대로 그럴 수 없다'고 강하게 말할 때 써요. 동사나 형용사 어간에 '-(으)ㄹ 리(가) 없다'를 붙여요. 과거는 '-았/었을 리가 없다'예요.
xe: Use it to say strongly 'that can't possibly be true'. Attach '-(으)ㄹ 리(가) 없다' to a verb or adjective stem. For the past, use '-았/었을 리가 없다'.
nk: 말하는 사람의 생각이에요. 이유가 있어서 아니라고 믿을 때 써요. 약한 추측 '-ㄹ 것 같다'보다 훨씬 강해요.
ne: It is the speaker's own strong belief, based on a reason. It is much stronger than a weak guess such as '-ㄹ 것 같다'.
ex: 이렇게 맛있는 집이 인기가 없을 리가 없어요.
There's no way such a tasty restaurant isn't popular.
There's no way Seoyeon would tell a lie.
오늘은 일요일이라서 회사에 사람이 있을 리가 없어요.
It's Sunday, so there's no way anyone is at the office.
지금 출발했으니까 벌써 도착했을 리가 없어요.
He left just now, so there's no way he has arrived already.
선생님이 쉽다고 했으니까 이 문제가 어려울 리 없어요.
The teacher said it's easy, so this problem can't be hard.
cz: Jiwoo went to bed early yesterday, so there's no way he's tired now.
저 식당은 항상 사람이 많은데 음식이 ___. (나쁘다)
That restaurant is always crowded, so there's no way the food is bad.

fk: 손님이 오기 전에 청소를 해 놓았어요.
fe: I cleaned up ahead of time, before the guests came.
xk: 어떤 일을 끝내 두고 그 결과를 남길 때 써요. 앞으로 쓰려고 미리 하는 일에 많이 써요. 동사 어간에 -아/어를 붙이고 '놓다'를 써요.
xe: Use it when you finish something and leave the result in place. It often means doing a task ahead of time. Add -아/어 to the verb stem, then 놓다.
nk: 뒤에 쓸 일이 있어서 미리 해 둘 때 자연스러워요. 'V-아/어 두다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 그냥 지금 한 일만 말할 때는 'V-았/었어요'를 써요.
ne: It fits when you do something now because you will need the result later. It means almost the same as V-아/어 두다. If you only report a finished action, use plain V-았/었어요.
ex: I've already done the grocery shopping for dinner.
I'll print the materials before the meeting.
내일 시험이라서 오늘 단어를 외워 놓았어요.
The test is tomorrow, so I memorized the words in advance.
아이가 배고플 텐데 간식을 만들어 놓았어요.
The kid is probably hungry, so I made a snack ahead of time.
내일 발표가 있어서 자료를 다 끝내 놓았어요.
I have a presentation tomorrow, so I finished all the materials ahead of time.
cz: 비가 올 것 같아서 우산을 ___ (챙기다, 놓다).
It looks like rain, so I got an umbrella ready.
친구가 오면 같이 먹을 거예요. 그래서 케이크를 ___ (사다, 놓다).
A friend will come and we will eat together, so I bought a cake ahead of time.

fe: It was hot, so I left the window open.
xk: 어떤 일을 하고, 그 모양을 그대로 둘 때 써요. 일을 한 뒤에 그 상태가 계속 남아 있어요.
xe: Use it when you do something and leave things in that state. The result of the action stays after it is done.
nk: '열려 있어요'는 상태만 말해요. '열어 놓았어요'는 사람이 한 일과 그 뒤의 상태를 함께 말해요. 상태가 남지 않는 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: '열려 있어요' only describes the state. '열어 놓았어요' says a person did it and the state remains. Don't use it for actions that leave nothing behind.
ex: I fell asleep with the light on.
집에 아무도 없어서 문을 잠가 놓았어요.
No one was home, so I locked the door and left it locked.
I wrote the date on the board and left it there.
I put the bag on the chair and left it there.
라면 물을 끓여 놓고 전화를 받았어요.
I set the ramen water to boil and answered the phone.
cz: 비가 와서 빨래를 방 안에 ___ (널다, 놓다).
It rained, so I hung the laundry up inside the room and left it.
The child is sleeping, so I turned the TV off and left it off.

f: V 어간+ㄴ다니까(요) / 받침 있는 V 어간+는다니까(요)
fe: I'm telling you, Minsu is really coming.
xk: 내 말을 다시 말하면서 '정말이에요' 하고 힘을 줄 때 써요. 동사에는 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ다니까요, 있으면 -는다니까요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to repeat what you said and press the point: 'it's true, believe me.' For verbs, add -ㄴ다니까요 after a vowel and -는다니까요 after a consonant.
nk: 상대가 믿지 않거나 못 들었을 때 써요. 말이 조금 세요. '-잖아요'는 '알고 있지요?'이고, '-다니까요'는 '내 말을 믿으세요'예요.
ne: Use it when the listener doesn't believe you or didn't hear you. It sounds a bit strong. -잖아요 means 'you know that, right?'; -다니까요 means 'trust what I say.'
ex: I really can eat spicy food well, I'm telling you.
My younger brother is doing his homework right now, I told you.
이 가게는 매일 아침에 빵을 굽는다니까요.
This shop bakes bread every morning, I'm telling you.
My child really does go to bed early every evening.
The boss will call in person, I'm telling you.
cz: I'm telling you, Jiwoo reads books at the library every day.
I'm telling you, I'm putting the key in the bag right now.

fe: I'm telling you, this kimchi stew is really good.
xk: 형용사에는 -다니까요를 붙여요. 명사에는 받침이 없으면 -라니까요, 있으면 -이라니까요를 붙여요. 내 말을 믿으라고 힘줘서 말할 때 써요.
xe: Add -다니까요 to adjectives. For nouns, use -라니까요 after a vowel and -이라니까요 after a consonant. It stresses that you mean what you say.
nk: 상대가 의심하거나 틀리게 알고 있을 때 써요. 같은 말을 다시 하는 느낌이라 조금 세게 들려요. 윗사람에게는 조심해서 써요.
ne: Use it when the other person doubts you or has it wrong. Because you repeat yourself, it can sound strong. Be careful with people older than you.
ex: It's really cold today, I'm telling you.
That person is my younger sibling, I'm telling you.
This bag isn't expensive at all, really.
This is our school, I'm telling you.
The person I mentioned earlier is a doctor, I told you.
cz: This movie is really fun, I'm telling you.
That person is my teacher, I'm telling you.

fe: Eat quickly, I said.
xk: '-(으)라고 했어요'의 힘준 말이에요. 같은 말을 다시 하면서 '내 말대로 해요' 하고 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -라니까요, 있으면 -으라니까요를 써요.
xe: It is a stronger form of 'I said to do it.' You repeat an instruction and say 'do as I told you.' Use -라니까요 after a vowel and -으라니까요 after a consonant.
nk: 여러 번 말했는데 상대가 안 할 때 써요. 답답하거나 짜증 난 마음이 들어가요. 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
ne: Use it when you've said it several times and the person still doesn't act. It carries impatience or annoyance. Better not to use it with people older than you.
ex: Do your homework first, I said.
Rest at home today, I said.
Ask the price at the shop first, I said.
Go to bed early, I said.
cz: If you're sick, go to the hospital quickly, I said.
It's raining, so use an umbrella, I said.

f: V 어간+ㄴ다죠 / 받침 있는 V 어간+는다죠
fe: I heard it's going to rain from tomorrow, right?
xk: 다른 사람에게 들은 말을 다시 확인할 때 써요. '-ㄴ다고 하죠'를 줄인 말이에요. 받침이 없는 동사는 -ㄴ다죠, 있는 동사는 -는다죠예요.
xe: Use it to check something you heard from others. It is a short form of '-ㄴ다고 하죠.' Use -ㄴ다죠 after a vowel and -는다죠 after a consonant.
nk: 들은 내용이 맞는지 가볍게 물을 때 써요. '-다면서요?'와 비슷한데 조금 더 부드러워요. 내가 직접 본 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: Use it to lightly ask whether what you heard is true. It is like -다면서요 but a little softer. Don't use it for things you saw yourself.
ex: I heard Minsu is moving next month, right?
I hear people line up at this restaurant on weekends, right?
I hear Hajun swims every morning, right?
I heard the new employee starts work on Monday, right?
I hear Yuna listens to a lot of Korean songs, right?
cz: I heard that shop closes on Sundays, right?
I heard Jiwoo is going to Busan this weekend, right?

fe: I heard that mountain is very high, right?
xk: 들은 말을 확인할 때 써요. 형용사에는 -다죠를 붙여요. 명사에는 받침이 없으면 -라죠, 있으면 -이라죠를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to check what you heard. Add -다죠 to adjectives. For nouns, add -라죠 after a vowel and -이라죠 after a consonant.
nk: 소문이나 남에게 들은 설명을 가볍게 확인해요. 말하는 사람은 그 내용을 직접 확인하지 않았어요. '-죠?'만 쓰면 내가 아는 일을 묻는 느낌이에요.
ne: It gently checks a rumor or something someone told you. The speaker hasn't confirmed it personally. Plain -죠? feels like asking about something you know yourself.
ex: I hear the sea in Jeju is very pretty, right?
I heard this movie is sad, right?
I hear Seoyeon's husband is a doctor, right?
I hear the new phone is expensive, right?
I hear Mike is American, right?
cz: I heard the exam is very hard these days, right?
I hear that person is the new teacher, right?

fe: The boss said to come early tomorrow, right?
xk: 다른 사람이 시킨 일을 다시 확인할 때 써요. '-(으)라고 하죠'를 줄인 말이에요. 받침이 없으면 -라죠, 있으면 -으라죠를 써요.
xe: Use it to check an instruction someone gave. It is a short form of '-(으)라고 하죠.' Use -라죠 after a vowel and -으라죠 after a consonant.
nk: 남이 한 지시를 내가 제대로 들었는지 확인해요. 앞에 '누가' 시켰는지 말하면 뜻이 분명해요. 내가 직접 시킬 때는 '-(으)세요'를 써요.
ne: You check that you heard someone else's instruction correctly. Naming who gave it makes the meaning clear. To give the instruction yourself, use -(으)세요.
ex: The teacher said to hand in the homework by tomorrow, right?
의사가 약을 하루에 세 번 먹으라죠?
The doctor said to take the medicine three times a day, right?
Mom said to go to bed early today, right?
The announcement said to wait here, right?
The company said to work from home tomorrow, right?
cz: Hajun told us to go first, right?
The guide told us to stand in line, right?

fk: 엄마가 왜 전화를 안 받냐며 화를 냈어요.
fe: Mom got angry, asking why I wasn't answering the phone.
xk: 다른 사람이 한 질문을 전하면서, 그 사람이 한 행동을 뒤에 말해요. '-냐고 하면서'를 줄인 말이에요. 진짜 궁금해서 묻기보다 따지거나 불평할 때가 많아요.
xe: You report someone's question and then say what that person did while asking. It is short for '-냐고 하면서.' It is often a complaint or a challenge, not a real question.
nk: '-냐고'는 질문만 전해요. '-냐며'는 질문하면서 한 행동(화냄, 웃음, 따짐)을 함께 말해요. 뒤에는 '화를 냈어요', '웃었어요' 같은 말이 자주 와요. '-냐면서'도 같은 뜻이에요.
ne: -냐고 only reports the question. -냐며 also says what the person did while asking (got angry, laughed, complained). The next words are often 화를 냈어요 or 웃었어요. -냐면서 means the same.
ex: My friend laughed, asking why I was late for the appointment.
누가 내 케이크를 먹었냐며 동생이 화를 냈어요.
My younger sibling got angry, asking who ate my cake.
The child followed me, asking where I was going.
손님이 왜 아직도 주문이 안 오냐며 소리를 질렀어요.
The customer shouted, asking why the order still hadn't come.
동료가 일을 언제 끝내냐며 짜증을 냈어요.
My coworker got annoyed, asking when I'd finish the work.
cz: My younger sibling shouted, asking where I had hidden the book.
아저씨가 왜 여기에 차를 ___ 화를 냈어요. (세우다)
The man got angry, asking why I parked my car here.

fk: 친구가 이 가방이 왜 이렇게 비싸냐며 놀랐어요.
fe: My friend was surprised, asking why this bag is so expensive.
xk: 형용사와 '이다'에는 -(으)냐며를 써요. 형용사는 받침이 없으면 -냐며, 있으면 -으냐며예요. 명사는 N(이)냐며예요.
xe: Use -(으)냐며 with adjectives and 이다. For adjectives, use -냐며 after a vowel and -으냐며 after a consonant. For nouns, use N(이)냐며.
nk: 상황이 이해가 안 될 때 따지듯이 말해요. 놀람이나 불만이 섞여 있어요. 말한 사람의 기분이 뒤 문장에 나와요.
ne: You say it when a situation doesn't make sense to you, in a questioning tone. Surprise or dissatisfaction is mixed in. The speaker's reaction comes in the next clause.
ex: 민수가 방이 왜 이렇게 좁으냐며 웃었어요.
Minsu laughed, asking why the room is so small.
엄마가 내 방이 왜 이렇게 지저분하냐며 화를 냈어요.
Mom got angry, asking why my room is so messy.
손님이 이게 정말 우리 가게 빵이냐며 따졌어요.
A customer demanded to know whether this is really our shop's bread.
My coworker was surprised, asking if this is really the office.
친구가 호텔 방이 왜 이렇게 작으냐며 실망했어요.
My friend was disappointed, asking why the hotel room is so small.
cz: 친구가 오늘 숙제가 왜 이렇게 ___ 화를 냈어요. (많다)
My friend got angry, asking why there is so much homework today.
동생이 이게 정말 우리 ___ 화를 냈어요. (집)
My younger sibling got angry, asking whether this is really our house.

fe: I sincerely hope you all stay healthy.
xk: 고마움, 사랑, 바람 같은 마음을 말하는 동사 뒤에 붙여요. 그 마음이 끝없이 크다는 뜻이에요. '마지아니하다'는 같은 말의 긴 형태예요.
xe: Attach it to verbs of feeling or hope (thank, love, hope). It means the feeling never stops. '마지아니하다' is the longer form.
nk: 편지, 인사말, 연설 같은 격식 있는 말에 써요. 친구와 하는 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 감사하다·사랑하다·기대하다 같은 마음 동사에만 쓰고, 먹다·가다 같은 행동 동사에는 못 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 따름이다'는 '그것뿐이다'라는 느낌이고, 이 문형은 '마음이 끝없다'는 느낌이에요.
ne: Use it in formal speeches, letters, and greetings, not in everyday talk with friends. It only works with feeling verbs like 감사하다, 사랑하다, 기대하다, never with action verbs like 먹다 or 가다. '-(으)ㄹ 따름이다' means 'that is all'; this pattern means 'my feeling never ends'.
ex: I am deeply and endlessly grateful for your help.
I love my family with all my heart.
이번 대회에서 좋은 결과가 있기를 기대해 마지않습니다.
I sincerely look forward to good results at this contest.
두 분의 결혼을 진심으로 축하해 마지않습니다.
I warmly congratulate you two on your wedding.
늘 응원해 주신 팬 여러분께 감사해 마지않습니다.
I am endlessly grateful to all the fans who always cheered for us.
cz: I always miss my family back home deeply.

fe: I'm asking you where you are going now.
xk: 내가 이미 한 질문을 다시 말할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-(느)냐니까'를 붙여요. '-느냐니까'는 '-냐니까'로 줄여 말해요.
xe: Use it to repeat a question you already asked. Add -(느)냐니까 to a verb stem. -느냐니까 is often shortened to -냐니까.
nk: 상대가 대답을 안 해서 답답하거나 조금 화날 때 써요. '-는'을 붙인 '-냐니까는'은 더 강하게 재촉하는 느낌이에요. 처음 묻는 말에는 쓰지 않아요. 처음에는 '-아/어요?'로 물어요.
ne: You use it when the other person did not answer and you feel impatient or a bit annoyed. -냐니까는 sounds even more insistent. Do not use it for a first-time question; ask normally first.
ex: 밥 먹었냐니까요? 왜 대답을 안 해요?
I'm asking if you ate. Why don't you answer?
내일 시험 보냐니까 왜 말을 안 해?
I'm asking if you have a test tomorrow. Why don't you say anything?
지민 씨한테 모임에 오냐니까는 대답이 없어요.
I'm asking Jimin if Jimin is coming to the meeting, but I get no answer.
이 책 읽었냐니까 계속 딴말만 해요.
I asked if you read this book, but you keep talking about other things.
주말에 뭐 하냐니까요. 왜 대답을 안 해요?
I'm asking what you are doing this weekend. Why don't you answer?
cz: I just said it. I'm asking if you are sleeping now.
I'm asking whether you already drank the coffee.

fe: I'm asking if this bag is expensive.
xk: 형용사에는 '-(으)냐니까', 명사에는 '-(이)냐니까'를 붙여요. 받침이 있으면 '-으냐니까', 없으면 '-냐니까'예요.
xe: Use -(으)냐니까 with adjectives and -(이)냐니까 with nouns. After a final consonant use -으냐니까 or -이냐니까; otherwise -냐니까.
nk: 동사 카드와 같아요. 이미 물은 질문에 대답을 못 들었을 때 다시 묻는 말이에요. 뜻은 '내가 ~냐고 묻잖아'예요. 말투가 세서 어른께는 조심해서 써야 해요.
ne: Same as the verb card: you already asked and got no answer. It means 'I'm asking you whether it is ...'. The tone is strong, so be careful with elders.
ex: 오늘 날씨가 추우냐니까요. 왜 대답을 안 해요?
I'm asking if it is cold today. Why don't you answer?
I'm asking who this person is.
저 사람이 네 친구냐니까 왜 웃기만 해?
I'm asking if that person is your friend. Why do you only laugh?
I'm asking if the room is big. Tell me quickly.
cz: I'm asking if this book is difficult.
I'm asking if that person is a teacher.

fe: I heard that Minsu is coming tomorrow.
xk: 다른 사람에게 들은 말을 전할 때 써요. '-다고 하더라고요'를 줄인 말이에요. 동사는 '-ㄴ다/는다더라고요', 형용사는 '-다더라고요', 명사는 '-(이)라더라고요'예요.
xe: Use it to pass on what someone told you. It is a short form of '-다고 하더라고요'. Verbs take -ㄴ다/는다더라고요, adjectives -다더라고요, nouns -(이)라더라고요.
nk: 내가 직접 들은 말을 지금 새로 알려 주는 느낌이에요. 친구와는 '-다더라고', 어른께는 '-다더라고요'를 써요. 내가 직접 본 일에는 '-더라고요'만 써요. '-다고 해요'는 단순한 전달이고, 이 문형은 들은 때의 기억이 들어 있어요.
ne: It feels like you are sharing, with fresh memory, something you personally heard. Use -다더라고 with friends and -다더라고요 with elders. For things you saw yourself, use plain -더라고요. '-다고 해요' is a neutral report; this one carries the memory of hearing it.
ex: I heard Seoyeon say this restaurant is tasty.
I heard Hajun read a book at home yesterday.
I heard that shop is closing down.
I heard it gets cold from tomorrow.
I heard that person is the new teacher.
cz: I heard Jimin is very busy these days.
I heard Yuna is going to Korea next week.

fe: The teacher said to come early tomorrow, I heard.
xk: 누가 명령한 말을 전할 때 동사 어간에 '-(으)라더라고요'를 붙여요. 같이 하자는 말은 '-자더라고요'예요.
xe: To report someone's command, add -(으)라더라고요 to a verb stem. For a suggestion ('let's'), use -자더라고요.
nk: '-(으)라고 하더라고요'를 줄인 말이에요. 내가 들은 일을 상대에게 알려 줄 때 써요. 친구와는 '-라더라고'로 끝내요.
ne: It is a short form of '-(으)라고 하더라고요'. You use it to tell someone about an order you heard. With friends, end with -라더라고.
ex: Mom said to close the door, I heard.
The doctor said to take the medicine.
The boss said to call before the meeting.
My friend said let's go together.
cz: Dad said to go to bed early.
The teacher said to sit here.

fe: I'm telling you, I don't know about that.
xk: 내가 이미 한 말을 다시 강하게 말할 때 써요. 동사는 '-ㄴ다/는다거든요', 형용사는 '-다거든요', 명사는 '-(이)라거든요'예요.
xe: Use it to repeat something you already said, more firmly. Verbs take -ㄴ다/는다거든요, adjectives -다거든요, nouns -(이)라거든요.
nk: 상대가 내 말을 안 믿거나 못 들었을 때 써요. '내가 ~라고 했잖아요'라는 느낌이에요. 강한 말투라서 처음 하는 말에는 안 써요. '-거든요'는 이유를 말할 때 쓰지만, '-다거든요'는 내가 한 말을 다시 말해요.
ne: You use it when the listener did not believe or hear you. It feels like 'I told you that...'. It is strong, so do not use it for a first statement. -거든요 gives a reason; -다거든요 restates your own words.
ex: 민수는 오늘 안 간다거든요. 그만 물어보세요.
I'm telling you, Minsu isn't going today. Please stop asking.
I'm telling you, this bag is mine.
그 식당은 정말 맛있다거든요. 제 말을 믿어 보세요.
I'm telling you, that restaurant is really good. Trust me.
I'm telling you, I went to bed early yesterday.
I'm telling you, that shop is closed on Sundays.
cz: I'm telling you, I don't drink coffee.
I'm telling you, this person is my younger sibling.

fe: The teacher said to sit here, you see.
xk: 다른 사람이 한 명령을 이유나 사정으로 전할 때 써요. 동사 어간에 '-(으)라거든요'를 붙여요.
xe: Use it to give someone else's command as the reason or background for what you are doing. Add -(으)라거든요 to a verb stem.
nk: 왜 그러냐고 물을 때 '나는 시킨 대로 하는 거예요'라고 설명하는 느낌이에요. 내가 한 명령을 다시 강하게 말할 때는 이 문형이 아니라 '-(으)라니까요'를 써요.
ne: It feels like explaining 'I'm only doing what I was told.' To firmly repeat a command you gave yourself, use -(으)라니까요 instead of this pattern.
ex: Mom said to close the door, you see.
The teacher said to do the homework first.
의사 선생님이 약을 하루에 세 번 먹으라거든요.
The doctor said to take the medicine three times a day.
Dad said to go to bed early.
cz: The teacher said to open the textbook.
엄마가 밥 먹기 전에 손을 ___ (씻다, 남의 명령 전달).
Mom said to wash your hands before eating.

fe: I'm telling you, I work out every day.
xk: 상대가 안 믿거나 못 들었을 때 같은 말을 힘주어 다시 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ다니까요, 있으면 -는다니까요를 써요.
xe: Use it to repeat your own statement firmly when the listener doesn't believe it or didn't listen. After a vowel use -ㄴ다니까요; after a final consonant use -는다니까요.
nk: '내가 말했잖아요, 정말이에요'라는 느낌이에요. 조금 답답하거나 화난 느낌이 들 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 조심해서 써요. 이유를 말하는 -거든요보다 더 강하게 주장해요.
ne: It feels like 'I said so, it's true!' It can sound a bit impatient or annoyed, so be careful with older people. It pushes your point harder than -거든요, which just gives a reason.
ex: I'm telling you, I get up early every morning.
이 가게는 빵이 금방 다 팔린다니까요.
I'm telling you, the bread here sells out fast.
I'm telling you, Hajun walks to school every day.
제 동생은 밥을 하루에 네 번 먹는다니까요.
I'm telling you, my younger sibling eats four times a day.
I'm telling you, Seoyeon leaves the office the latest.
여행 가면 안나는 사진을 정말 많이 찍는다니까요.
I'm telling you, Anna takes so many photos when we travel.
cz: It's true! I'm telling you, Minsu reads a book every day.
It's true! I'm telling you, Jiu runs for an hour every day.

fe: I'm telling you, the kimchi stew here is really good.
xk: 형용사나 있다/없다 뒤에 -다니까요를 붙여요. 받침과 상관없이 그대로 붙여요.
xe: Attach -다니까요 directly to adjectives and 있다/없다, whether or not there is a final consonant.
nk: 상대가 '정말요?' 하고 의심할 때 '진짜예요' 하고 강하게 말해요. 가까운 사이에서 자연스러워요. 윗사람에게는 목소리가 세게 들릴 수 있어요.
ne: Use it when the other person doubts you, like saying 'really, I mean it.' It's natural between close people. To someone older it can sound too strong.
ex: I'm telling you, this bag is really light.
I'm telling you, that person is very kind.
I'm telling you, the room is too small.
I'm telling you, there's nobody at the office today.
I'm telling you, Jeju Island is warm even in winter.
I'm telling you, I'm really fine.
cz: It's true! I'm telling you, this box is heavy.
It's true! I'm telling you, the prices at that shop are cheap.

fe: I'm telling you, this person is my younger sibling.
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙여서 '이거예요, 정말이에요' 하고 힘주어 말해요. 받침이 있으면 -이라니까요, 없으면 -라니까요를 써요.
xe: Attach it to a noun to insist 'it really is this.' Use -이라니까요 after a final consonant and -라니까요 after a vowel.
nk: 상대가 잘못 알고 있을 때 바로잡는 말로 많이 써요. 같은 말을 이미 한 번 했다는 느낌이 있어요. 처음 말할 때는 N이에요/예요를 써요.
ne: It's often used to correct someone who has it wrong. It implies you've already said it once. The first time, just say N이에요/예요.
ex: I'm telling you, this is salt.
I'm telling you, that building is our school.
I'm telling you, today is my birthday.
I'm telling you, that person is the president of our company.
I'm telling you, this umbrella is mine.
I'm telling you, this is my seat.
cz: It's true. I'm telling you, that person is my older sister.
It's true. I'm telling you, that person is our teacher.

fe: I'm telling you, I clearly said it yesterday.
xk: 지난 일을 힘주어 다시 말할 때 -았/었다니까요를 써요. 과거 -았/었- 뒤에 -다니까요를 붙여요.
xe: Use -았/었다니까요 to insist on something that already happened. Add -다니까요 after the past -았/었-.
nk: 상대가 '안 했잖아요' 하고 말할 때 '아니에요, 했어요' 하고 맞서는 말이에요. 조금 답답한 느낌이 있어서 가까운 사이에서 주로 써요.
ne: It's used when someone says 'you didn't tell me' or 'that didn't happen.' It sounds defensive or impatient, so it's mostly for close people.
ex: I'm telling you, I put my wallet here.
I'm telling you, it rained a lot yesterday.
I'm telling you, I already saw that movie.
I'm telling you, I definitely locked the door this morning.
I'm telling you, that restaurant closed yesterday.
I'm telling you, Hajun already went home.
cz: 아니에요, 저는 어제 편지를 세 장 ___ (쓰다).
No, I'm telling you, I wrote three letters yesterday.
No, I'm telling you, Mike already ate lunch.

fe: What time did Seoyeon say she's coming?
xk: 다른 사람이 한 말을 듣고 온 사람에게 '그 사람이 ~라고 했어요?' 하고 물어요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ답디까, 있으면 -는답디까를 써요.
xe: Ask someone who heard another person's words, 'Did that person say ...?' Use -ㄴ답디까 after a vowel and -는답디까 after a final consonant.
nk: 합쇼체 질문이라 조금 옛날 말투예요. 어른들 말이나 드라마에서 들을 수 있어요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 -다고 했어요?를 더 많이 써요.
ne: It's a formal-style question and sounds a bit old-fashioned. You may hear it from older people or in dramas. In everyday talk today, -다고 했어요? is more common.
ex: When did Hajun say he's leaving?
의사 선생님이 약을 하루에 몇 번 먹는답디까?
How many times a day did the doctor say to take the medicine?
When did the shop owner say he closes?
What did your friend say he's doing this weekend?
What time did the boss say the meeting starts?
What time did the hotel say they serve breakfast?
cz: What did Mike say he's buying tomorrow?
Until when did the teacher say he accepts the homework?

fe: Did they say the food at that restaurant is good?
xk: 형용사나 있다/없다 뒤에 -답디까를 붙여요. 다른 사람이 '~하다'고 한 말이 맞는지 물어요.
xe: Attach -답디까 to adjectives and 있다/없다. You ask whether someone said that something is a certain way.
nk: 직접 확인하지 못한 일을 전해 들은 사람에게 물을 때 써요. 말투가 옛날식이에요. 보통 어른이 아랫사람에게 물을 때 어울려요.
ne: Use it to ask someone who heard about something you couldn't check yourself. The tone is old-style. It fits best when an older person asks a younger one.
ex: Did they say the weather in Jeju is cold these days?
Did they say that room is big?
Did they say the test is hard?
Did they say they have no time this weekend?
Did they say the prices at that shop are high?
Did they say the new house is far?
cz: Did Hajun say that movie is fun?
Did Seoyeon say she's sick today?

fe: Who did they say that person was?
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙여서 '그것이 ~라고 했어요?' 하고 물어요. 받침이 있으면 -이랍디까, 없으면 -랍디까를 써요.
xe: Attach it to a noun to ask 'Did they say it is ...?' Use -이랍디까 after a final consonant and -랍디까 after a vowel.
nk: 이름·값·시간처럼 전해 들은 정보를 다시 물을 때 많이 써요. 어원은 -(이)라고 합디까예요. 요즘은 -(이)래요?나 -(이)라고 했어요?를 더 써요.
ne: It's often used to ask again about heard information like names, prices, or times. It comes from -(이)라고 합디까. Today people more often say -(이)라고 했어요?
ex: Which country did they say the new teacher is from?
What kind of medicine did they say it is?
How much did they say this book is?
What time did they say the meeting is?
Did they say the new student's name is Jiu?
Did they say the test date is next Monday?
cz: Where did they say we're meeting tomorrow?
Did they say that person's job is doctor?

fe: What did the doctor say?
xk: '뭐라고 합디까?'를 줄인 말이에요. 다른 사람이 한 말이 무엇인지 물을 때 써요.
xe: A short form of '뭐라고 합디까?' You use it to ask what another person said.
nk: 그 사람의 말이 궁금하거나 결과가 걱정될 때 물어요. 옛날식 말투라서 가까운 친구보다 어른이 쓰는 느낌이에요. 요즘은 뭐래요?를 더 많이 써요.
ne: You ask it when you're curious about what someone said or worried about the result. It sounds old-fashioned, more like something an older person says. These days 뭐래요? is more common.
ex: What did the boss say in the meeting?
What did Dad say on the phone?
What did the hotel staff say?
What did the teacher say at school?
cz: What did the photo shop owner say?
What did Mom say on the phone?

fk: 지민이 오늘 온댔는데 아직 안 와요.
fe: Jimin said she'd come today, but she's not here yet.
xk: '-ㄴ다고 했는데'를 줄인 말이에요. 남에게 들은 말을 먼저 하고, 뒤에 다른 상황을 이어요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ댔는데, 있으면 -는댔는데를 써요. ㄹ받침 동사는 ㄹ이 빠지고 -ㄴ댔는데를 붙여요(만들다 → 만든댔는데).
xe: A short form of '-ㄴ다고 했는데.' You state what someone said first, then add a different situation. Use -ㄴ댔는데 after a vowel and -는댔는데 after a final consonant. Verbs ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ and take -ㄴ댔는데 (만들다 → 만든댔는데).
nk: 들은 말과 실제가 다를 때 많이 써요. 말할 때 쓰는 편한 말이라 글에서는 잘 안 써요. 문장 끝에 -요를 붙여 -댔는데요로도 말해요.
ne: It's often used when what you heard differs from reality. It's casual spoken style and rarely used in writing. You can add -요 at the end: -댔는데요.
ex: 서연이 지금 간댔는데 왜 아직 여기 있어요?
Seoyeon said she was leaving now, so why is she still here?
엄마가 저녁에 비빔밥을 만든댔는데 냄새가 안 나요.
Mom said she'd make bibimbap for dinner, but I don't smell anything.
가게 주인이 오늘 문을 연댔는데 닫혀 있어요.
The shop owner said he'd open today, but it's closed.
하준이 주말에 같이 운동한댔는데 연락이 없어요.
Hajun said he'd work out with me this weekend, but I haven't heard from him.
선생님이 숙제를 안 낸댔는데 숙제가 많아요.
The teacher said he wouldn't give homework, but there's a lot.
사라가 한국에서 일한댔는데 왜 미국에 있어요?
Sarah said she works in Korea, so why is she in the US?
cz: Mike said he'd buy bread, but he didn't bring any.
준이 매일 책을 ___ 지금은 게임만 해요. (읽다)
Jun said he'd read a book every day, but now he only plays games.

fe: They said this restaurant is good, but it's not great.
xk: '-다고 했는데'를 줄인 말이에요. 형용사와 있다/없다 뒤에 -댔는데를 붙여요.
xe: A short form of '-다고 했는데.' Attach -댔는데 to adjectives and 있다/없다.
nk: 기대와 다른 걸 알았을 때 '들은 것과 달라요' 하고 말해요. 가볍게 불평하는 느낌이 있어요. 말로 하는 편한 표현이에요.
ne: You say it when reality turns out different from what you expected, like 'it wasn't what I was told.' It carries a light complaint. It's casual spoken style.
ex: They said the weather is warm today, but it's too cold.
They said that movie is fun, but it's not fun at all.
They said this bag is cheap, but the price is high.
They said the hotel room is big, but it's very small.
그 시험이 쉽댔는데 저는 많이 틀렸어요.
They said that test is easy, but I got a lot wrong.
They said there are no people here, but there are a lot.
cz: Minsu said the new bag is light, but it's too heavy.
Dohyun said that mountain is low, but it's hard for me.

fe: They said that person is a teacher, but he's a student.
xk: 'N(이)라고 했는데'를 줄인 말이에요. 받침이 있으면 -이랬는데, 없으면 -랬는데를 써요.
xe: A short form of 'N(이)라고 했는데.' Use -이랬는데 after a final consonant and -랬는데 after a vowel.
nk: 들은 정보가 틀렸을 때 많이 써요. 사람·장소·날짜·값처럼 이름이나 숫자를 말할 때 자주 나와요. 말로 하는 편한 표현이에요.
ne: It's often used when information you heard turns out wrong. It often comes up with names, places, dates, and prices. It's casual spoken style.
ex: They said today is a holiday, but the shop is open.
They said this road is a shortcut, but it's too far.
They said that shop is a bakery, but it's a flower shop.
They said the meeting is at two, but it's at three.
이 책이 만 원이랬는데 이만 원이에요.
They said this book is 10,000 won, but it's 20,000 won.
They said she's a doctor, but she's a nurse.
cz: Hajun said that person is a singer, but actually he's a student.
Mike said this is a restaurant, but it's a library.

fk: 엄마가 일찍 자랬는데 아직 게임을 해요.
fe: Mom told me to go to bed early, but I'm still playing games.
xk: '-(으)라고 했는데'를 줄인 말이에요. 남이 하라고 한 말을 하고 뒤에 다른 상황을 이어요. 받침이 있으면 -으랬는데, 없으면 -랬는데를 써요.
xe: A short form of '-(으)라고 했는데.' You say what someone told you to do, then add a different situation. Use -으랬는데 after a final consonant and -랬는데 after a vowel.
nk: 들은 지시를 지키지 않았거나 지시와 다를 때 써요. 말하는 사람의 후회나 불평이 들어 있어요. 말로 하는 편한 표현이에요.
ne: Use it when you didn't follow an instruction or when things differ from what you were told. It often carries regret or complaint. It's casual spoken style.
ex: The teacher told me to hand in the homework by tomorrow, but I forgot.
의사 선생님이 약을 먹으랬는데 안 먹었어요.
The doctor told me to take the medicine, but I didn't.
My friend told me to wait here, but where did he go?
The boss told me to come early today, but I was late.
Dad told me to close the window, but it's open.
선생님이 단어를 매일 쓰랬는데 안 썼어요.
The teacher told us to write the words every day, but I didn't.
cz: Mom told me to wash my hands, but I didn't.
Jimin told me to buy milk, but I bought coffee.

fk: 하준이 매일 운동한다지만 저는 안 믿어요.
fe: Even though Hajun says he works out every day, I don't believe it.
xk: '-ㄴ다고 하지만'을 줄인 말이에요. 남이 한 말을 일단 받아들이고, 뒤에 반대되는 말을 해요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ다지만, 있으면 -는다지만을 써요.
xe: A short form of '-ㄴ다고 하지만.' You accept what someone said for now, then say something opposite. Use -ㄴ다지만 after a vowel and -는다지만 after a final consonant.
nk: 말하는 사람이 그 말을 다 믿지는 않아요. 의심하거나 다른 생각이 있다는 뜻이에요. 그냥 -지만은 말한 사람이 따로 없어서 이런 거리감이 없어요.
ne: The speaker doesn't fully buy what was said. It signals doubt or a different view. Plain -지만 has no such distance, since no one else is quoted.
ex: 친구가 이 약을 먹는다지만 저는 안 먹을 거예요.
